# M4 Administration Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Give the kit its administration: organisations (wizard with first-admin invitation, edit with a super-admin-only slug rename, archive / restore / purge, "Open" through the handoff), users (index, edit-as-show page, status, delete and restore), invitations (invite with locale, remind, cancel, accept, copy link, pending list), custom team roles with protected system roles, the optional in-house impersonation module, and an audit log with a viewer. Every page is host-aware, every user-management write is limited to targets whose permissions the actor holds, and Appendix A W1–W6 and W8–W14 are closed with regression tests.

**Architecture:** Domain work lives in single-purpose actions (`App\Actions\{Audit,Users,Invitations,Organisations,Roles}`) that authorise themselves with `Gate::forUser($actor)`, run in transactions, guard lock-outs by locking the whole candidate set in id order (`lockForUpdate()->pluck()`) and log through one `App\Actions\Audit\RecordActivity`. Livewire MFC pages under `resources/views/pages/**` keep only `#[Locked]` ids, re-resolve and re-authorise on every action and call those actions. Any-host pages read tenant models through `App\Tenancy\HostScope::read()` (scoped on a tenant host; `Tenant::bypass()` for super admins on central hosts) and filter central models (organisations, roles, pivots) explicitly with `HostScope::organisationId()`; actions that work for a given organisation lock and re-check it with `HostScope::lockForWrite()` and run inside `Tenant::run()`. Non-super actors act on a user only when the target's effective permissions are a subset of their own (`App\Authorization\EffectivePermissions`, `App\Authorization\UserAbilities`). spatie/laravel-activitylog v5 writes to a tenant-model `App\Models\Activity` (plain-string `event`, indexed `organisation_id` without FK, IP, user agent, soft deletes) through a custom log action that tags authentication, security and impersonation events by host and administrative events by subject, and rewrites the causer during impersonation; user field changes are recorded by an observer, not by the vendor `LogsActivity` trait. Impersonation is an in-house, session-level identity swap on the stock session guard, owned by `App\Tenancy\Auth\Impersonation`, gated by `UserPolicy::impersonate` and `config('skv.modules.impersonation')`, and re-validated on every request by `EnforceImpersonation`, which ends it (logged) as soon as the pair no longer qualifies. Invitations are a tenant model whose token is stored as a sha256 hash (lookup) plus an encrypted copy (mails, "Copy invite link"; cleared on accept); invitation mails are queued after commit and build their signed relative accept URL in the worker. Users carry a `locale` (`App\Enums\Locale`) that invitation mails and the accept page use.

**Tech Stack:** PHP 8.4, Laravel 13.35, Livewire 4.4.7 (MFC), Flux 2.20.1 (free components only), Fortify 1.41, laravel/passkeys 0.2.1, spatie/laravel-permission 8.3 (teams), **spatie/laravel-activitylog 5.1.1 (new)**, Pest 5.3, Larastan 3 level 8, PostgreSQL 18 (Herd), SQLite.

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-10-skv3-design.md` — read §3 (version baseline), §4.3–§4.8, §6.2 (route × host matrix, strict mode, queue context), §6.3, §6.4, §6.7 (free variants), §6.8 (impersonation flag), §7.2, §11.2 (M4 row) and Appendix A W1–W14 before starting. Decisions: `docs/decisions.md` DEC-20 (Pro-only components), DEC-21 (template role), DEC-26 (M2 rulings) and DEC-27 (M3 rulings, M4 deferrals). This plan's rulings, including the owner rulings OD-1 = C (in-house impersonation; the spec §3 `lab404/laravel-impersonate` row is struck), OD-2 = A (`Locale` enum and `users.locale` in M4) and OD-3 = B (only super admins change a slug), are recorded as DEC-28 in Task 25.

---

## Global Constraints

- PHP floor `^8.4`; `laravel/framework ^13.35`; Pest `^5.3`; Larastan level **8**, **no baseline**, no new `ignoreErrors` entries (MFC component `.php` files under `resources/views/pages/**` are analysed too: typed props, `@var` shapes, paginator generics).
- Pint: `laravel` preset + `declare_strict_types`, `strict_comparison`, `ordered_class_elements`. Every PHP file starts with `declare(strict_types=1);` (the `make:livewire` stub has none — add it). Run `composer fix` after editing PHP.
- **Dependencies:** M4 adds exactly one package, `spatie/laravel-activitylog` (`^5.1.1`, resolves to 5.1.1), in Task 1, and no other Composer or npm dependency. Impersonation is built in-house (OD-1 = C): `lab404/laravel-impersonate` is **not** added. Also not added: `pestphp/pest-plugin-livewire` (tests keep `Livewire::test()`) and `pestphp/pest-plugin-browser` (M5, DEC-25). The owner's approval of this plan is the approval AGENTS.md asks for; the Task 1 commit message names the package.
- Livewire components are multi-file (MFC), created with `php artisan make:livewire pages::<area>.<name> --no-interaction`, no ⚡ in any path, never `$this->view()`; data reaches Blade through public props, `#[Computed]` (per-request only, never `persist`/`cache`) or `with()`.
- **Execution:** tasks run strictly in sequence on one branch; no parallel subagents. `lang/{nl,en}.json`, `resources/views/layouts/app/sidebar.blade.php`, `tests/Feature/Tenancy/RouteHostMatrixTest.php`, `tests/Pest.php` and `resources/views/pages/users/index/*` are touched by many tasks (OR-M12).
- **Gate per task:** `composer check` green on SQLite **and** `composer test:pgsql` green on PostgreSQL; from Task 19 on (when the CI off path exists) also `php artisan config:clear && MODULE_IMPERSONATION=false vendor/bin/pest --parallel` (OR-I1).
- Never driver-specific SQL (`ilike`, raw `like`, `ALTER TABLE … CONSTRAINT`, `FOR UPDATE` with aggregates); search with `whereLike(..., caseSensitive: false)`; lock-and-decide with `orderBy('id')->lockForUpdate()->pluck()` over the whole candidate set (RL-27). Never `env()` outside `config/`.
- No hard-coded kit or site name (`skv`) in app-identity values; `config/skv.php` and `config('skv.…')` keys are allowed (NameLeakTest).
- `livewire/flux-pro` and `composer.fluxui.dev` never appear in `composer.json` / `composer.lock`. Views use only free Flux 2.20.1 components and variants (DEC-20): role assignment = `flux:checkbox.group`; active/archived = `flux:radio.group variant="segmented"` bound to `#[Url] $view`; date range = two `flux:input type="date"`; `flux:select` default (native) variant only; detail flyout = free `flux:modal flyout`. No `flux:tabs`, `date-picker`, `listbox`/`combobox` selects.
- No permission string literals in `app`, `routes`, `resources/views` (routes `->can(Permission::X)`, Blade `@can(\App\Authorization\Permission::X)`, PHP `$user->can(Permission::X)`); `setPermissionsTeamId()` only in `PermissionsTeam`; team switches through `withPermissionsTeam()` / `PermissionsTeam::run()` with `unsetRelation('roles')` around them. Never compute permissions through Spatie relations on a collection (`getAllPermissions()` lazy-loads): use `EffectivePermissions` (RK-I6).
- Tenancy: `Tenant::bypass()` / scope removal only in the allowed namespaces; **admin pages never join the bypass allow-list** — they read tenant models through `HostScope::read()` (Task 7, RL-8). `HostScope` scopes **tenant models only**: every central-model read on an any-host page (organisations, Spatie roles/permissions, `model_has_*`, `sessions`) filters by `HostScope::organisationId()`, and client-sent organisation ids (`#[Url] $organisation`, form pickers) are ignored on tenant hosts (RK-I4). Actions that take an `Organisation` call `HostScope::lockForWrite()` before `Tenant::run()` (refuses archived and cross-tenant organisations, RK-I11). New tenant models (`Activity`, `Invitation`) use `BelongsToOrganisation` + `SoftDeletes`, keep `organisation_id` out of mass assignment and are listed in `config('tenancy.tenant_models')`.
- Authorisation: every action authorises itself (`Gate::forUser($actor)->authorize(...)`) and is the source of truth; components additionally `$this->authorize()` in `mount()` and before calling an action. A policy method named like an `ALWAYS_CHECKED` ability (`impersonate`, `delete`, `forceDelete`, `updateStatus`, `updateRoles`, `updateSuperAdmin`) grants super admins explicitly; new non-destructive abilities use other names (`remind`, `cancel`, `viewLink`, `restore`) so `Gate::before` covers super admins (FU2-3). For non-super actors, `update`, `updateStatus`, `delete`, `restore`, `impersonate` and `viewLink` also require the permission-subset rule (RL-26).
- Audit: entries are written only through `App\Actions\Audit\RecordActivity`; the vendor `LogsActivity` trait is used nowhere (arch rules, Task 1). Never log a password, a token, an accept URL or the Fortify `Failed` credentials beyond a valid email address (R-4, CV-17, RK-M11).
- Mails and notifications: `App\Mail\*` implement `ShouldQueue`, call `afterCommit()`, and build links with `tenant_url()` when they render (worker context); new notifications follow M3's `EmailChangeRequested`.
- Strict Eloquent is on in tests: eager-load every relation an index renders; never lazy-load inside a list; never eager-load a `morphTo` to `User` through `TenantScope` (use `App\Tenancy\UserNames`, Task 13).
- Code, comments, docs: English. UI copy: `nl` default with `en`; every new `__()` key goes into **both** `lang/nl.json` and `lang/en.json` (identical keys, PHP `sort()` order; Dutch informal "je"; keep skv3's "Inloggen als …" wording for impersonation). `LangCoverageTest` (Task 1) fails when a key used in the M4 paths is missing from `nl.json` (OR-I8). Enum labels (`ActivityEvent`, `Locale`) are `nl.json` keys with a test like `PermissionCatalogueTest`. `#[Title]` values stay English literals (M5 translates them).
- Tests are Pest functions (`it(...)`), typed closures; each file starts with a `/** covers §x.y */` docblock as its first statement; Appendix A regression tests carry the finding id in their name. **"Fails on main"** marks only a test whose behaviour can be shown failing against `main` (existing code); a test of a class that does not exist yet is ordinary TDD and carries no such label (RK-M10). A test expecting a database error wraps the statement in `DB::transaction(...)`; `Event::fake()` is never called bare (`Event::fake([X::class])` or `->except([TenantResolved::class, TenantForgotten::class])`). After-commit mail is tested on the real sync queue with the `array` mailer, never with `Mail::fake()` (which ignores `afterCommit`, RK-I8). Session-swap tests sign in through `route('login.store')` and call `Auth::guard('web')->forgetUser()` before each follow-up request (RK-I9). Tests that change the admin subdomain use `config()`, not the environment (OR-M11).
- `Livewire::test()` skips all middleware: host rules, `can:` route gates, membership and impersonation session behaviour are tested over HTTP, and host-bound component actions with a forged `/livewire/update` from the wrong host (HostScopingTest pattern, `callPageAction()`).
- **Global test helper names already taken (37, never redeclare):** `onTenant`, `onApex`, `onAdminHost`, `asSuperAdmin`, `asOrgAdmin`, `asMember`, `kitSourceFiles`, `filesMatching`, `confirmationLinkFor`, `viewFiles`, `memberWithRecoveryCodes`, `memberOnSecurityPage`, `expirePasswordConfirmation`, `securityPageSnapshot`, `callOnSecurityPage`, `memberChangingEmail`, `useLoginHost`, `matrixRoutes`, `routeMatrixOutcome`, `twoTenantsWithMembers`, `admittedInBurst`, `burstRequest`, `trustedProxiesConfig`, `deletedAtOf`, `userPolicyCast`, `registerPasskeyFor`, `passkeyHost`, `signInWithPasskey`, `passkeyRelyingPartyIdWith`, `badgeRows`, `teamRole`, `systemRoleId`, `roleNamesOf`, `dutchTranslationKeys`, `lastQueuedPayload`, `workOneJob`, `systemRole`. `dutchTranslationKeys()` **moves** from `PermissionCatalogueTest.php` to `tests/Pest.php` in Task 1 (same name, so later files do not depend on another test file under `--parallel`, OR-I9).
- **Global test helper names reserved for M4 (each added once, in the task named, nowhere else):** `recordedActivity` (Task 1, `tests/Pest.php`), `pageSnapshot` and `callPageAction` (Task 7, `tests/Pest.php`), `matrixParameters` (Task 9, `tests/Feature/Tenancy/RouteHostMatrixTest.php`), `inviteMember` and `acceptLinkFor` (Task 11, `tests/Pest.php`), `useImpersonationModule` (Task 19, `tests/Pest.php`; extended with route rebuilding in Task 20), `startImpersonatingOverHttp` (Task 20, `tests/Pest.php`). No other new global helper; file-local helpers are closures or `beforeEach` (FU3-18).
- Every new named GET route goes into `matrixRoutes()` or the exclusions of `tests/Feature/Tenancy/RouteHostMatrixTest.php`; parameter pages stay in the matrix through `matrixParameters()` (RL-10). A task that introduces a new outcome also adds its `match` arm in the assertion and widens `routeMatrixOutcome()`'s `@return` (OR-M13).
- Migrations: **additive new files only**, `database/migrations/0001_01_01_000005_…` onward (M3's `0001_01_01_000004_create_handoff_tokens_table` is the precedent, OR-M9), hand-written, portable; existing migrations are not edited, so the owner's development database needs `php artisan migrate` only — Claude asks before running it and never runs `migrate:fresh` / `db:wipe`.
- Commits: Conventional Commits, lower case, imperative; end with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`.
- Never run `herd sites` or the Herd MCP `get_all_sites`; `tinker`, `migrate` and `db:seed` prompt for approval.

## Conventions used in this plan

- All M4 work happens on branch `m4-administration`, created from `main` in Task 1.
- Bracketed ids in task and test names are traceability tags: `ORG-*`, `USR-*`, `INV-*`, `ROLE-*`, `IMP-*`, `AUD-*`, `TEN-*`, `AUTHZ-*`, `HND-*`, `TST-*`, `DEC2x-*`, `FU2-*`, `FU3-*`, `C-*`, `D-*`, `R-*` come from the M4 requirement inventory, `W*` from spec Appendix A, `X*` from the skv2 lessons, `CV-*`, `OR-*`, `RK-*` from the plan reviews, `RL-*` and `OD-*` from "## Rulings" below. Each task spells out the requirement itself; the tag only lets a reviewer trace it.
- `routes/admin.php` (required from `routes/web.php` like `routes/settings.php`) has two parts: a `Route::middleware(['auth'])->group(...)` for the admin pages and, **outside** that group, the signed `invitations.accept` route (OR-B1). Single-host routes use `Route::tenant()` / `Route::central()`; module routes live in `routes/impersonation.php` (Task 20).
- Test hosts: apex `localhost`, admin `admin.localhost`, tenants `{slug}.localhost`, scheme `http`. Create every model a test needs **before** switching to a central host (strict mode). Call the host helper after the actor helper when they differ (`asSuperAdmin(); onTenant($org);`, `asOrgAdmin($org); onAdminHost();`).
- Facts verified for this plan (vendor reads of activitylog 5.1.1, Fortify, Livewire and the framework):
  - activitylog does not load its migration (hand-write it).
  - `ActivityLogger::setEvent()` assigns the raw event name to the model at once and `LogsActivity` passes vendor names (`updated`), so an enum cast on `event` would throw before any hook runs (RK-B1).
  - `CleanActivityLogAction::deleteOldActivities(string $cutOffDate, ?string $logName): int` calls `->delete()` (a soft delete on a SoftDeletes model).
  - `LogActivityAction::beforeActivityLogged(Model $activity): void` runs for manual and model-event logs (buffering stays off).
  - `CauserResolver` precedence makes `setCauser()` override explicit causers (never use it).
  - Fortify `Failed` carries the plain password (R-4) and the login field is `required|string`, not `email`; Fortify ships `TwoFactorAuthenticationFailed` and `RecoveryCodeReplaced`; `PasswordResetLinkSent` fires inside `defer()`.
  - Event discovery of `app/Listeners` is on; a union-typed `handle()` registers for each type.
  - `SessionGuard::hashPasswordForCookie()` is public in Laravel 13; `SessionGuard::logout()` cycles the **current guard user's** remember token, `logoutCurrentDevice()` does not.
  - `MailFake::queue()` ignores `afterCommit`; `SyncQueue` honours it.
  - `Illuminate\Routing\RouteCollection` has no remove API.
  - `Route::livewire()` stores only the component name, so a route can be registered before its page exists.
  - `BelongsToOrganisation`'s `creating` hook fills a null `organisation_id` from the bound tenant.
  - `UserPolicy::update` passes for your own account (`managesMember` excludes only super-admin targets).
  - Livewire re-applies `Authenticate`, `Authorize` (`can:`), `SubstituteBindings` and the two host middleware on updates, not `signed` and not `password.confirm`.
  - Public Eloquent props rehydrate through `newQueryWithoutScopes()` (no TenantScope, no SoftDeletes), so components hold `#[Locked]` ids.
  - Spatie's `roles` relation filters on the current team (null on central hosts) and `getAllPermissions()` lazy-loads `permissions`.
  - A Livewire method attribute hooks in with `call(array $parameters): void` (`SupportAttributes::call()`, like `BaseAuthorize`).
  - Middleware order: `Authenticate → AuthenticateSession → VerifyTenantMembership → EnsureTenantHost|EnsureCentralHost → SubstituteBindings → Authorize`.

## Scope

**In M4:** spec §4.3 (organisations UI, wizard, archive/restore/purge, slug rule, slug-rename redirect, "Open" via handoff), §4.4 (users index/edit/show, status, delete, restore, audit of fields, per-user locale column), §4.5 (invitations with locale, except bulk), §4.6 (roles index and CRUD with system-role protection, `RolePolicy`, remaining guards), §4.7 + §6.8 impersonation module (flag, policy matrix, per-request enforcement, banner, stop route, module-off behaviour and CI path), §4.8 (activity log, authentication subscriber, viewer, retention action; not the dashboard widget and CSV export), §6.2 rows for every M4 page (incl. `/` for super admins on central hosts, `#[RequiresTenant]`), §6.4 handoff callers and the FU3-2 decision, §7.2 datasets (impersonation matrix, module flag) and Appendix A W1–W6, W8–W14 regression tests (W7 is re-pinned for the wizard), plus E1 kept closed for the new admin email path. Plus the M4 items of DEC-26, DEC-27, FU2 and FU3 listed in the traceability table, and the minimal interim UI M4's pages need (permission-gated "Administration" sidebar group, flash→toast bridge, sticky impersonation banner).

**Deferred:**
- **M5:** the single navigation definition, its role × module render test and the Overzicht/Beheer/Systeem groups (§6.5; M4's interim group is replaced); `layouts/base` (the M4 toast bridge and banner move there); translated `#[Title]`s and Dutch copy for existing starter screens; error pages incl. a friendly "this invitation is no longer valid" hint on the 404 page (X12 wording, CV-11); the dashboard incl. the "last 10 entries" audit widget (AUD-4, C-7; M4 provides `UserNames` for it); per-user locale middleware, language switchers and the profile language field (M4 stores the locale and uses it for invitation mails and the accept page only); Pest browser plugin and the §7.2 browser tests for invitation acceptance and impersonation (TST-5, IMP-14, C-19); Flux Pro variants (§6.7) and the Pro lint test (DEC25-4); removing starter layouts/links (DEC25-1); "organisation_id never fillable" arch rule (FU2-7; M4 tests its own two models); tenant 404 for JSON/Livewire (FU2-8); passkeys module flag and `MODULE_PASSKEYS` in CI (§6.8, DEC-27); FU3-19 items.
- **M6:** doctor checks for the template role and badge drift; `SyncResult` reporting stripped badge permissions (FU2-13); `skv:create-organisation` reusing `CreateOrganisation`; demo seeder with invitations and activity.
- **M7 (ops + extras, incl. limits and hardening):** `require_second_factor` toggle, enforcement and its audit (ORG-2, §6.6); sessions list and its audit (AUD-7 part); bulk invitations (INV-18); audit CSV export (AUD-8 part); avatars incl. purge's avatar-file deletion (USR-18, ORG-11 part); scheduling `activitylog:clean --force` (AUD-10 part, §4.9); `EnsureSecondFactor`'s impersonation pass-through (IMP-15; M4 exposes `Impersonation::isActive()`); `model:prune` for handoff tokens (DEC-27); **hardening** (CV-6): rate limits on invite/remind and email-change requests (D-20, FU3-10), limiter input casting (FU3-11), clearing failure counters on success (FU3-12), request-derived origins for the password-reset and email-change mail links and other request-built links (FU3-14 residual), passkey bucket key and origin listener (FU3-15). Reason: M7 owns ops and limits (§4.9 scheduler/health) and the limiter family should land together; M4's invite/remind senders are authenticated, permission-gated and audited.
- **M8 (release gate, polish sweep):** FU2-11 rest (soft-delete exclusion and idempotency test-strength gaps), FU2-12 (debug-call arch rule, strict-default test), FU3-16 rest, FU3-20 (trustedproxy docblock). Reason: M8's release gate reviews test strength and docs as a whole.
- **Resolved, no work:** FU3-13 (stale: DEC-27 (2) already says the IP limit has no backstop; Task 25 removes it from the memory note, CV-18).
- **Not in v1:** a reservation or redirect of an organisation's old slug after a rename (OD-3 = B).

## Rulings

Recorded in DEC-28 (Task 25). RL-1…RL-25 are the revision-1 rulings, amended where a review changed them; RL-26…RL-30 came out of the reviews. The owner rulings OD-1…OD-3 follow the RL list; the critic decisions settled without the owner close the section.

- **RL-1 Dependencies.** Only spatie/laravel-activitylog is added; impersonation is in-house (OD-1 = C). No Livewire or browser Pest plugins.
- **RL-2 `config/skv.php`** is created once, in Task 11, with all three keys M4 reads: `invitations.expires_in_days` (env `INVITATION_EXPIRES_IN_DAYS`, default 7), `invitations.signature_grace_days` (30) and `modules.impersonation` (env `MODULE_IMPERSONATION`, default true) (OR-M3). Passkeys/backups flags and `second_factor.*` arrive with their features (M5/M7). (D-3, C-22)
- **RL-3 Migrations** are new, additive files numbered after M3's handoff migration: `0001_01_01_000005_create_activity_log_table` (Task 1), `0001_01_01_000006_add_locale_to_users_table` (Task 10), `0001_01_01_000007_create_invitations_table` (Task 11); hand-written instead of the vendor stub (explicit morph index names). (D-31, OR-M9)
- **RL-4 Activity schema.** `App\Models\Activity` extends the vendor model; it is a tenant model (`BelongsToOrganisation`, `SoftDeletes`, listed in `tenancy.tenant_models`, `mayExistWithoutOrganisation()` = true) with `organisation_id` guarded. `event` stays a **plain string column with no enum cast**; `Activity::kitEvent(): ?ActivityEvent` (`tryFrom`) serves labels and the viewer (RK-B1). Columns added to the vendor stub: `organisation_id` (unsigned big int, nullable, indexed, no FK), `ip_address` string(45), `user_agent` text, `deleted_at`; indexes on `event`, `created_at` and `(organisation_id, created_at)`. Every row: `event` = the `ActivityEvent` value, `description` = the same value, `log_name` = `ActivityEvent::group()`; reason, typed email, `impersonated_as`, host and counts go in `properties`; diffs in `attribute_changes`; buffering stays off. (D-26, C-13, C-24)
- **RL-5 Organisation tagging** has two modes (RK-I5). **Host mode** — events of the `authentication`, `security` and `impersonation` groups (incl. the consumed handoff): the bound tenant, else `null` (central); the subject's organisation is ignored, so a promoted super admin's sign-in on the admin host is central and on tenant B is B's. **Subject mode** — every other event: explicit organisation → the subject's organisation (`Organisation` subject = itself; any model with `organisation_id`) → the bound tenant → `null`. Role events always pass the organisation explicitly (a Spatie role carries `team_id`, not `organisation_id`). `null` means "derive"; an explicitly central entry while a tenant is bound is not needed by any M4 flow and is not supported (the `creating` hook would refill it). Central actions on an organisation's data show in that organisation's log (X7). (D-25)
- **RL-6 One writer.** All kit entries go through `RecordActivity`. The vendor `LogsActivity` trait is **not used** (RK-B1, CV-16): `App\Observers\UserActivityObserver` (`#[ObservedBy]` on `User`) records `user.updated` with old/new values when `name` or `email` changed, for every writer (admin edit, profile name, `ConfirmEmailChange`); writers that log their own event save quietly (`AcceptInvitation`). Status, super-admin, role, deletion and restore changes are explicit events (fillable fields alone would miss them, C-12); role CRUD is logged in the role actions, with no Spatie `Role` subclass; `permissions:sync` changes are not audited (deploy-time console; M6's doctor reports drift) (CV-h). (D-27)
- **RL-7 Visibility, retention and failed sign-ins.** Central viewers include soft-deleted (archived organisations') rows; tenant viewers see their own rows only; `organisation_id = null` rows show only centrally. Retention (`CleanActivityLog`) force-deletes old rows including trashed ones inside `Tenant::bypass()`, uniformly (purge keeps rows until retention, ORG-12; RK-D8 residual). Failed sign-ins are host-tagged and store the typed value only when it is a valid email address (lower-cased, `properties.email`); anything else is stored as `email = null`, `invalid_address = true`, so a password typed into the email field is never kept (CV-17, RK-D2). Viewers of that host see the typed address (spec §4.8 "with email"). Causer names are shown across scopes, super admins included (spec §4.8 "causers resolved without the tenant scope", RK-D1). (D-28, R-3, R-4, C-17)
- **RL-8 Host-scoped reads.** Any-host pages read tenant models only through `App\Tenancy\HostScope::read(Closure)`: tenant bound → the closure as is (scoped); no tenant and the signed-in user is a super admin → `Tenant::bypass()`; otherwise `AuthorizationException`. `HostScope` covers tenant models only: central-model reads filter with `HostScope::organisationId()` (the tenant id on a tenant host; `null` = all for a super admin centrally) and client-sent organisation ids are ignored on tenant hosts (RK-I4). `HostScope::lockForWrite(Organisation)` locks and re-reads the organisation inside the caller's transaction, refuses an archived one (`organisation` validation error) and one that is not the bound tenant (`AuthorizationException`) (RK-I11). Pages are not added to the bypass allow-list (resolves C-2). `users.edit` and `organisations.edit` take `int` parameters and resolve per request (DEC26-8, USR-20, OR-M5); components hold `#[Locked]` ids, never model props (R-7).
- **RL-9 Cross-scope names.** `App\Tenancy\UserNames::of(list<int>)` resolves display names across organisations (incl. deleted users) for causers, inviters and impersonators, and is fed only ids taken from rows the caller already read through its scope — never a client-sent id (RK-M4). (R-5)
- **RL-10 Matrix.** Parameter pages (`users.edit`, `organisations.edit`) stay in the matrix via `matrixParameters()`; new outcomes `forbidden` (Task 8), `organisations` (Task 17) and `not found` (Task 18), each with its assertion arm; the signed `invitations.accept` is excluded (Task 11) and covered by its own host tests. (C-25, DEC26-17)
- **RL-11 Interim UI.** One permission-gated "Administration" (nl "Beheer") group in the current sidebar; a `<x-flash-toast />` bridge that turns `session('status')` into a Flux toast on app pages (the profile page's duplicate status callout is dropped); a sticky impersonation banner component in the app layout. M5 replaces or moves all three. (C-5, D-30)
- **RL-12 Wizard.** `organisations.create` is a `Route::central()` page; the organisation, its pending first admin (organisation_admin template, chosen locale) and the invitation are created in one transaction; the mail is queued after commit and its worker-built link is pinned in `CreateOrganisationTest` (OR-I2); no per-organisation role is ever created (DEC-21, W7); the wizard writes exactly `organisation.created`, `user.roles_changed` and `invitation.sent` (OR-M10). (C-6, D-12)
- **RL-13 Invitations.** Roles attach to the pending user at invite time through `UpdateUserRoles` (spec §4.6), so inviting needs `users.create` **and** `roles.assign` — `InvitationPolicy::create` checks both and the invite page authorises it in `mount()` (OR-M7) — and the escalation guard applies (X5); at least one role is required. An invite writes `user.roles_changed` and `invitation.sent`, never the token or link (OR-M10, RK-M11). The pending user's name is the address until the invitee chooses one. The token is 64 random characters, stored as `token_hash` (sha256, unique, lookup) and `token` (encrypted cast, nullable, **cleared on accept**), never plain and never on `users` (W13, RK-B3). "Copy invite link" is the `viewLink` ability: the `remind` conditions plus `roles.assign` plus the subset rule over the pending user's permissions (super admins via `Gate::before`), because the link is a bearer credential for the invitation's roles (RK-B3). Foreign keys: `invited_by` nullable `nullOnDelete`; `organisation_id` `restrictOnDelete` (purge deletes invitations first); `user_id` `cascadeOnDelete`. `InviteUser` locks the organisation with `HostScope::lockForWrite()` **before** `Tenant::run()` (inside it the cross-tenant check would be trivially true). Cancel `forceDelete()`s the invitation and soft-deletes the pending user (spec §4.5; OR-E1 rejected); purge `forceDelete()`s (C-8). Remind = resend: renews `expires_at`, keeps the token, sets `reminder_sent_at`, is allowed when expired and refused once accepted (W5, C-10); cancel is refused once accepted; accept locks the row (X9); links are built at send time in the worker; outstanding links after a slug rename are rebuilt by a reminder (X13, accepted residual). (D-16, D-17, D-18)
- **RL-14 Address availability.** One rule, `App\Rules\AvailableEmail`, for invite, admin edit, restore and the profile email change: deleted users never block; an address held by a user of another organisation or by a super admin gets the generic "This address can't be used."; inside the actor's own organisation the specific message — "already has an open invitation" when the holder's status is `pending_activation` (no `invitations` lookup, so it also covers W4's hand-set pending users, OR-I3), otherwise "already used in this organisation". The rule remains an existence oracle for "used somewhere"; accepted as a residual until M7's limits (RK-M1, RK-D3). (D-19, W9)
- **RL-15 Accept page.** State order: `accepted` ("already accepted — please log in") → `expired` (resend shown to signed-in users who may `remind`) → `signed-in` ("You are signed in as :name" with a sign-out button) → `form` (OR-I10, OR-E4). `accept()` refuses while anyone is signed in and re-checks, inside the locked transaction, that the pending user is not trashed and still `pending_activation` (RK-M3). Unknown or cancelled tokens and foreign hosts answer 404 (friendly wording arrives with M5's 404 page, CV-11). The page sends `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` (RK-M12). After accepting, the invitee is signed in (session regenerated) and lands on the dashboard with a welcome toast. The page and the invitation mails render in the invitee's `users.locale` (OD-2 = A). (C-11, X12)
- **RL-16 Users.** `users.edit` is gated by `users.view` (it doubles as show page) with editable sections per ability. On your own account the address is read-only with a link to the profile page and `UpdateUser` refuses it (E1 stays closed: no address change without the signed self-service link, CV-1, RK-B2), and there are no status/role controls. A pending user's address and status are read-only (only accepting activates; address changes go through cancel + re-invite), and deleting a pending user is refused (cancel the invitation instead). Changing another user's address needs a fresh password confirmation (RL-18) and notifies the old address (`EmailChangedByAdministrator`, parity with M3's `EmailChangeRequested`; D-14, CV-a). Disabling or deleting a user cuts their sessions and remember token (RL-28). The archived view excludes pending users (cancelled invitations, C-9); pending rows have no delete control and link to the pending invitations list (CV-20). An admin email change applies directly and forgets the pending self-service email-change link and the old address's reset tokens (FU3-7). Restore is enforced in `RestoreUser` (`ALWAYS_CHECKED` unchanged, D-7). The central index lists every user incl. super admins (organisation column "Platform"), filters by organisation and reads team roles with one pivot query (R-6, C-26, D-29); super admins are hidden from non-super actors (DEC-26 (12)); row controls come from one batch evaluation of the same rules the policy uses (RL-26); `UserStatus::color()` lands now (D-24).
- **RL-17 Organisations.** `require_second_factor` is not shown until M7 (D-21). Archive, restore and purge run in actions with a transaction and audit (the cascade stays in the observer); restore and purge lock the organisation row and re-check `trashed()` inside the transaction (RK-I10). Restore is refused while a cascaded user's address is taken (the message lists the addresses, C-15). Archive cuts the cascaded users' sessions and remember tokens (RL-28). Purge detaches promoted super admins — trashed ones included — (`organisation_id` → null, listed in the `organisation.purged` properties) instead of refusing (D-11, RK-I10), force-deletes invitations `withTrashed()`, deletes `sessions` rows explicitly (no FK, C-16) and the purged users' `password_reset_tokens`, forgets the permission cache after commit (CV-13, RK-I10) and keeps activity rows. Names and slugs of archived organisations stay reserved — the message that says so is shown to super admins only, everyone else gets "This name can't be used." (C-14, RK-M2). Demoting a promoted super admin whose organisation is archived is refused ("Restore the organisation before removing super admin."), which keeps `Hosts::homeOf()`'s `LogicException` out of the reset and email-change paths (FU3-4, CV-3, CV-f). `restore`/`forceDelete` keep checking super admin (equivalent to `organisations.delete` while it is super-only, C-27). Only super admins change a slug (OD-3 = B).
- **RL-18 Fresh password confirmation** (`ConfirmsPasswords`, now with a server-built return URL) guards irreversible, platform-power or account-takeover actions: purge, the super-admin switch, and changing **another** user's address (RK-D4, CV-a). Archive, delete user and impersonation start do not ask (reversible, or session-bound with reason + audit). (D-13, C-18, DEC27-4)
- **RL-19 Roles.** System-role names are refused trimmed, case-insensitively and with spaces/hyphens folded to `_` (`Organisation_Admin`, ` super admin `), in the role actions and in `UpdateUserRoles` (FU2-4, D-22); comparisons happen in PHP over the team's names (no LIKE: `_` is a wildcard). Deleting an assigned custom role is allowed: the modal shows the holder count, holders lose the role, and it is logged (X14, D-23). `RolePolicy` is registered with `Gate::policy()` and, for non-super actors, also requires `$role->team_id === $actor->organisation_id` (RK-M9). System-role protection lives in the actions (super admins pass `update` through `Gate::before`) and in `RolePolicy::delete` (always checked). Only `roles.manage` (super-only per spec §4.6) manages roles; organisation admins see them read-only (C-20, CV-d). `UpdateRole` keeps permissions the editor hides (`users.impersonate` while the module is off), so a save never strips them (§6.8 "stable sync", CV-4). Permission input is converted with `Permission::tryFrom()`; unknown or non-assignable values are a validation error (OR-M8, RK-M7). Role actions lock the organisation with `HostScope::lockForWrite()` (RK-I11) and forget the permission cache after commit.
- **RL-20 Impersonation.** It starts from a Livewire action on `users.index` marked `#[RequiresTenant]` (module off → 404 and hidden) — this is §6.8's "start route" — and stops through `DELETE /impersonation` (`impersonation.stop`), registered only when the module is on; the controller and the start and confirm actions also `abort_unless(Impersonation::enabled(), 404)` (RK-I12). The flag check lives in `UserPolicy::impersonate` (a policy method wins over `Gate::define`, so none is added, C-3). The target must belong to the current tenant (super admins "Open" the organisation first) and be active and not deleted (W3). "Non-admin" means the target does not hold the organisation_admin template (by id), and for non-super actors the target's effective permissions — role and direct ones, read with explicit queries — are a subset of the actor's (DEC-26 (12) principle, X6, RK-I6) (C-4, D-6). Targets with 2FA are allowed. Start and stop forget `auth.password_confirmed_at` and rewrite `password_hash_web`; the impersonator's password hash is stored at start.
  **`EnforceImpersonation`** (web group, before `Authenticate`, reads the pair from the session without touching the guard) re-validates every request: module on; target resolvable, active and passing `HostLoginRule`; impersonator resolvable, active and passing `HostLoginRule` with an unchanged password hash; `UserAbilities::mayImpersonate()` still true. On failure it logs `impersonation.stop` with `ended_because` (`module_disabled`, `target_unavailable`, `no_longer_allowed`, `impersonator_unavailable`, `impersonator_credentials_changed`) and an explicit causer (the impersonator, or none plus `properties.impersonator_id` when they no longer resolve), then returns to the impersonator when they still qualify, otherwise signs out with `Impersonation::signOut()` (clear + `logoutCurrentDevice()` + invalidate — never `logout()`, which would cycle the target's remember token) (RK-B4, RK-I1, RK-I2, RK-I3, RK-M6, IMP-8, FU3-6). `isActive()` and the causer rewrite do not depend on the flag.
  A real `Login` clears impersonation state; logout while impersonating stops it (logged) and then signs the real user out; handoffs cannot be issued while impersonating, and consuming one while impersonating stops it first (logged) and never takes the same-user shortcut (RK-I1). After a stop the impersonator lands on `users.index` when they hold `users.view`, otherwise on the dashboard (OR-M6). Settings actions while impersonating stay behind the target's password confirmation (forgotten at start), pinned by a test; there is no extra page block (RK-D7). Start is logged after the swap (with the reason), stop before it; the causer of everything logged meanwhile is the impersonator, with `impersonated_as` = the target id. (D-5, R-2)
- **RL-21 Module-flag tests.** Module routes live in `routes/impersonation.php`, required only when the flag is on. `useImpersonationModule(bool)` flips the config (Task 19) and rebuilds the route collection (Task 20: off → `Route::setRoutes()` with a filtered new `RouteCollection` + `refreshNameLookups()`; on → require the module file when its routes are missing) (CV-19, RK-I12). `phpunit.xml` pins `MODULE_IMPERSONATION=true` **without** `force`, so the `sqlite-free` CI job's `MODULE_IMPERSONATION=false` runs the whole suite on the off path; that env and its `CiWorkflowTest` assertion land in Task 19, every impersonation test from then on starts with `useImpersonationModule(true)` (or `false` for off rows), and every gate from Task 19 on runs the off suite locally (OR-B2, CV-2, OR-I1, OR-E3). (R-8, IMP-12)
- **RL-22 Handoff follow-ups.** A link opened by the already signed-in token user is consumed, dispatches `HandoffConsumed` and redirects without a new sign-in (no remember-token cycling, CV-14). A link opened while **another** user is signed in renders a confirmation page ("You are signed in as :name. Continue as :other?") whose POST consumes the token and replaces only this browser's session (`logoutCurrentDevice()` + invalidate); a GET never replaces a different user's session (FU3-2, RK-I14, CV-b). `IssueHandoff` turns `Hosts::homeOf()`'s `LogicException` into `AuthorizationException` (FU3-4); callers pass only the authenticated actor (FU3-1); consumption is tested on the apex and the admin host (FU3-3, CV-9).
- **RL-23 Slug rule.** `App\Rules\OrganisationSlug`: lower-case `[a-z0-9-]`, 3–63 characters, no edge hyphen, not in `tenancy.reserved_slugs`, not `config('tenancy.admin_subdomain')`; `Hosts::slugOf()` also excludes the admin subdomain (FU2-1, FU3-5).
- **RL-24 Rate limiting** of invite/remind (D-20) and the other limiter items are M7 hardening (see Scope), not M4 (CV-6, CV-e).
- **RL-25 Current-user helper.** The private `user(): User` helper (DEC25-2) becomes `App\Concerns\ResolvesCurrentUser::currentUser()` in Task 7, and the three settings components switch to it, because M4 adds about ten more components.
- **RL-26 Permission-subset rule** (RK-B2, RK-B3, RK-D5). For non-super actors, `UserPolicy::{update,updateStatus,delete,restore,impersonate}` and `InvitationPolicy::viewLink` also require that the target's effective permissions in the target's team are a subset of the actor's. `App\Authorization\EffectivePermissions` reads them with explicit queries (roles assigned with that team id, the template included, plus direct `model_has_permissions` rows of that team; no Spatie relations, no cache), with a batch variant for a page of users. `App\Authorization\UserAbilities` holds the decision logic once; `UserPolicy` calls it with sets for one target, index pages with sets for a page. Equal permission sets pass, so organisation admins still manage each other (W12 still guards the last one); a helpdesk role with `users.update` cannot touch an organisation admin.
- **RL-27 Lock order** (RK-I13, CV-8). `App\Authorization\LockoutGuard` locks every candidate row — all non-deleted super admins, or all non-deleted template holders of the team — **target included**, with `orderBy('users.id')->lockForUpdate()->pluck()`, and decides "another active one remains" in PHP. Concurrent mutual demotions then serialise instead of deadlocking. FU2-4's optional deadlock retry is not added (ordered locking removes the cycle, and a retry cannot work inside the nested transactions of `InviteUser`/`CreateOrganisation`).
- **RL-28 Sessions on lock-out** (RK-I7). Disabling a user, deleting a user and archiving an organisation (for its cascaded users) delete the users' `sessions` rows and cycle `remember_token` inside the transaction, through one helper, `App\Tenancy\Auth\Sessions::endFor()` (a plain delete by `sessions.user_id`; Task 6), so a re-enable or restore never revives an old session or remember cookie (applies with the database session driver, the kit default).
- **RL-29 Extra security events** (CV-g). The authentication subscriber also records `auth.two_factor_failed` (Fortify `TwoFactorAuthenticationFailed`) and `auth.recovery_code_used` (`RecoveryCodeReplaced`), host-tagged.
- **RL-30 Residuals accepted for v1** (recorded in DEC-28): the address-availability oracle (RL-14); personal data of a purged organisation stays in its activity rows until retention (spec ORG-12 "activity rows are kept"; anonymisation is a possible later option, RK-D8); outstanding invitation links after a slug rename (X13).

### Owner rulings (2026-10-11)

- **OD-1 = C: impersonation is in-house.** `App\Tenancy\Auth\Impersonation` performs the swap on the stock session guard (session keys, `migrate(true)` + `setUser()`, password-hash refresh, stored impersonator hash, clearing on a real `Login`). `lab404/laravel-impersonate` is not installed: its discovery replaces Laravel's `session` guard driver for the whole app, which drops `auth.timebox_duration` (silently regressing DEC-27 (1)), keys the password-hash cookie HMAC with a constant instead of `APP_KEY`, and its `take()`/`leave()` do no authorisation or depth check (R-1, D-1, D-2). The per-request enforcement (`EnforceImpersonation`, RL-20) is kit code either way. Consequences: no new dependency besides activitylog, full Larastan typing, no forced logout of existing sessions on install; skv3 owns the swap code, pinned by HTTP tests; DEC-28 strikes the spec §3 `lab404/laravel-impersonate` row.
- **OD-2 = A: locale in M4.** Task 10 adds `App\Enums\Locale` (`nl`, `en`, `default()`) and `users.locale` (new migration, default taken from `Locale::default()`, CV-21). The invite form and the organisation wizard ask for the invitee's locale; invitation mails and the accept page use it. M5 only adds the locale middleware, the language switchers and the profile field. This pulls one DEC-26 M5 item forward and resolves the spec conflict between §4.5 "invite by email with locale" and DEC-26 (C-1, D-4, USR-3).
- **OD-3 = B: only super admins change a slug.** Organisation admins edit their organisation's name and description and see the slug read-only; `UpdateOrganisation` applies a slug change only for super-admin actors (Tasks 14 and 18). A rename made on the organisation's own host moves the editor to the new host through a handoff (ORG-16). The old slug is free immediately; there is no reservation or redirect of old slugs in v1 (D-9, D-10).

| Critic decision | Ruling |
|---|---|
| CV-a / RK-D4 admin email change: notice and confirmation | Both: old-address notice (M3 parity) and fresh confirmation for another user's address (RL-16, RL-18). |
| CV-b / RK-D6 / RK-I14 handoff while another user is signed in | Confirmation page with POST; a GET never swaps a different session (RL-22). |
| CV-c / RK-D2 failed-login addresses | Spec §4.8 settles "with email"; only valid addresses stored, shown to that host's viewers (RL-7). |
| CV-d only super admins manage roles | Spec §4.6 settles it (`roles.manage` super-only) (RL-19). |
| CV-e hardening milestone | M7, with invite/remind limits (Scope, RL-24). |
| CV-f demote a promoted super admin of an archived organisation | Refused until the organisation is restored (RL-17). |
| CV-g 2FA failures and recovery-code use | Audited (RL-29). |
| CV-h `permissions:sync` audit | Not audited; M6's doctor reports drift (RL-6). |
| CV-i / CV-11 unknown or cancelled token page | 404 now; friendly wording with M5's error pages (RL-15). |
| OR-E1 cancel force-deletes the pending user | Rejected: spec §4.5 says soft-delete; C-9 keeps the rows out of views and restore (RL-13). |
| OR-E2 audit entries per invitation | `user.roles_changed` + `invitation.sent` (+ `organisation.created` in the wizard), pinned by tests (RL-12, RL-13). |
| OR-E3 when to run the flag-off suite | Every gate from Task 19 on (RL-21). |
| OR-E4 signed-in admin on an expired link | The expired state (with resend) wins over "signed in as" (RL-15). |
| RK-D1 super admins in tenant audit logs | Names shown (spec §4.8 cross-scope causer names) (RL-7). |
| RK-D3 address oracle | Accepted residual (RL-14, RL-30). |
| RK-D5 scope of the subset rule | Every non-super user-management write and the invite link (RL-26). |
| RK-D7 settings while impersonating | Rely on the target-password confirmation gates; pinned by a test (RL-20). |
| RK-D8 purge and personal data | Spec ORG-12 keeps rows; uniform retention; residual recorded (RL-7, RL-30). |

## Route × host matrix end state

End state of `tests/Feature/Tenancy/RouteHostMatrixTest.php` after Task 24:

- `matrixRoutes()` adds: `users.index` (Task 8), `users.edit` (Task 9), `users.invite` and `invitations.pending` (Task 13), `organisations.index` (Task 17), `organisations.create` and `organisations.edit` (Task 18), `roles.index` (Task 23), `activity.index` (Task 24).
- Exclusions add: `invitations.accept` (Task 11, signed token route, covered by its own host tests). `auth.handoff` stays excluded; its new POST is not a GET route.
- Outcomes: `'ok'|'login'|'dashboard'|'confirm'|'forbidden'|'not found'|'organisations'`, each new one with its assertion arm and its `@return` widening in the task that introduces it (`forbidden` Task 8, `organisations` Task 17, `not found` Task 18). `matrixParameters()` (Task 9) supplies `{user}` (a member of the test organisation, Task 9) and `{organisation}` (the test organisation, Task 18), both created before the host switch.
- Rules: signed-in non-super actors on central hosts → `login` first (membership); `organisations.create` on a tenant host → `not found` for every signed-in actor (the host check runs before `can:`); permission pages → `forbidden` for the role-less member on its tenant host; `home` (`/`) → `organisations` for super admins on the apex and the admin host.

### Task 1: Audit-log foundation (activitylog, Activity model, events, one writer, retention, lang coverage)

**Covers:** AUD-1 (model, organisation tagging, diffs in `attribute_changes`), AUD-5 (real indexed `organisation_id` column without FK, `created_at` index, IP address and user agent captured), AUD-6 (`ActivityEvent` enum with translated labels), AUD-10 (published config with `clean_after_days => (int) env('ACTIVITYLOG_RETENTION_DAYS', 365)` and `actions.clean_log` = `App\Actions\Audit\CleanActivityLog`, which deletes inside `Tenant::bypass()`; scheduling is M7), AUD-11 (rows with `organisation_id = null` are central and never appear in tenant reads), AUD-12 (the organisation soft-delete cascade over `tenancy.tenant_models` includes `Activity`), ORG-12 (activity rows outlive a purged organisation: no FK), R-3 (retention must force-delete, trashed rows included), C-8, C-13 (`organisation_id` never mass-assignable), C-24 (no clash with the vendor `ActivityEvent`), X7 (central actions on an organisation's data appear in that organisation's log), TEN-5/TEN-7 (the new tenant model follows the tenant-model rules), RL-1, RL-3, RL-4, RL-5, RL-6 (arch rule), RL-7 (retention), OR-I8, OR-I9, RK-B1, RK-I5, CV-16.

What this task must achieve, in plain words:
- Add exactly one Composer dependency, `spatie/laravel-activitylog` 5.1.1. The owner approved it with this plan; the commit message names it.
- `App\Models\Activity` extends the vendor model and is a tenant model: `BelongsToOrganisation` + `SoftDeletes`, listed in `config('tenancy.tenant_models')`, `mayExistWithoutOrganisation()` returns `true` (central events have no organisation), and `organisation_id` is guarded. The `event` column is a plain string with **no enum cast** (vendor code assigns raw names such as `updated`; an enum cast would throw, RK-B1); `kitEvent()` turns it into an `ActivityEvent` with `tryFrom()`.
- Every kit entry is written by one class, `App\Actions\Audit\RecordActivity`. It stores `event` = the `ActivityEvent` value, `description` = the same value, `log_name` = `ActivityEvent::group()`, custom data in `properties`, diffs in `attribute_changes`. The vendor `activity()` helper, facade, `ActivityLogger` and the vendor model-event trait are used nowhere else (arch rules).
- Organisation tagging has two modes (RL-5). **Host mode** — events of the `authentication`, `security` and `impersonation` groups: the bound tenant's id, else `null` (central); the subject's organisation and an explicit organisation are ignored. **Subject mode** — every other event: an explicit organisation first, then the subject's organisation (an `Organisation` subject is itself; any model with an `organisation_id` attribute uses it), then the bound tenant, else `null`.
- IP address and user agent are stored only for a routed web request (`request()->route() !== null`), never in a queued job or a command.
- Retention: `activitylog:clean` force-deletes rows older than `clean_after_days` across all organisations, soft-deleted (archived) rows included; the period comes from `ACTIVITYLOG_RETENTION_DAYS` as an integer (default 365).
- `LangCoverageTest` fails when a `__()` / `trans()` / `@lang()` key used in the M4 paths is missing from `lang/nl.json`. The test helper `dutchTranslationKeys()` moves from `PermissionCatalogueTest.php` to `tests/Pest.php` so later test files never depend on another test file under `--parallel`.

```php
/** @return list<string> */
function dutchTranslationKeys(): array
{
    /** @var array<string, string> $dutch */
    $dutch = json_decode((string) file_get_contents(lang_path('nl.json')), true, flags: JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR);

    return array_keys($dutch);
}

/**
 * Every audit entry with this event, oldest first, read across organisations and including archived
 * (soft-deleted) rows, whatever host the test is on.
 *
 * @return EloquentCollection<int, Activity>
 */
function recordedActivity(ActivityEvent $event): EloquentCollection
{
    return app(CurrentTenant::class)->bypass(fn (): EloquentCollection => Activity::query()
        ->withTrashed()
        ->where('event', $event->value)
        ->orderBy('id')
        ->get());
}
```

```php
it('captures no IP address in a queued job or a command', function (string $context): void {
    $organisation = Organisation::factory()->create();
    $organisationId = $organisation->id;

    if ($context === 'queued job') {
        // Runs through the sync queue (JobProcessing, central context); static: a queued closure is serialised.
        dispatch(static function () use ($organisationId): void {
            app(RecordActivity::class)->handle(ActivityEvent::OrganisationUpdated, Organisation::query()->findOrFail($organisationId));
        });
    } else {
        Artisan::registerCommand(new ClosureCommand('audit:probe', function () use ($organisationId): void {
            app(RecordActivity::class)->handle(ActivityEvent::OrganisationUpdated, Organisation::query()->findOrFail($organisationId));
        }));
        expect(Artisan::call('audit:probe'))->toBe(0);
    }

    $entry = recordedActivity(ActivityEvent::OrganisationUpdated)->sole();
    expect([$entry->ip_address, $entry->user_agent, $entry->organisation_id])->toBe([null, null, $organisationId]);
})->with(['queued job', 'command']);
```

```php
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

/** covers §4.8, §4.9 */

use App\Models\Activity;
use App\Models\Organisation;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Artisan;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;

it('force-deletes entries older than the retention period, archived ones included, and keeps newer ones (R-3)', function (): void {
    config(['activitylog.clean_after_days' => 30]);
    $organisation = Organisation::factory()->create();

    $this->travelTo(now()->subDays(31));
    Activity::factory()->for($organisation)->create();
    Activity::factory()->for($organisation)->create()->delete();
    Activity::factory()->create();
    $this->travelBack();
    $recent = Activity::factory()->for($organisation)->create();

    expect(Artisan::call('activitylog:clean', ['--force' => true]))->toBe(0)
        ->and(Artisan::output())->toContain('Deleted 3 record(s)')
        ->and(DB::table('activity_log')->pluck('id')->map(fn (mixed $id): int => (int) $id)->all())->toBe([$recent->id]);
});

it('reads the retention period from the environment as an integer', function (): void {
    // Laravel's env() also reads the process environment (putenv), where Dotenv put the developer's .env
    // values at boot, so that is saved and cleared too.
    $retentionWith = function (?string $value): mixed {
        $saved = [$_ENV['ACTIVITYLOG_RETENTION_DAYS'] ?? null, $_SERVER['ACTIVITYLOG_RETENTION_DAYS'] ?? null];
        $savedPutenv = getenv('ACTIVITYLOG_RETENTION_DAYS');
        unset($_ENV['ACTIVITYLOG_RETENTION_DAYS'], $_SERVER['ACTIVITYLOG_RETENTION_DAYS']);
        putenv('ACTIVITYLOG_RETENTION_DAYS');

        if ($value !== null) {
            $_ENV['ACTIVITYLOG_RETENTION_DAYS'] = $_SERVER['ACTIVITYLOG_RETENTION_DAYS'] = $value;
            putenv('ACTIVITYLOG_RETENTION_DAYS='.$value);
        }

        try {
            /** @var array{clean_after_days: mixed} $config */
            $config = require config_path('activitylog.php');

            return $config['clean_after_days'];
        } finally {
            unset($_ENV['ACTIVITYLOG_RETENTION_DAYS'], $_SERVER['ACTIVITYLOG_RETENTION_DAYS']);

            if ($saved[0] !== null) {
                $_ENV['ACTIVITYLOG_RETENTION_DAYS'] = $saved[0];
            }

            if ($saved[1] !== null) {
                $_SERVER['ACTIVITYLOG_RETENTION_DAYS'] = $saved[1];
            }

            putenv('ACTIVITYLOG_RETENTION_DAYS');

            if ($savedPutenv !== false) {
                putenv('ACTIVITYLOG_RETENTION_DAYS='.$savedPutenv);
            }
        }
    };

    expect($retentionWith('30'))->toBe(30)
        ->and($retentionWith(null))->toBe(365);
});
```

```php
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

/** covers §6.5 */

use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Lang;

it('has a Dutch translation for every __() key in the M4 paths (OR-I8)', function (): void {
    // The paths M4 writes copy in. Starter screens (settings, auth views) get their Dutch copy in M5.
    $directories = [
        'app/Actions', 'app/Authorization', 'app/Concerns', 'app/Enums', 'app/Http/Controllers', 'app/Mail',
        'app/Notifications', 'app/Rules', 'app/Tenancy', 'resources/views/pages/users', 'resources/views/pages/invitations',
        'resources/views/pages/organisations', 'resources/views/pages/roles', 'resources/views/pages/activity',
        'resources/views/mail',
    ];
    $singleFiles = [
        'resources/views/pages/auth/handoff-confirm.blade.php',
        'resources/views/components/flash-toast.blade.php',
        'resources/views/components/impersonation-banner.blade.php',
    ];

    $files = [
        ...kitSourceFiles(...$directories),
        ...array_values(array_filter($singleFiles, fn (string $path): bool => is_file(base_path($path)))),
    ];
    $dutch = dutchTranslationKeys();
    $missing = [];

    foreach ($files as $path) {
        preg_match_all(
            '/(?:(?<![\w$>:])(?:__|trans_choice|trans)|@lang)\(\s*([\'"])((?:\\\\.|(?!\1).)*)\1/s',
            (string) file_get_contents(base_path($path)),
            $matches,
            PREG_SET_ORDER,
        );

        foreach ($matches as $match) {
            $key = $match[1] === "'" ? str_replace(["\\'", '\\\\'], ["'", '\\'], $match[2]) : stripcslashes($match[2]);
            // Group keys (passwords.token) live in lang/nl/*.php; every other key in lang/nl.json.
            $isGroupKey = preg_match('/^[\w-]+\.[\w.-]+$/', $key) === 1;
            $known = in_array($key, $dutch, true) || ($isGroupKey && Lang::hasForLocale($key, 'nl'));

            if (! $known) {
                $missing[] = "{$path}: {$key}";
            }
        }
    }

    expect($missing)->toBe([]);
});
```

- [ ] **Step 7: Add the audit vocabulary**

`app/Enums/ActivityEvent.php`:

```php
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace App\Enums;

use Illuminate\Support\Str;
use LogicException;

/**
 * The audit vocabulary (§4.8). The value is stored as the entry's event and description, group() as its
 * log name. Entries of the authentication, security and impersonation groups are tagged with the host's
 * organisation, every other entry with its subject's (RL-5). Not the vendor's
 * Spatie\Activitylog\Enums\ActivityEvent (created, updated, …), which the kit does not use.
 */
enum ActivityEvent: string
{
    case Login = 'auth.login';
    case LoginFailed = 'auth.login_failed';
    case Logout = 'auth.logout';
    case PasswordResetRequested = 'auth.password_reset_requested';
    case PasswordResetCompleted = 'auth.password_reset_completed';
    case HandoffConsumed = 'auth.handoff_consumed';
    case TwoFactorFailed = 'auth.two_factor_failed';
    case RecoveryCodeUsed = 'auth.recovery_code_used';
    case PasswordChanged = 'security.password_changed';
    case TwoFactorEnabled = 'security.two_factor_enabled';
    case TwoFactorDisabled = 'security.two_factor_disabled';
    case RecoveryCodesRegenerated = 'security.recovery_codes_regenerated';
    case PasskeyRegistered = 'security.passkey_registered';
    case PasskeyDeleted = 'security.passkey_deleted';
    case UserUpdated = 'user.updated';
    case UserStatusChanged = 'user.status_changed';
    case UserDeleted = 'user.deleted';
    case UserRestored = 'user.restored';
    case UserRolesChanged = 'user.roles_changed';
    case SuperAdminGranted = 'user.super_admin_granted';
    case SuperAdminRevoked = 'user.super_admin_revoked';
    case InvitationSent = 'invitation.sent';
    case InvitationReminderSent = 'invitation.reminder_sent';
    case InvitationAccepted = 'invitation.accepted';
    case InvitationCancelled = 'invitation.cancelled';
    case OrganisationCreated = 'organisation.created';
    case OrganisationUpdated = 'organisation.updated';
    case OrganisationArchived = 'organisation.archived';
    case OrganisationRestored = 'organisation.restored';
    case OrganisationPurged = 'organisation.purged';
    case RoleCreated = 'role.created';
    case RoleUpdated = 'role.updated';
    case RoleDeleted = 'role.deleted';
    case ImpersonationStarted = 'impersonation.start';
    case ImpersonationStopped = 'impersonation.stop';

    public function label(): string
    {
        return match ($this) {
            self::Login => __('Signed in'),
            self::LoginFailed => __('Sign-in failed'),
            self::Logout => __('Signed out'),
            self::PasswordResetRequested => __('Password reset requested'),
            self::PasswordResetCompleted => __('Password reset completed'),
            self::HandoffConsumed => __('Signed in with a handoff link'),
            self::TwoFactorFailed => __('Two-factor code rejected'),
            self::RecoveryCodeUsed => __('Recovery code used'),
            self::PasswordChanged => __('Password changed'),
            self::TwoFactorEnabled => __('Two-factor authentication enabled'),
            self::TwoFactorDisabled => __('Two-factor authentication disabled'),
            self::RecoveryCodesRegenerated => __('Recovery codes regenerated'),
            self::PasskeyRegistered => __('Passkey added'),
            self::PasskeyDeleted => __('Passkey removed'),
            self::UserUpdated => __('User updated'),
            self::UserStatusChanged => __('User status changed'),
            self::UserDeleted => __('User deleted'),
            self::UserRestored => __('User restored'),
            self::UserRolesChanged => __('Roles changed'),
            self::SuperAdminGranted => __('Super admin granted'),
            self::SuperAdminRevoked => __('Super admin revoked'),
            self::InvitationSent => __('Invitation sent'),
            self::InvitationReminderSent => __('Invitation resent'),
            self::InvitationAccepted => __('Invitation accepted'),
            self::InvitationCancelled => __('Invitation cancelled'),
            self::OrganisationCreated => __('Organisation created'),
            self::OrganisationUpdated => __('Organisation updated'),
            self::OrganisationArchived => __('Organisation archived'),
            self::OrganisationRestored => __('Organisation restored'),
            self::OrganisationPurged => __('Organisation purged'),
            self::RoleCreated => __('Role created'),
            self::RoleUpdated => __('Role updated'),
            self::RoleDeleted => __('Role deleted'),
            self::ImpersonationStarted => __('Impersonation started'),
            self::ImpersonationStopped => __('Impersonation stopped'),
        };
    }

    /** The log name: authentication, security, users, invitations, organisations, roles or impersonation. */
    public function group(): string
    {
        return match (Str::before($this->value, '.')) {
            'auth' => 'authentication',
            'security' => 'security',
            'user' => 'users',
            'invitation' => 'invitations',
            'organisation' => 'organisations',
            'role' => 'roles',
            'impersonation' => 'impersonation',
            default => throw new LogicException("Activity event [{$this->value}] has no group."),
        };
    }

    /** RL-5 host mode: tagged with the host's organisation (central = none), whatever the subject. */
    public function tagsByHost(): bool
    {
        return in_array($this->group(), ['authentication', 'security', 'impersonation'], true);
    }
}
```

The bypass arch rule (`tests/Arch/TenancyRulesTest.php`) also scans comments, so never write the bypass call syntax in a docblock outside the allowed namespaces. Do not add `app/Models` to its allow-list.

`app/Models/Activity.php`:

```php
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace App\Models;

use App\Enums\ActivityEvent;
use App\Tenancy\Concerns\BelongsToOrganisation;
use Database\Factories\ActivityFactory;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Factories\HasFactory;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\SoftDeletes;
use Illuminate\Support\Carbon;
use Spatie\Activitylog\Models\Activity as VendorActivity;

/**
 * An audit entry (§4.8): a tenant model, so tenant hosts read only their own organisation's rows and
 * central hosts read it inside a tenant bypass. Rows with organisation_id NULL are central events. The
 * event column is a plain string: the vendor writes its own names (updated, …) into it, so an enum cast
 * would break those writes (RK-B1); kitEvent() reads it as an ActivityEvent.
 *
 * @property int|null $organisation_id
 * @property string|null $ip_address
 * @property string|null $user_agent
 * @property Carbon|null $deleted_at
 */
class Activity extends VendorActivity
{
    /** @use HasFactory<ActivityFactory> */
    use BelongsToOrganisation, HasFactory, SoftDeletes;

    /**
     * Public because the vendor model declares it public. organisation_id is set only by the log action.
     *
     * @var list<string>
     */
    public $guarded = ['id', 'organisation_id'];

    public function kitEvent(): ?ActivityEvent
    {
        return $this->event === null ? null : ActivityEvent::tryFrom($this->event);
    }

    /** Central events (super admins on the admin host, failed sign-ins on the apex) have no organisation. */
    public function mayExistWithoutOrganisation(): bool
    {
        return true;
    }
}
```

```php
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Database\Factories;

use App\Enums\ActivityEvent;
use App\Models\Activity;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Factories\Factory;

/** @extends Factory<Activity> */
class ActivityFactory extends Factory
{
    /** @return array<string, mixed> */
    public function definition(): array
    {
        $event = ActivityEvent::OrganisationUpdated;

        return [
            'log_name' => $event->group(),
            'description' => $event->value,
            'event' => $event->value,
            'properties' => [],
        ];
    }

    public function forEvent(ActivityEvent $event): static
    {
        return $this->state(fn (array $attributes): array => [
            'log_name' => $event->group(),
            'description' => $event->value,
            'event' => $event->value,
        ]);
    }
}
```

- [ ] **Step 9: Add the writer, the log action and the retention action**

`app/Actions/Audit/RecordActivity.php`:

```php
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace App\Actions\Audit;

use App\Enums\ActivityEvent;
use App\Models\Activity;
use App\Models\Organisation;
use App\Models\User;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Model;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Auth;
use Spatie\Activitylog\Support\Config;

/**
 * The only writer of audit entries (§4.8, RL-6). The event's value is stored as event and description and
 * its group as log name; custom data goes into properties and diffs into attribute_changes. The entry
 * passes through the configured log action (App\Actions\Audit\LogActivity), which tags the organisation
 * and adds the request's IP address and user agent. Never put a password, a token or a link in here.
 */
final class RecordActivity
{
    /**
     * @param  array<string, mixed>  $properties
     * @param  array{attributes?: array<string, mixed>, old?: array<string, mixed>}  $changes
     * @param  User|null  $causer  who did it; null means the signed-in user, unless $defaultCauser is false
     * @param  Organisation|null  $organisation  explicit tag for subject-mode events (RL-5); null means derive it
     */
    public function handle(
        ActivityEvent $event,
        ?Model $subject = null,
        array $properties = [],
        array $changes = [],
        ?User $causer = null,
        ?Organisation $organisation = null,
        bool $defaultCauser = true,
    ): Activity {
        $causer ??= $defaultCauser ? $this->signedInUser() : null;

        $activity = new Activity;
        $activity->forceFill([
            'log_name' => $event->group(),
            'event' => $event->value,
            'properties' => $properties,
            'attribute_changes' => $changes === [] ? null : $changes,
            'organisation_id' => $organisation?->id,
            'subject_type' => null,
            'subject_id' => null,
            'causer_type' => null,
            'causer_id' => null,
        ]);

        if ($subject instanceof Model) {
            $activity->subject()->associate($subject);
        }

        if ($causer instanceof User) {
            $activity->causer()->associate($causer);
        }

        Config::logActivityAction()->execute($activity, $event->value);

        return $activity;
    }

    private function signedInUser(): ?User
    {
        $user = Auth::guard('web')->user();

        return $user instanceof User ? $user : null;
    }
}
```

`app/Actions/Audit/LogActivity.php`:

```php
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace App\Actions\Audit;

use App\Enums\ActivityEvent;
use App\Models\Organisation;
use App\Tenancy\CurrentTenant;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Model;
use Spatie\Activitylog\Actions\LogActivityAction;

/**
 * Enriches every entry before it is saved (§4.8): the organisation tag (RL-5) and, for a routed web
 * request only, the IP address and user agent. Registered as activitylog.actions.log_activity.
 *
 * Host mode (authentication, security, impersonation): the bound tenant, else central. Subject mode
 * (everything else): the explicit organisation, then the subject's, then the bound tenant, else central.
 */
final class LogActivity extends LogActivityAction
{
    protected function beforeActivityLogged(Model $activity): void
    {
        parent::beforeActivityLogged($activity);

        $activity->forceFill(['organisation_id' => $this->organisationIdFor($activity)]);

        $request = request();

        if ($request->route() !== null) {
            $activity->forceFill([
                'ip_address' => $request->ip(),
                'user_agent' => $request->userAgent(),
            ]);
        }
    }

    private function organisationIdFor(Model $activity): ?int
    {
        $boundId = app(CurrentTenant::class)->current()?->id;

        if (ActivityEvent::tryFrom((string) $activity->getAttribute('event'))?->tagsByHost() === true) {
            return $boundId;
        }

        $explicit = $activity->getAttribute('organisation_id');

        if ($explicit !== null) {
            return (int) $explicit;
        }

        return $this->subjectOrganisationId($activity) ?? $boundId;
    }

    /** The subject was associated by RecordActivity, so reading it never queries. */
    private function subjectOrganisationId(Model $activity): ?int
    {
        $subject = $activity->relationLoaded('subject') ? $activity->getRelation('subject') : null;

        if ($subject instanceof Organisation) {
            return $subject->id;
        }

        // Spatie roles carry team_id instead: role events pass their organisation explicitly.
        if ($subject instanceof Model && array_key_exists('organisation_id', $subject->getAttributes())) {
            $organisationId = $subject->getAttribute('organisation_id');

            return $organisationId === null ? null : (int) $organisationId;
        }

        return null;
    }
}
```

`app/Actions/Audit/CleanActivityLog.php`:

```php
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace App\Actions\Audit;

use App\Models\Activity;
use App\Tenancy\Facades\Tenant;
use Spatie\Activitylog\Actions\CleanActivityLogAction;

/**
 * Retention for `activitylog:clean` (§4.8, R-3): removes old entries of every organisation for good,
 * archived (soft-deleted) ones included. The vendor action would only soft-delete them.
 * Registered as activitylog.actions.clean_log.
 */
final class CleanActivityLog extends CleanActivityLogAction
{
    protected function deleteOldActivities(string $cutOffDate, ?string $logName): int
    {
        return Tenant::bypass(function () use ($cutOffDate, $logName): int {
            $query = Activity::query()->withTrashed()->where('created_at', '<', $cutOffDate);

            if ($logName !== null) {
                $query->where('log_name', $logName);
            }

            return (int) $query->forceDelete();
        });
    }
}
```

### Task 2: Authentication and security audit subscriber

**Covers:** AUD-2 (sign-in, failed sign-in with the typed address, sign-out, password reset requested and completed, two-factor enabled and disabled), AUD-7 (security settings: password change, recovery codes, passkeys; sessions and the second-factor setting are M7), AUD-13 (`HandoffConsumed` audited), HND-1 (audit part), DEC27-1, R-4 (Fortify's `Failed` event carries the plain password: never store any credential except a valid address), RL-5 (host mode), RL-7 (failed sign-ins), RL-29 (failed two-factor code and used recovery code), CV-17, CV-g, RK-I5.

What this task must achieve, in plain words:
- One auto-discovered listener, `App\Listeners\RecordAuthenticationActivity`, records the authentication and security events through `RecordActivity`. All of them are host-mode events (Task 1): tagged with the organisation of the host they happen on, or central on the apex and the admin host, whatever the user's own organisation is. So a promoted super admin's sign-in on the admin host is central and on organisation B's host is B's.
- A failed sign-in stores the typed value only when it is a valid email address (lower-cased, `properties.email`); anything else becomes `['email' => null, 'invalid_address' => true]`, so a password typed into the email field is never kept. The password itself is never read.
- Two-factor "enabled" is recorded from Fortify's `TwoFactorAuthenticationConfirmed` (the kit requires confirmation; `TwoFactorAuthenticationEnabled` fires before the code is confirmed). "Disabled" is recorded only when a confirmed setup is turned off: the security page silently clears an abandoned, never confirmed setup on mount, which is not a change of the second factor.
- The security page's password change dispatches no event, so the page records `security.password_changed` itself.
- Nothing stores a recovery code, a token or a link.

**Files:**
- Create: `app/Listeners/RecordAuthenticationActivity.php`
- Modify: `resources/views/pages/settings/security/security.php` (record `PasswordChanged` after `updatePassword`)
- Test: `tests/Feature/Audit/AuthenticationActivityTest.php`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `App\Actions\Audit\RecordActivity::handle(...)`, `App\Enums\ActivityEvent`, `recordedActivity()` (Task 1); events `Illuminate\Auth\Events\{Login,Failed,Logout,PasswordResetLinkSent,PasswordReset}`, `Laravel\Fortify\Events\{TwoFactorAuthenticationConfirmed,TwoFactorAuthenticationDisabled,RecoveryCodesGenerated,TwoFactorAuthenticationFailed,RecoveryCodeReplaced}`, `Laravel\Passkeys\Events\{PasskeyRegistered,PasskeyDeleted}`, `App\Events\HandoffConsumed(User $user, string $host)`; `Laravel\Fortify\Fortify::username()`; `App\Actions\Auth\IssueHandoff::handle(User $user, string $targetHost, string $path = '/dashboard'): string`.
- Produces: `App\Listeners\RecordAuthenticationActivity::handle(Login|Failed|Logout|PasswordResetLinkSent|PasswordReset|TwoFactorAuthenticationConfirmed|TwoFactorAuthenticationDisabled|RecoveryCodesGenerated|TwoFactorAuthenticationFailed|RecoveryCodeReplaced|PasskeyRegistered|PasskeyDeleted|HandoffConsumed $event): void` (auto-discovered from `app/Listeners`; every entry host-tagged; subject = the event's user). `Failed` records `properties.email` (lower-cased) only when `filter_var($value, FILTER_VALIDATE_EMAIL)` passes, otherwise `['email' => null, 'invalid_address' => true]`; `Login` records `properties.remember`; `HandoffConsumed` records `properties.host`; passkey events record `properties.passkey` (the passkey's name). Causer: the event's user for `Login`, `Logout` and `HandoffConsumed`; the signed-in user (none for guests) for every other event. `PasswordResetLinkSent` and `PasswordReset` record nothing when a tenant is bound and the user does not belong to that host (`! $user->belongsToCurrentHost()`), so another organisation's log never names a user whose address was typed there; on central hosts (no bound tenant) they are recorded as central entries.

```php
        ->assertRedirect(route('two-factor.login'));
```
