- [ ] **Step 3: Add the listener**

`app/Listeners/RecordAuthenticationActivity.php`:

```php
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace App\Listeners;

use App\Actions\Audit\RecordActivity;
use App\Enums\ActivityEvent;
use App\Events\HandoffConsumed;
use App\Models\User;
use App\Tenancy\Facades\Tenant;
use Illuminate\Auth\Events\Failed;
use Illuminate\Auth\Events\Login;
use Illuminate\Auth\Events\Logout;
use Illuminate\Auth\Events\PasswordReset;
use Illuminate\Auth\Events\PasswordResetLinkSent;
use Illuminate\Support\Str;
use Laravel\Fortify\Events\RecoveryCodeReplaced;
use Laravel\Fortify\Events\RecoveryCodesGenerated;
use Laravel\Fortify\Events\TwoFactorAuthenticationConfirmed;
use Laravel\Fortify\Events\TwoFactorAuthenticationDisabled;
use Laravel\Fortify\Events\TwoFactorAuthenticationFailed;
use Laravel\Fortify\Fortify;
use Laravel\Passkeys\Events\PasskeyDeleted;
use Laravel\Passkeys\Events\PasskeyRegistered;

/**
 * Records sign-in and security events in the audit log (§4.8, RL-29). All of them are tagged with the
 * host's organisation (RL-5 host mode). A failed sign-in keeps the typed value only when it is a valid
 * email address, and never any other credential (R-4). Two-factor "enabled" is the confirmation: Fortify's
 * Enabled event fires before the code is confirmed. A password reset for a user of another organisation is
 * never recorded on a tenant host. Auto-discovered (one registration per union member).
 */
final readonly class RecordAuthenticationActivity
{
    /** @var array<class-string, ActivityEvent> */
    private const array EVENTS = [
        Login::class => ActivityEvent::Login,
        Logout::class => ActivityEvent::Logout,
        PasswordResetLinkSent::class => ActivityEvent::PasswordResetRequested,
        PasswordReset::class => ActivityEvent::PasswordResetCompleted,
        HandoffConsumed::class => ActivityEvent::HandoffConsumed,
        TwoFactorAuthenticationFailed::class => ActivityEvent::TwoFactorFailed,
        RecoveryCodeReplaced::class => ActivityEvent::RecoveryCodeUsed,
        TwoFactorAuthenticationConfirmed::class => ActivityEvent::TwoFactorEnabled,
        TwoFactorAuthenticationDisabled::class => ActivityEvent::TwoFactorDisabled,
        RecoveryCodesGenerated::class => ActivityEvent::RecoveryCodesRegenerated,
        PasskeyRegistered::class => ActivityEvent::PasskeyRegistered,
        PasskeyDeleted::class => ActivityEvent::PasskeyDeleted,
    ];

    public function __construct(private RecordActivity $recordActivity) {}

    public function handle(Login|Failed|Logout|PasswordResetLinkSent|PasswordReset|TwoFactorAuthenticationConfirmed|TwoFactorAuthenticationDisabled|RecoveryCodesGenerated|TwoFactorAuthenticationFailed|RecoveryCodeReplaced|PasskeyRegistered|PasskeyDeleted|HandoffConsumed $event): void
    {
        if ($event instanceof Failed) {
            $this->recordFailedSignIn($event);

            return;
        }

        $user = $event->user;
        $activityEvent = self::EVENTS[$event::class] ?? null;

        if (! $user instanceof User || ! $activityEvent instanceof ActivityEvent) {
            return;
        }

        // A reset asked for on another organisation's host names a user who does not belong here; the link
        // goes to their own host (R1), and this host's log never names them. Central hosts still record it.
        if (($event instanceof PasswordResetLinkSent || $event instanceof PasswordReset) && Tenant::current() !== null && ! $user->belongsToCurrentHost()) {
            return;
        }

        // The security page clears an abandoned, never confirmed setup on mount: no second factor changed.
        if ($event instanceof TwoFactorAuthenticationDisabled && ! $user->wasChanged('two_factor_confirmed_at')) {
            return;
        }

        // At Login the guard has not stored the user yet, so the signed-in user is named explicitly.
        $signsInOrOut = $event instanceof Login || $event instanceof Logout || $event instanceof HandoffConsumed;

        $this->recordActivity->handle($activityEvent, $user, $this->propertiesOf($event), causer: $signsInOrOut ? $user : null);
    }

    /** R-4: the credentials hold the plain password; only a valid address is kept (CV-17). */
    private function recordFailedSignIn(Failed $event): void
    {
        $typed = $event->credentials[Fortify::username()] ?? null;

        $properties = is_string($typed) && filter_var($typed, FILTER_VALIDATE_EMAIL) !== false
            ? ['email' => Str::lower($typed)]
            : ['email' => null, 'invalid_address' => true];

        $this->recordActivity->handle(ActivityEvent::LoginFailed, $event->user instanceof User ? $event->user : null, $properties);
    }

    /** @return array<string, mixed> */
    private function propertiesOf(object $event): array
    {
        return match (true) {
            $event instanceof Login => ['remember' => (bool) $event->remember],
            $event instanceof HandoffConsumed => ['host' => $event->host],
            $event instanceof PasskeyRegistered, $event instanceof PasskeyDeleted => ['passkey' => $event->passkey->name],
            default => [],
        };
    }
}
```

Note for reviewers: a wrong password on the password-confirmation screen fires no `Failed` event (Fortify's ConfirmPassword uses `SessionGuard::validate()`, which dispatches nothing), so it is not audited in M4.

```php
    /**
     * Update the password for the currently authenticated user.
     */
    public function updatePassword(RecordActivity $recordActivity): void
    {
        try {
            $validated = $this->validate([
                'current_password' => $this->currentPasswordRules(),
                'password' => $this->passwordRules(),
            ]);
        } catch (ValidationException $e) {
            $this->reset('current_password', 'password', 'password_confirmation');

            throw $e;
        }

        $this->user()->update([
            'password' => $validated['password'],
        ]);

        // §4.8: the page changes the password without an event, so it records the change itself.
        $recordActivity->handle(ActivityEvent::PasswordChanged, $this->user());

        $this->reset('current_password', 'password', 'password_confirmation');

        Flux::toast(variant: 'success', text: __('Password updated.'));
    }
```

### Task 3: Audit user, role and super-admin changes; `LockoutGuard`; harden `UpdateUserRoles` and `SetSuperAdmin`

**Covers:** USR-4 (audit the user's fields except the password), AUD-7 (role assignments), AUD-9 (role assignments and super-admin changes are logged; `SetSuperAdmin` also runs from the console and seeders, where the causer is null), AUTHZ-1 / DEC26-12 / FU2-5 (`SetSuperAdmin` decides on the stored row, not on a possibly stale model), DEC26-6, FU2-4 (`UpdateUserRoles` defence in depth: template matched by id, team roles named like system roles rejected, `guard_name` filtered; the optional deadlock retry is not needed, see RL-27), FU3-4 (demotion guard), ROLE-10, ROLE-14 (audit), ROLE-15 (guard extraction), RL-6, RL-17 (demotion of a promoted super admin of an archived organisation), RL-19 (reserved names in `UpdateUserRoles`), RL-27, C-12, RK-B1, OR-I4, OR-M1, CV-3, CV-8, RK-I13.

What this task must achieve, in plain words:
- `App\Observers\UserActivityObserver` (attached with `#[ObservedBy]` on `User`) records `user.updated` with old and new values whenever a user's `name` or `email` changed, whoever saved it (admin edit, profile page, the email-change link). Only those two fields; never the password, the remember token or the two-factor columns. Status, roles, super admin, deletion and restore get their own explicit events (fillable fields alone would miss them, C-12). A quiet save (`saveQuietly()`) records nothing, for writers that log their own event. The vendor model-event trait is not used.
- `UpdateUserRoles` logs `user.roles_changed` with the old and new role names (sorted), only when the set changed, with the acting user as causer. It matches the organisation_admin template **by id** (a team role that happens to be called `organisation_admin` is not the template), refuses team roles whose name looks like a system role (trimmed, case-insensitive, spaces and hyphens folded to `_`: `Organisation_Admin`, ` super admin `, `organisation-admin`), and ignores roles of another guard (they are "not available").
- `SetSuperAdmin` decides on the stored flag (read after its locks), not on the in-memory model; it attaches or detaches the super_admin badge on **every** call (the test helper `asSuperAdmin()` relies on that), logs `user.super_admin_granted` / `user.super_admin_revoked` only when the flag really changed, and refuses to demote a promoted super admin whose organisation is archived ("Restore the organisation before removing super admin."), so later reset and email-change paths never meet an archived home host.
- `App\Authorization\LockoutGuard` holds both lock-out guards. Each locks the whole candidate set — every non-deleted super admin, or every non-deleted holder of the template in the team — **target included**, ordered by `users.id`, with `lockForUpdate()->pluck()`, and decides in PHP whether another active one remains. Concurrent mutual demotions then wait for each other instead of deadlocking. The messages stay byte-identical: "At least one active super admin must remain." and "An organisation needs at least one active organisation admin.".

**Files:**
- Create: `app/Observers/UserActivityObserver.php`, `app/Authorization/LockoutGuard.php`
- Modify: `app/Models/User.php` (`#[ObservedBy]`), `app/Actions/Users/UpdateUserRoles.php`, `app/Authorization/SetSuperAdmin.php`, `app/Authorization/Role.php`, `lang/nl.json`, `lang/en.json`
- Test: `tests/Feature/Audit/UserActivityTest.php`, `tests/Feature/Users/UpdateUserRolesTest.php` (added cases), `tests/Feature/Authorization/SetSuperAdminTest.php` (added cases), `tests/Feature/Authorization/LockoutGuardTest.php`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `RecordActivity::handle(...)`, `ActivityEvent`, `recordedActivity()` (Task 1); `App\Authorization\PermissionsTeam::run()`, `App\Authorization\SyncPermissions::GUARD` (`'web'`), `App\Enums\UserStatus`, Spatie `Role` model (`roles`, `model_has_roles` with `team_id`); test helpers `asOrgAdmin()`, `asSuperAdmin()`, `onTenant()`, and the file-local `teamRole()`, `systemRoleId()`, `roleNamesOf()` (in `UpdateUserRolesTest.php`) and `badgeRows()` (in `SetSuperAdminTest.php`).
- Produces:
  - `App\Observers\UserActivityObserver::updated(User $user): void` — when `wasChanged('name')` or `wasChanged('email')`: `RecordActivity::handle(ActivityEvent::UserUpdated, $user, changes: ['old' => …, 'attributes' => …])` for the changed fields only (old values from `getOriginal()`, which still holds them during `updated`).
  - `App\Authorization\Role::isReservedName(string $name): bool` (trim, lower-case, runs of spaces/hyphens → `_`, compared with `Role::values()`).
  - `App\Authorization\LockoutGuard` (final): `ensureAnotherActiveSuperAdmin(User $user, string $field): void`, `ensureAnotherActiveOrganisationAdmin(User $user, int $teamId, string $field): void` — `@throws ValidationException` (error under `$field`); call inside the caller's transaction. Tasks 6 and 9 reuse it.
  - `UpdateUserRoles::handle(User $actor, User $target, array $roleIds): void` (signature unchanged) — now constructor-injected (`LockoutGuard`, `RecordActivity`), so it is resolved with `app()` as before; logs `UserRolesChanged` with `['old' => ['roles' => list<string>], 'attributes' => ['roles' => list<string>]]` and `causer: $actor`, only when the set changed.
  - `SetSuperAdmin::handle(User $user, bool $isSuperAdmin): void` (signature unchanged) — now constructor-injected (`LockoutGuard`, `RecordActivity`); demotion guards in this order: no organisation → `is_super_admin`: "Assign an organisation before removing super admin."; archived organisation → `is_super_admin`: "Restore the organisation before removing super admin."; last active super admin → `LockoutGuard`. Logs `SuperAdminGranted`/`SuperAdminRevoked` only when the flag changed (causer = the `web` guard user, null in the console and seeders).

`tests/Feature/Authorization/LockoutGuardTest.php`:

```php
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

/** covers §4.4, §4.6, §6.3 */

use App\Authorization\LockoutGuard;
use App\Authorization\Role;
use App\Models\Organisation;
use App\Models\User;
use Illuminate\Database\Events\QueryExecuted;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;
use Illuminate\Validation\ValidationException;

it('locks every candidate row in id order, the target included (RL-27)', function (): void {
    $organisation = Organisation::factory()->create();
    [$firstAdmin, $secondAdmin] = User::factory()->for($organisation)->count(2)->create()->all();
    withPermissionsTeam($organisation->id, function () use ($firstAdmin, $secondAdmin): void {
        $firstAdmin->assignRole(Role::OrganisationAdmin->value);
        $secondAdmin->assignRole(Role::OrganisationAdmin->value);
    });
    $firstSuperAdmin = User::factory()->superAdmin()->create();
    User::factory()->superAdmin()->create();

    $queries = [];
    DB::listen(function (QueryExecuted $query) use (&$queries): void {
        $queries[] = $query->sql;
    });

    DB::transaction(function () use ($firstSuperAdmin, $firstAdmin, $organisation): void {
        app(LockoutGuard::class)->ensureAnotherActiveSuperAdmin($firstSuperAdmin, 'is_super_admin');
        app(LockoutGuard::class)->ensureAnotherActiveOrganisationAdmin($firstAdmin, $organisation->id, 'roles');
    });

    $superAdmins = collect($queries)->first(fn (string $sql): bool => str_contains($sql, '"is_super_admin"'));
    $organisationAdmins = collect($queries)->first(fn (string $sql): bool => str_contains($sql, '"model_has_roles"."role_id"'));

    foreach ([$superAdmins, $organisationAdmins] as $sql) {
        // The target is not filtered out in SQL (no "!=" / "<>"): it is locked with the others, in id order.
        expect($sql)->toBeString()
            ->toContain('order by "users"."id" asc')
            ->not->toContain('!=')
            ->not->toContain('<>');

        // SQLite has no row locks and compiles no FOR UPDATE clause.
        if (DB::getDriverName() !== 'sqlite') {
            expect($sql)->toContain('for update');
        }
    }
});

it('keeps the existing lock-out messages', function (): void {
    $onlySuperAdmin = User::factory()->superAdmin()->create();
    User::factory()->superAdmin()->disabled()->create();
    $organisation = Organisation::factory()->create();
    $onlyAdmin = User::factory()->for($organisation)->create();
    withPermissionsTeam($organisation->id, fn (): User => $onlyAdmin->assignRole(Role::OrganisationAdmin->value));

    // A try/catch instead of toThrow(Closure): Pest types that closure as Closure(Throwable), so a
    // ValidationException-typed parameter fails Larastan.
    try {
        DB::transaction(fn () => app(LockoutGuard::class)->ensureAnotherActiveSuperAdmin($onlySuperAdmin, 'is_super_admin'));
        $this->fail('Expected a ValidationException.');
    } catch (ValidationException $exception) {
        expect($exception->errors())->toBe(['is_super_admin' => [__('At least one active super admin must remain.')]]);
    }

    try {
        DB::transaction(fn () => app(LockoutGuard::class)->ensureAnotherActiveOrganisationAdmin($onlyAdmin, $organisation->id, 'roles'));
        $this->fail('Expected a ValidationException.');
    } catch (ValidationException $exception) {
        expect($exception->errors())->toBe(['roles' => [__('An organisation needs at least one active organisation admin.')]]);

});
```

```php
    /**
     * Whether a custom role name would pass for a system role (§4.6, FU2-4, RL-19): trimmed, lower-cased,
     * runs of spaces and hyphens folded to "_", then compared with the system role names.
     * "Organisation_Admin", " super admin " and "organisation-admin" are all reserved.
     */
    public static function isReservedName(string $name): bool
    {
        $folded = Str::of($name)->trim()->lower()->replaceMatches('/[\s-]+/', '_')->toString();

        return in_array($folded, self::values(), true);
    }
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Add `LockoutGuard`**

`app/Authorization/LockoutGuard.php`:

```php
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace App\Authorization;

use App\Enums\UserStatus;
use App\Models\User;
use Illuminate\Support\Collection;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;
use Illuminate\Validation\ValidationException;
use LogicException;
use Spatie\Permission\Models\Role as RoleModel;

/**
 * The lock-out guards (§4.4, §4.6, §6.3): never remove the last active, non-deleted super admin or the
 * last active organisation admin of a team. Each guard locks the whole candidate set, target included,
 * in id order and decides in PHP (RL-27), so two concurrent demotions wait for each other instead of
 * deadlocking. Call inside the caller's transaction. pluck() instead of count() or exists(): PostgreSQL
 * refuses FOR UPDATE with aggregates and in EXISTS subqueries.
 */
final class LockoutGuard
{
    /** @throws ValidationException */
    public function ensureAnotherActiveSuperAdmin(User $user, string $field): void
    {
        $statuses = DB::table('users')
            ->where('is_super_admin', true)
            ->whereNull('deleted_at')
            ->orderBy('users.id')
            ->lockForUpdate()
            ->pluck('users.status', 'users.id');

        if (! $this->anotherActiveRemains($statuses, $user)) {
            throw ValidationException::withMessages([
                $field => __('At least one active super admin must remain.'),
            ]);
        }
    }

    /** @throws ValidationException */
    public function ensureAnotherActiveOrganisationAdmin(User $user, int $teamId, string $field): void
    {
        $statuses = DB::table('model_has_roles')
            ->join('users', 'users.id', '=', 'model_has_roles.model_id')
            ->where('model_has_roles.role_id', $this->templateId())
            ->where('model_has_roles.model_type', $user->getMorphClass())
            ->where('model_has_roles.team_id', $teamId)
            ->whereNull('users.deleted_at')
            ->orderBy('users.id')
            ->lockForUpdate()
            ->pluck('users.status', 'users.id');

        if (! $this->anotherActiveRemains($statuses, $user)) {
            throw ValidationException::withMessages([
                $field => __('An organisation needs at least one active organisation admin.'),
            ]);
        }
    }

    /** @param  Collection<array-key, mixed>  $statuses  status per user id */
    private function anotherActiveRemains(Collection $statuses, User $user): bool
    {
        return $statuses->contains(
            fn (mixed $status, int|string $id): bool => (int) $id !== $user->id && $status === UserStatus::Active->value,
        );
    }

    private function templateId(): int
    {
        $id = RoleModel::query()
            ->whereNull('team_id')
            ->where('name', Role::OrganisationAdmin->value)
            ->where('guard_name', SyncPermissions::GUARD)
            ->value('id');

        return $id === null
            ? throw new LogicException('The organisation_admin template role is missing; run permissions:sync.')
            : (int) $id;
    }
}
```

Replace `app/Actions/Users/UpdateUserRoles.php` with:

```php
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace App\Actions\Users;

use App\Actions\Audit\RecordActivity;
use App\Authorization\LockoutGuard;
use App\Authorization\PermissionsTeam;
use App\Authorization\Role;
use App\Authorization\SyncPermissions;
use App\Enums\ActivityEvent;
use App\Models\User;
use Illuminate\Auth\Access\AuthorizationException;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Builder;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Collection;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Gate;
use Illuminate\Validation\ValidationException;
use LogicException;
use Spatie\Permission\Models\Role as RoleModel;

/**
 * The only way to change a user's organisation roles (§4.6). Accepts web-guard roles of the target's own
 * team plus the global organisation_admin template, matched by id (DEC-21 option A, FU2-4); the
 * super_admin badge, other teams' roles, other guards' roles and team roles named like a system role are
 * rejected, and non-super-admins only hand out roles whose permissions they hold (W1). Refuses removing
 * your own organisation admin role and demoting the last active organisation admin (W12). Records
 * user.roles_changed with the old and new role names when the set changes (§4.8).
 */
final readonly class UpdateUserRoles
{
    public function __construct(private LockoutGuard $lockoutGuard, private RecordActivity $recordActivity) {}

    /**
     * @param  list<int>  $roleIds
     *
     * @throws AuthorizationException
     * @throws ValidationException
     */
    public function handle(User $actor, User $target, array $roleIds): void
    {
        Gate::forUser($actor)->authorize('updateRoles', $target);

        $teamId = $target->organisation_id ?? throw new LogicException('updateRoles allows only users with an organisation.');
        $templateId = $this->templateId();
        $roles = $this->resolveRoles($teamId, $templateId, $roleIds);
        $keepsAdmin = $roles->contains(fn (RoleModel $role): bool => (int) $role->getKey() === $templateId);

        PermissionsTeam::run($teamId, function () use ($actor, $target, $roles, $keepsAdmin, $teamId, $templateId): void {
            DB::transaction(function () use ($actor, $target, $roles, $keepsAdmin, $teamId, $templateId): void {
                $target->unsetRelation('roles');
                $before = $this->roleNamesOf($target, $teamId);
                $this->guardEscalation($actor, $target, $roles);

                if (! $keepsAdmin && $this->holdsTemplate($target, $teamId, $templateId)) {
                    $this->guardAdminRemoval($actor, $target, $teamId);
                }

                $target->syncRoles($roles);
                $target->unsetRelation('roles');

                $after = $roles->map(fn (RoleModel $role): string => $role->name)->values()->all();
                sort($after);

                if ($before !== $after) {
                    $this->recordActivity->handle(
                        ActivityEvent::UserRolesChanged,
                        $target,
                        changes: ['old' => ['roles' => $before], 'attributes' => ['roles' => $after]],
                        causer: $actor,
                    );
                }
            });
        });
    }

    /**
     * @param  list<int>  $roleIds
     * @return Collection<int, RoleModel>
     *
     * @throws ValidationException
     */
    private function resolveRoles(int $teamId, int $templateId, array $roleIds): Collection
    {
        $roleIds = array_values(array_unique($roleIds));

        $roles = RoleModel::query()
            ->whereKey($roleIds)
            ->where('guard_name', SyncPermissions::GUARD)
            ->where(function (Builder $query) use ($teamId, $templateId): void {
                $query->where('team_id', $teamId)->orWhere('id', $templateId);
            })
            ->get();

        // A team role that reads like a system role would pass for it in lists and checks (FU2-4, W6).
        $lookalike = $roles->contains(
            fn (RoleModel $role): bool => (int) $role->getKey() !== $templateId && Role::isReservedName($role->name),
        );

        if ($lookalike || $roles->count() !== count($roleIds)) {
            throw ValidationException::withMessages([
                'roles' => __('One or more roles are not available for this organisation.'),
            ]);
        }

        return $roles;
    }

    /**
     * Non-super-admins may only give or take away roles whose permissions they hold themselves,
     * so roles.assign alone never leads to organisation admin (W1).
     *
     * @param  Collection<int, RoleModel>  $roles
     *
     * @throws ValidationException
     */
    private function guardEscalation(User $actor, User $target, Collection $roles): void
    {
        if ($actor->isSuperAdmin()) {
            return;
        }

        $currentIds = $target->roles()->pluck('roles.id')->map(fn (mixed $id): int => (int) $id)->all();
        $newIds = $roles->map(fn (RoleModel $role): int => (int) $role->getKey())->all();
        $changedIds = array_values(array_unique([...array_diff($newIds, $currentIds), ...array_diff($currentIds, $newIds)]));

        $actor->unsetRelation('roles');

        foreach (RoleModel::query()->whereKey($changedIds)->with('permissions')->get() as $role) {
            foreach ($role->permissions as $permission) {
                if (! $actor->checkPermissionTo($permission->name)) {
                    throw ValidationException::withMessages([
                        'roles' => __('You can only give or take away roles whose permissions you have yourself.'),
                    ]);
                }
            }
        }
    }

    /** @throws ValidationException */
    private function guardAdminRemoval(User $actor, User $target, int $teamId): void
    {
        if ($actor->is($target)) {
            throw ValidationException::withMessages([
                'roles' => __('You cannot remove your own organisation admin role.'),
            ]);
        }

        $this->lockoutGuard->ensureAnotherActiveOrganisationAdmin($target, $teamId, 'roles');
    }

    /** The template by id, in this team: a team role that merely shares its name does not count (FU2-4). */
    private function holdsTemplate(User $target, int $teamId, int $templateId): bool
    {
        return DB::table('model_has_roles')
            ->where('role_id', $templateId)
            ->where('model_type', $target->getMorphClass())
            ->where('model_id', $target->id)
            ->where('team_id', $teamId)
            ->exists();
    }

    /** @return list<string> sorted in PHP, so both databases give the same order */
    private function roleNamesOf(User $target, int $teamId): array
    {
        $names = DB::table('model_has_roles')
            ->join('roles', 'roles.id', '=', 'model_has_roles.role_id')
            ->where('model_has_roles.model_type', $target->getMorphClass())
            ->where('model_has_roles.model_id', $target->id)
            ->where('model_has_roles.team_id', $teamId)
            ->pluck('roles.name')
            ->map(fn (mixed $name): string => (string) $name)
            ->values()
            ->all();
        sort($names);

        return $names;
    }

    private function templateId(): int
    {
        $id = RoleModel::query()
            ->whereNull('team_id')
            ->where('name', Role::OrganisationAdmin->value)
            ->where('guard_name', SyncPermissions::GUARD)
            ->value('id');

        return $id === null
            ? throw new LogicException('The organisation_admin template role is missing; run permissions:sync.')
            : (int) $id;
    }
}
```

- [ ] **Step 6: Decide `SetSuperAdmin` on the stored row and audit it**

Replace `app/Authorization/SetSuperAdmin.php` with:

```php
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace App\Authorization;

use App\Actions\Audit\RecordActivity;
use App\Enums\ActivityEvent;
use App\Models\Organisation;
use App\Models\User;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;
use Illuminate\Validation\ValidationException;

/**
 * The only writer of users.is_super_admin (§6.3). Sets the flag and attaches or detaches the super_admin
 * badge (null team) in one transaction; the badge is synced on every call, also when the flag was already
 * set. It decides on the stored flag, read after its locks, never on a possibly stale model (FU2-5). It
 * never removes the last active, non-deleted super admin (LockoutGuard), nor demotes a super admin who has
 * no organisation (W8) or whose organisation is archived (FU3-4). Records user.super_admin_granted /
 * user.super_admin_revoked when the flag changes (§4.8). Authorization is the caller's job (policy ability
 * updateSuperAdmin); console commands and seeders call it directly, so their entries have no causer.
 */
final readonly class SetSuperAdmin
{
    public function __construct(private LockoutGuard $lockoutGuard, private RecordActivity $recordActivity) {}

    /** @throws ValidationException */
    public function handle(User $user, bool $isSuperAdmin): void
    {
        DB::transaction(function () use ($user, $isSuperAdmin): void {
            if ($isSuperAdmin) {
                // Serialises concurrent promotions of the same user, so the grant is recorded once.
                DB::table('users')->where('id', $user->id)->lockForUpdate()->value('id');
            } elseif ($this->storedFlag($user)) {
                // The lock-out guard locks every super admin row, this one included, in id order (RL-27).
                $this->guardDemotion($user);
            }

            $wasSuperAdmin = $this->storedFlag($user);

            // Align the model with the stored row first, so the save writes only a real change.
            $user->forceFill(['is_super_admin' => $wasSuperAdmin])->syncOriginalAttribute('is_super_admin');
            $user->forceFill(['is_super_admin' => $isSuperAdmin])->save();

            PermissionsTeam::run(null, function () use ($user, $isSuperAdmin): void {
                $user->unsetRelation('roles');

                if ($isSuperAdmin) {
                    $user->assignRole(Role::SuperAdmin->value);
                } else {
                    $user->removeRole(Role::SuperAdmin->value);
                }

                $user->unsetRelation('roles');
            });

            if ($wasSuperAdmin !== $isSuperAdmin) {
                $this->recordActivity->handle(
                    $isSuperAdmin ? ActivityEvent::SuperAdminGranted : ActivityEvent::SuperAdminRevoked,
                    $user,
                );
            }
        });
    }

    private function storedFlag(User $user): bool
    {
        return (bool) DB::table('users')->where('id', $user->id)->value('is_super_admin');
    }

    /** @throws ValidationException */
    private function guardDemotion(User $user): void
    {
        $organisationId = DB::table('users')->where('id', $user->id)->value('organisation_id');

        // A user without an organisation must stay a super admin: a regular user needs one (W8).
        if ($organisationId === null) {
            throw ValidationException::withMessages([
                'is_super_admin' => __('Assign an organisation before removing super admin.'),
            ]);
        }

        // An archived organisation has no host to come home to (FU3-4): restore it first.
        if (Organisation::onlyTrashed()->whereKey($organisationId)->exists()) {
            throw ValidationException::withMessages([
                'is_super_admin' => __('Restore the organisation before removing super admin.'),
            ]);
        }

        $this->lockoutGuard->ensureAnotherActiveSuperAdmin($user, 'is_super_admin');
    }
}
```

`app/Observers/UserActivityObserver.php`:

```php
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace App\Observers;

use App\Actions\Audit\RecordActivity;
use App\Enums\ActivityEvent;
use App\Models\User;

/**
 * Records user.updated with old and new values when a user's name or email address changes (§4.4, §4.8,
 * RL-6), whoever saved it: the admin edit page, the profile page or the email-change link. Passwords,
 * remember tokens and two-factor columns are never recorded; status, roles, super admin, deletion and
 * restore have their own events. A quiet save records nothing, for writers that record their own event.
 */
final readonly class UserActivityObserver
{
    private const array AUDITED = ['name', 'email'];

    public function __construct(private RecordActivity $recordActivity) {}

    /** During "updated" the original still holds the old values; it is synced after "saved". */
    public function updated(User $user): void
    {
        $old = [];
        $new = [];

        foreach (self::AUDITED as $field) {
            if ($user->wasChanged($field)) {
                $old[$field] = $user->getOriginal($field);
                $new[$field] = $user->getAttribute($field);
            }
        }

        if ($new === []) {
            return;
        }

        $this->recordActivity->handle(ActivityEvent::UserUpdated, $user, changes: ['old' => $old, 'attributes' => $new]);
    }
}
```

```php
#[ObservedBy(UserActivityObserver::class)]
```

### Task 4: Effective permissions and the permission-subset rule

**Covers:** USR-11 (policy), USR-15, DEC26-11, DEC26-12, FU2-11, ORG-13, X6, RL-26, RK-B2, RK-I6, RK-D5.

What this task delivers, in full: a non-super-admin may update, enable/disable, delete or restore another user **only when every permission the target holds in the target's organisation is also held by the actor** (the permission-subset rule). "Holds" means the permissions of the roles assigned to the user with that organisation's team id (the global `organisation_admin` template role included) plus the user's direct permissions with that team id. The sets are read with two explicit queries over Spatie's tables (`model_has_roles ⨝ role_has_permissions ⨝ permissions` and `model_has_permissions ⨝ permissions`), never through Spatie relations or `getAllPermissions()` (those lazy-load and break strict mode on a collection) and never from the permission cache. Equal sets pass, so two organisation admins still manage each other; a "helpdesk" role holding `users.update` + `users.delete` can no longer touch an organisation admin. The decision logic lives once, in `App\Authorization\UserAbilities`; `UserPolicy` asks it for one target and the users index (Task 8) asks it for a page of users with one batch load. A new `restore` ability = `users.delete` + same organisation + the subset rule; super admins pass it through `Gate::before` (it is deliberately **not** added to `SuperAdminGate::ALWAYS_CHECKED`; `RestoreUser` in Task 6 applies the domain guards). `view` and `updateRoles` keep their behaviour (`UpdateUserRoles` already applies the same principle to roles). Super admins still manage everyone but never disable or delete themselves (`delete` and `updateStatus` stay always-checked). Users without an organisation (a state only reachable by hand) are refused every target-bound user ability (view, update, updateStatus, delete, restore, updateRoles, updateSuperAdmin); `viewAny` stays permission-only (FU2-11).

**Files:**
- Create: `app/Authorization/EffectivePermissions.php`, `app/Authorization/UserAbilities.php`
- Modify: `app/Policies/UserPolicy.php`
- Test: `tests/Feature/Authorization/EffectivePermissionsTest.php` (new), `tests/Feature/Authorization/UserPolicyTest.php` (added cases)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `App\Authorization\Role::OrganisationAdmin` (template role name; the template row has `team_id` NULL and is attached per team with `model_has_roles.team_id` = the organisation id), `App\Authorization\SyncPermissions::GUARD` (`'web'`), Spatie tables `model_has_roles`, `role_has_permissions`, `model_has_permissions`, `permissions`, `roles`; `SuperAdminGate::before` (super admins pass every ability except `impersonate`, `delete`, `forceDelete`, `updateStatus`, `updateRoles`, `updateSuperAdmin`).
- Produces:
  - `App\Authorization\EffectivePermissions` (final): `of(User $user, int $teamId): list<string>`; `forUsers(list<int> $userIds, int $teamId): array<int, list<string>>` (two queries for any number of users; every requested id is a key, names sorted and unique; `[]` without a query for an empty list); `holdsTemplate(list<int> $userIds, int $teamId): list<int>` (ids holding the template role **by role id** in that team, ascending).
  - `App\Authorization\UserAbilities` (final readonly, container-resolved, constructor `__construct(private EffectivePermissions $permissions)`): `covers(list<string> $actorPermissions, list<string> $targetPermissions): bool`; `forTarget(User $actor, User $target): array{view: bool, update: bool, updateStatus: bool, delete: bool, restore: bool}`; `forPage(User $actor, Illuminate\Support\Collection<int, User> $users): array<int, array{view: bool, update: bool, updateStatus: bool, delete: bool, restore: bool}>` (keyed by user id; one batch load of the sets). Task 19 adds the `impersonate` key and `mayImpersonate(User $actor, User $target): bool`.
  - `App\Policies\UserPolicy` (final readonly, constructor `__construct(private UserAbilities $abilities)`): `view`, `update`, `updateStatus`, `delete` and the new `restore(User $actor, User $target): bool` return `UserAbilities::forTarget()[ability]`; `viewAny`, `updateRoles`, `updateSuperAdmin` unchanged in behaviour.

```php
        ->and($permissions->of($editor, $organisation->id))->toBe([Permission::RolesAssign->value, Permission::UsersUpdate->value, Permission::UsersView->value])
        ->and($permissions->of($plain, $organisation->id))->toBe([])
        ->and($permissions->holdsTemplate([$admin->id, $editor->id, $plain->id], $organisation->id))->toBe([$admin->id]);
});

it('ignores assignments of another team and the super admin badge', function () use ($roleIn, $assign): void {
    $own = Organisation::factory()->create();
    $other = Organisation::factory()->create();
    $user = User::factory()->for($own)->create();
    $assign($user, $roleIn($other, 'foreign', Permission::UsersDelete), $other->id);
    withPermissionsTeam(null, fn (): User => $user->givePermissionTo(Permission::ActivityLogView->value));
    app(SetSuperAdmin::class)->handle($user, true);
    $permissions = app(EffectivePermissions::class);

    expect($permissions->of($user, $own->id))->toBe([])
        ->and($permissions->of($user, $other->id))->toBe([Permission::UsersDelete->value])
        ->and($permissions->holdsTemplate([$user->id], $own->id))->toBe([]);

it('loads a page of users with a fixed number of queries and matches of()', function () use ($roleIn, $assign): void {
    $organisation = Organisation::factory()->create();
    $editor = $roleIn($organisation, 'editor', Permission::UsersView, Permission::UsersUpdate);
    $users = User::factory()->for($organisation)->count(6)->create();

    foreach ($users->values() as $index => $user) {
        if ($index % 2 === 0) {
            $assign($user, $editor, $organisation->id);
        } else {
            withPermissionsTeam($organisation->id, fn (): User => $user->givePermissionTo(Permission::RolesView->value));
        }
    }

    $ids = array_values($users->map(fn (User $user): int => $user->id)->all());
    $permissions = app(EffectivePermissions::class);

    DB::enableQueryLog();
    $sets = $permissions->forUsers($ids, $organisation->id);
    $pageQueries = count(DB::getQueryLog());
    DB::flushQueryLog();
    $permissions->forUsers([$ids[0]], $organisation->id);
    $singleQueries = count(DB::getQueryLog());
    DB::disableQueryLog();

    expect($pageQueries)->toBe(2)
        ->and($singleQueries)->toBe(2)
        ->and(array_keys($sets))->toBe($ids)
        ->and($permissions->forUsers([], $organisation->id))->toBe([]);

    foreach ($users as $user) {
        expect($sets[$user->id])->toBe($permissions->of($user, $organisation->id));
    }
});

it('reads no Spatie relation, so a collection raises no lazy-loading violation (RK-I6)', function () use ($roleIn, $assign): void {
    $organisation = Organisation::factory()->create();
    $editor = $roleIn($organisation, 'editor', Permission::UsersView);

    foreach (User::factory()->for($organisation)->count(3)->create() as $member) {
        $assign($member, $editor, $organisation->id);
    }

    $admin = asOrgAdmin($organisation);
    $users = User::query()->where('organisation_id', $organisation->id)->get();

    expect(fn (): mixed => $users->first()?->roles)->toThrow(LazyLoadingViolationException::class);

    $abilities = app(UserAbilities::class)->forPage($admin, $users);

    foreach ($users as $user) {
        expect(Gate::forUser($admin)->allows('update', $user))->toBe($abilities[$user->id]['update']);
    }

    expect($abilities)->toHaveCount(4);
});
```

Replace `tests/Feature/Authorization/UserPolicyTest.php` with the version below. The seven existing tests are unchanged; new are the imports, the three file-local closures (no new global helper) and the five tests at the end. Every new test runs over both paths, the policy and the page batch (dataset `['policy', 'page']`), so the two can never disagree. The page path keeps only the five abilities of this task, so Task 19's extra `impersonate` key does not break these expectations.

```php
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

/** covers §4.4, §4.6 */

use App\Authorization\Permission;
use App\Authorization\PermissionsTeam;
use App\Authorization\Role;
use App\Authorization\SetSuperAdmin;
use App\Authorization\UserAbilities;
use App\Models\Organisation;
use App\Models\User;
use Illuminate\Support\Arr;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Gate;
use Spatie\Permission\Models\Role as RoleModel;

/** @return array{organisation: Organisation, admin: User, member: User, outsider: User, superAdmin: User, otherSuperAdmin: User} */
function userPolicyCast(): array
{
    $organisation = Organisation::factory()->create();
    $outsider = User::factory()->create();
    $superAdmin = asSuperAdmin();
    $otherSuperAdmin = User::factory()->superAdmin()->create();
    $member = User::factory()->for($organisation)->create();
    $admin = asOrgAdmin($organisation);

    return ['organisation' => $organisation, 'admin' => $admin, 'member' => $member, 'outsider' => $outsider, 'superAdmin' => $superAdmin, 'otherSuperAdmin' => $otherSuperAdmin];
}

/** A user of the organisation holding one custom team role with these permissions. */
$memberWithRole = function (Organisation $organisation, string $role, Permission ...$permissions): User {
    $teamRole = RoleModel::query()->create(['name' => $role, 'guard_name' => 'web', 'team_id' => $organisation->id]);
    $teamRole->givePermissionTo(array_map(fn (Permission $permission): string => $permission->value, $permissions));
    $user = User::factory()->for($organisation)->create();
    withPermissionsTeam($organisation->id, fn (): User => $user->assignRole($teamRole));
    $user->unsetRelation('roles');

    return $user;
};

$adminOf = function (Organisation $organisation): User {
    $user = User::factory()->for($organisation)->create();
    withPermissionsTeam($organisation->id, fn (): User => $user->assignRole(Role::OrganisationAdmin->value));
    $user->unsetRelation('roles');

    return $user;
};

/**
 * The five user-management abilities, through the policy or through the batch evaluation an index
 * page uses (RL-26). Later abilities of the page rows (impersonate) are left out on purpose.
 *
 * @return array<string, bool>
 */
$abilitiesOf = function (string $path, User $actor, User $target): array {
    if ($path === 'page') {
        return Arr::only(
            app(UserAbilities::class)->forPage($actor, collect([$target]))[$target->id],
            ['view', 'update', 'updateStatus', 'delete', 'restore'],
        );
    }

    $gate = Gate::forUser($actor);

    return [
        'view' => $gate->allows('view', $target),
        'update' => $gate->allows('update', $target),
        'updateStatus' => $gate->allows('updateStatus', $target),
        'delete' => $gate->allows('delete', $target),
        'restore' => $gate->allows('restore', $target),
    ];
};

it('lets an organisation admin manage members of their own organisation', function (): void {
    ['admin' => $admin, 'member' => $member] = userPolicyCast();
    $gate = Gate::forUser($admin);

    expect($gate->allows('viewAny', User::class))->toBeTrue()
        ->and($gate->allows('view', $member))->toBeTrue()
        ->and($gate->allows('update', $member))->toBeTrue()
        ->and($gate->allows('updateStatus', $member))->toBeTrue()
        ->and($gate->allows('updateRoles', $member))->toBeTrue()
        ->and($gate->allows('delete', $member))->toBeTrue();
});

it('keeps an organisation admin out of other organisations and away from super admins', function (): void {
    ['admin' => $admin, 'outsider' => $outsider, 'superAdmin' => $superAdmin] = userPolicyCast();
    $gate = Gate::forUser($admin);

    foreach (['view', 'update', 'updateStatus', 'updateRoles', 'delete'] as $ability) {
        expect($gate->allows($ability, $outsider))->toBeFalse("{$ability} outsider")
            ->and($gate->allows($ability, $superAdmin))->toBeFalse("{$ability} super admin");
    }

    expect($gate->allows('updateSuperAdmin', $outsider))->toBeFalse();
});

it('stops users from deleting or disabling themselves, super admins included (W2, W12)', function (): void {
    ['admin' => $admin, 'superAdmin' => $superAdmin] = userPolicyCast();

    expect(Gate::forUser($admin)->allows('delete', $admin))->toBeFalse()
        ->and(Gate::forUser($admin)->allows('updateStatus', $admin))->toBeFalse()
        ->and(Gate::forUser($superAdmin)->allows('delete', $superAdmin))->toBeFalse()
        ->and(Gate::forUser($superAdmin)->allows('updateStatus', $superAdmin))->toBeFalse()
        ->and(Gate::forUser($superAdmin)->allows('updateSuperAdmin', $superAdmin))->toBeFalse();
});

it('keeps organisation admins away from a super admin of their own organisation', function (): void {
    $organisation = Organisation::factory()->create();
    $promoted = User::factory()->for($organisation)->create();

it('lets super admins manage everyone else', function (): void {

        ->and($gate->allows('delete', $outsider))->toBeTrue()
        ->and($gate->allows('delete', $other))->toBeTrue()
        ->and($gate->allows('updateRoles', $outsider))->toBeTrue()
        ->and($gate->allows('updateSuperAdmin', $outsider))->toBeTrue();
});

it('never assigns organisation roles to super admins', function (): void {
    ['superAdmin' => $superAdmin, 'otherSuperAdmin' => $other] = userPolicyCast();

    expect(Gate::forUser($superAdmin)->allows('updateRoles', $other))->toBeFalse();
});

it('gives members without permissions nothing', function (): void {

    $member = asMember($organisation);
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Add the effective permission sets**

`app/Authorization/EffectivePermissions.php`:

```php
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace App\Authorization;

use App\Models\User;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;

/**
 * The permissions users hold in one team (RL-26): the permissions of the roles assigned with that
 * team id (the organisation_admin template included) plus the direct permissions of that team.
 * Read with explicit queries, never through Spatie relations or its cache, so a page of users costs
 * two queries and no model lazy-loads anything (RK-I6). The super_admin badge (null team) adds nothing.
 */
final class EffectivePermissions
{
    /** @return list<string> */
    public function of(User $user, int $teamId): array
    {
        return $this->forUsers([$user->id], $teamId)[$user->id] ?? [];
    }

    /**
     * @param  list<int>  $userIds
     * @return array<int, list<string>> sorted permission names per user id; every id is a key
     */
    public function forUsers(array $userIds, int $teamId): array
    {
        $userIds = array_values(array_unique($userIds));

        if ($userIds === []) {
            return [];
        }

        $morphClass = new User()->getMorphClass();

        $viaRoles = DB::table('model_has_roles')
            ->join('role_has_permissions', 'role_has_permissions.role_id', '=', 'model_has_roles.role_id')
            ->join('permissions', 'permissions.id', '=', 'role_has_permissions.permission_id')
            ->where('model_has_roles.model_type', $morphClass)
            ->whereIn('model_has_roles.model_id', $userIds)
            ->where('model_has_roles.team_id', $teamId)
            ->where('permissions.guard_name', SyncPermissions::GUARD)
            ->get(['model_has_roles.model_id as user_id', 'permissions.name as name']);

        $direct = DB::table('model_has_permissions')
            ->join('permissions', 'permissions.id', '=', 'model_has_permissions.permission_id')
            ->where('model_has_permissions.model_type', $morphClass)
            ->whereIn('model_has_permissions.model_id', $userIds)
            ->where('model_has_permissions.team_id', $teamId)
            ->where('permissions.guard_name', SyncPermissions::GUARD)
            ->get(['model_has_permissions.model_id as user_id', 'permissions.name as name']);

        $names = [];

        foreach ($viaRoles->concat($direct) as $row) {
            $names[(int) $row->user_id][] = (string) $row->name;
        }

        $sets = [];

        foreach ($userIds as $userId) {
            $set = array_values(array_unique($names[$userId] ?? []));
            sort($set);
            $sets[$userId] = $set;
        }

        return $sets;
    }

    /**
     * The users among $userIds that hold the organisation_admin template in this team, by role id
     * (a team role that is merely named like it never counts, FU2-4).
     *
     * @param  list<int>  $userIds
     * @return list<int>
     */
    public function holdsTemplate(array $userIds, int $teamId): array
    {
        if ($userIds === []) {
            return [];
        }

        return array_values(DB::table('model_has_roles')
            ->join('roles', 'roles.id', '=', 'model_has_roles.role_id')
            ->whereNull('roles.team_id')
            ->where('roles.name', Role::OrganisationAdmin->value)
            ->where('roles.guard_name', SyncPermissions::GUARD)
            ->where('model_has_roles.model_type', new User()->getMorphClass())
            ->where('model_has_roles.team_id', $teamId)
            ->whereIn('model_has_roles.model_id', $userIds)
            ->orderBy('model_has_roles.model_id')
            ->pluck('model_has_roles.model_id')
            ->map(fn (mixed $id): int => (int) $id)
            ->unique()
            ->all());
    }
}
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Add the shared decisions**

`app/Authorization/UserAbilities.php`:

```php
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace App\Authorization;

use App\Models\User;
use Illuminate\Support\Collection;

/**
 * The user-management decisions (§4.4, RL-26), held once: UserPolicy asks for one target, index
 * pages for a page of users with one batch load. Super admins manage everyone but never disable or
 * delete themselves (W2). Other actors need the permission, the same organisation, a target that is
 * not a super admin and, for every write, a target whose effective permissions in that team are a
 * subset of their own, so a helpdesk role with users.update cannot touch an organisation admin.
 * Equal sets pass: organisation admins still manage each other (W12 guards the last one).
 */
final readonly class UserAbilities
{
    public function __construct(private EffectivePermissions $permissions) {}

    /**
     * @param  list<string>  $actorPermissions
     * @param  list<string>  $targetPermissions
     */
    public function covers(array $actorPermissions, array $targetPermissions): bool
    {
        return array_diff($targetPermissions, $actorPermissions) === [];
    }

    /** @return array{view: bool, update: bool, updateStatus: bool, delete: bool, restore: bool} */
    public function forTarget(User $actor, User $target): array
    {
        return $this->forPage($actor, collect([$target]))[$target->id];
    }

    /**
     * @param  Collection<int, User>  $users
     * @return array<int, array{view: bool, update: bool, updateStatus: bool, delete: bool, restore: bool}>
     */
    public function forPage(User $actor, Collection $users): array
    {
        if ($actor->isSuperAdmin()) {
            return $users->mapWithKeys(fn (User $user): array => [$user->id => [
                'view' => true,
                'update' => true,
                'updateStatus' => $actor->isNot($user),
                'delete' => $actor->isNot($user),
                'restore' => true,
            ]])->all();
        }

        $managed = $users->filter(fn (User $user): bool => $this->manages($actor, $user));
        $sets = $actor->organisation_id === null || $managed->isEmpty()
            ? []
            : $this->permissions->forUsers([$actor->id, ...array_values($managed->map(fn (User $user): int => $user->id)->all())], $actor->organisation_id);
        $actorPermissions = $sets[$actor->id] ?? [];

        $mayView = $actor->can(Permission::UsersView);
        $mayUpdate = $actor->can(Permission::UsersUpdate);
        $mayDelete = $actor->can(Permission::UsersDelete);

        $abilities = [];

        foreach ($users as $user) {
            $manages = $this->manages($actor, $user);
            $covered = $manages && $this->covers($actorPermissions, $sets[$user->id] ?? []);
            $isSelf = $actor->is($user);

            $abilities[$user->id] = [
                'view' => $mayView && $manages,
                'update' => $mayUpdate && $covered,
                'updateStatus' => $mayUpdate && $covered && ! $isSelf,
                'delete' => $mayDelete && $covered && ! $isSelf,
                'restore' => $mayDelete && $covered,
            ];
        }

        return $abilities;
    }

    /** Organisation members never act on super admins, even promoted ones that keep an organisation_id (§6.3). */
    private function manages(User $actor, User $target): bool
    {
        return ! $target->isSuperAdmin()
            && $actor->organisation_id !== null
            && $actor->organisation_id === $target->organisation_id;
    }
}
```

`$actor->can()` reads the actor's own Spatie relations once per call; pass the authenticated user (a single model), never a row of the page, so strict mode's lazy-loading check is not triggered.

- [ ] **Step 5: Let the policy delegate to `UserAbilities`**

Replace `app/Policies/UserPolicy.php` with:

```php
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace App\Policies;

use App\Authorization\Permission;
use App\Authorization\UserAbilities;
use App\Models\User;

/**
 * §4.4, §4.6. view, update, updateStatus, delete and restore are decided by UserAbilities, the same
 * code the users index evaluates for a page (RL-26). restore is not always-checked: super admins pass
 * Gate::before and RestoreUser applies the domain guards (archived organisation, taken address).
 */
final readonly class UserPolicy
{
    public function __construct(private UserAbilities $abilities) {}

    public function viewAny(User $actor): bool
    {
        return $actor->can(Permission::UsersView);
    }

    public function view(User $actor, User $target): bool
    {
        return $this->abilities->forTarget($actor, $target)['view'];
    }

    public function update(User $actor, User $target): bool
    {
        return $this->abilities->forTarget($actor, $target)['update'];
    }

    /** Always checked: nobody deletes themselves, super admins included (W2). */
    public function delete(User $actor, User $target): bool
    {
        return $this->abilities->forTarget($actor, $target)['delete'];
    }

    /** Always checked: nobody disables themselves (W12). */
    public function updateStatus(User $actor, User $target): bool
    {
        return $this->abilities->forTarget($actor, $target)['updateStatus'];
    }

    /** users.delete + same organisation + the permission-subset rule (DEC-26 (11)). */
    public function restore(User $actor, User $target): bool
    {
        return $this->abilities->forTarget($actor, $target)['restore'];
    }

    /** Always checked: roles belong to an organisation; super admins carry only the badge (W1). */
    public function updateRoles(User $actor, User $target): bool
    {
        if ($target->isSuperAdmin() || $target->organisation_id === null) {
            return false;
        }

        if ($actor->isSuperAdmin()) {
            return true;
        }

        return $actor->can(Permission::RolesAssign)
            && $actor->organisation_id !== null
            && $actor->organisation_id === $target->organisation_id;
    }

    /** Always checked: only another super admin changes the flag (§6.3). */
    public function updateSuperAdmin(User $actor, User $target): bool
    {
        return $actor->isSuperAdmin() && $actor->isNot($target);
    }
}
```

Policies are resolved through the container, so the constructor dependency needs no registration (policy auto-discovery maps `App\Models\User` to it as before).

### Task 5: `UpdateUser` and one address-availability rule (W9)

**Covers:** USR-12 (action), USR-14, USR-21, INV-19 (rule), W9, X2, FU3-7, FU3-8, D-14, RL-14, RL-16 (email edit), E1 (kept closed), CV-1, RK-B2, OR-I3, CV-a.

What this task delivers, in full:
- **One address rule** `App\Rules\AvailableEmail` for the admin edit, restoring a user (Task 6), inviting (Task 11) and the profile email change. Soft-deleted users never block an address. When the holder is a super admin or belongs to another organisation the message is the generic "This address can't be used." (no cross-organisation enumeration); inside the organisation being edited it names the conflict: "This address already has an open invitation." when the holder's status is `pending_activation` (decided from the status, not from an `invitations` lookup, so it also covers hand-set pending users), otherwise "This address is already used in this organisation.". The rule reads `users` with `DB::table()` on purpose: it must see every organisation whatever tenant is bound (the generic message is an accepted existence oracle until M7's rate limits, RL-30).
- `ProfileValidationRules::emailRules()` uses the rule instead of `Rule::unique(...)->withoutTrashed()`; the profile page, `RequestEmailChange` and `ConfirmEmailChange` pass the user's organisation.
- **`App\Actions\Users\UpdateUser`**: an administrator renames a user and changes their address. It authorises `update` (so Task 4's subset rule applies), trims and lower-cases, refuses changing **your own** address here (that goes through the signed link on the profile page, E1 stays closed) and refuses changing a **pending** user's address (cancel the invitation and invite the new address instead); names stay editable in both cases. A changed address applies at once, deletes the old address's `password_reset_tokens`, forgets the pending self-service change (`RequestEmailChange::cacheKey()`, so an older confirmation link can no longer move the address, FU3-7) and mails the old address an `EmailChangedByAdministrator` notice after commit (D-14). A unique-index race between validation and save becomes a validation error, also in `ConfirmEmailChange` (FU3-8). `UpdateUser` logs nothing itself: `UserActivityObserver` (Task 3) records `user.updated`.
- The fresh password confirmation before changing another user's address (RL-18) and the read-only fields belong to the page (Task 9), not to this action.

**Files:**
- Create: `app/Rules/AvailableEmail.php`, `app/Actions/Users/UpdateUser.php`, `app/Notifications/EmailChangedByAdministrator.php`
- Modify: `app/Concerns/ProfileValidationRules.php`, `app/Actions/Settings/RequestEmailChange.php`, `app/Actions/Settings/ConfirmEmailChange.php`, `resources/views/pages/settings/profile/profile.php` (passes the organisation id), `lang/nl.json`, `lang/en.json`
- Test: `tests/Feature/Users/UpdateUserTest.php` (new); update `tests/Feature/Settings/ProfileUpdateTest.php`, `tests/Feature/Settings/EmailChangeTest.php`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `UserPolicy::update` (Task 4, subset rule), `RequestEmailChange::cacheKey(User $user): string`, `UserActivityObserver` (Task 3, records `user.updated` on any name/email save), `UserStatus::PendingActivation`, test helper `confirmationLinkFor(string $address): string` (exists, needs `Notification::fake()`).
- Produces:
  - `App\Rules\AvailableEmail implements Illuminate\Contracts\Validation\ValidationRule` (final readonly): `__construct(public ?int $organisationId, public ?int $ignoreUserId = null)`; `validate(string $attribute, mixed $value, Closure $fail): void`. Messages: `__('This address already has an open invitation.')`, `__('This address is already used in this organisation.')`, `__('This address can\'t be used.')`.
  - `ProfileValidationRules::profileRules(?int $userId = null, ?int $organisationId = null): array` and `ProfileValidationRules::emailRules(?int $userId = null, ?int $organisationId = null): array` — `['required', 'string', 'email', 'lowercase', 'max:255', new AvailableEmail($organisationId, $userId)]` (both `protected`, trait methods).
  - `App\Actions\Users\UpdateUser::handle(User $actor, User $target, string $name, string $email): void` — `@throws AuthorizationException|ValidationException`; errors on `name` / `email`: `__('Change your own address on your profile page.')`, `__('Cancel the invitation and invite the new address.')`, the `AvailableEmail` messages, and `__('This address can\'t be used.')` for a lost race.
  - `App\Notifications\EmailChangedByAdministrator` (final, `ShouldQueue`, after commit): `__construct(public readonly string $newEmail)`; mail channel; routed on demand to the old address.

Create it with `php artisan make:rule AvailableEmail --no-interaction`, then replace the file with:

`app/Rules/AvailableEmail.php`:

```php
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace App\Rules;

use Closure;
use Illuminate\Contracts\Validation\ValidationRule;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;
use Illuminate\Support\Str;
use Illuminate\Translation\PotentiallyTranslatedString;

/**
 * One address rule for inviting, the admin edit, restoring a user and the profile email change
 * (§4.4, §4.5, W9, RL-14). Deleted users never block an address. Inside the organisation being
 * edited the message names the conflict; an address held in another organisation or by a super
 * admin gets one generic message, so the rule does not tell which organisation uses it. The query
 * reads the users table directly: the check must see every organisation, whatever tenant is bound.
 */
final readonly class AvailableEmail implements ValidationRule
{
    public function __construct(public ?int $organisationId, public ?int $ignoreUserId = null) {}

    /** @param  Closure(string, ?string=): PotentiallyTranslatedString  $fail */
    public function validate(string $attribute, mixed $value, Closure $fail): void
    {
        if (! is_string($value) || $value === '') {
            return;
        }

        $holders = DB::table('users')
            ->where('email', Str::lower($value))
            ->whereNull('deleted_at');

        if ($this->ignoreUserId !== null) {
            $holders->where('id', '!=', $this->ignoreUserId);
        }

        $holder = $holders->first(['organisation_id', 'is_super_admin', 'status']);

        if ($holder === null) {
            return;
        }

        $sameOrganisation = $this->organisationId !== null
            && ! (bool) $holder->is_super_admin
            && $holder->organisation_id !== null
            && (int) $holder->organisation_id === $this->organisationId;

        if (! $sameOrganisation) {
            $fail(__('This address can\'t be used.'));

            return;
        }

        $fail($holder->status === 'pending_activation'
            ? __('This address already has an open invitation.')
            : __('This address is already used in this organisation.'));
    }
}
```

`app/Concerns/ProfileValidationRules.php`:

```php
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace App\Concerns;

use App\Rules\AvailableEmail;
use Illuminate\Contracts\Validation\ValidationRule;
use Stringable;

trait ProfileValidationRules
{
    /**
     * Get the validation rules used to validate user profiles.
     *
     * @return array<string, array<int, ValidationRule|Stringable|array<mixed>|string>>
     */
    protected function profileRules(?int $userId = null, ?int $organisationId = null): array
    {
        return [
            'name' => $this->nameRules(),
            'email' => $this->emailRules($userId, $organisationId),
        ];
    }

    /**
     * Get the validation rules used to validate user names.
     *
     * @return array<int, ValidationRule|Stringable|array<mixed>|string>
     */
    protected function nameRules(): array
    {
        return ['required', 'string', 'max:255'];
    }

    /**
     * Get the validation rules used to validate user emails: lower case and available (W9). Pass the
     * organisation the address will be used in, so conflicts there get a specific message.
     *
     * @return array<int, ValidationRule|Stringable|array<mixed>|string>
     */
    protected function emailRules(?int $userId = null, ?int $organisationId = null): array
    {
        return [
            'required',
            'string',
            'email',
            'lowercase',
            'max:255',
            new AvailableEmail($organisationId, $userId),
        ];
    }
}
```

Replace `app/Actions/Settings/ConfirmEmailChange.php` with (new: the organisation id for the rule and the unique-race catch, FU3-8):

`app/Actions/Settings/ConfirmEmailChange.php`:

```php
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace App\Actions\Settings;

use App\Concerns\ProfileValidationRules;
use App\Models\User;
use Illuminate\Database\UniqueConstraintViolationException;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Cache;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Validator;
use Illuminate\Support\Str;
use Illuminate\Validation\ValidationException;

/**
 * Applies a confirmed email change (E1). Only the newest link works, and only once: the nonce is
 * forgotten when it matches, so an older link never removes the newest one.
 */
final class ConfirmEmailChange
{
    use ProfileValidationRules;

    /** @throws ValidationException */
    public function handle(User $user, string $email, string $nonce): void
    {
        $email = Str::lower($email);
        $key = RequestEmailChange::cacheKey($user);
        $expected = Cache::get($key);

        if (! is_string($expected) || ! hash_equals($expected, hash('sha256', $nonce.'|'.$email))) {
            throw ValidationException::withMessages(['email' => [__('This confirmation link is no longer valid.')]]);
        }

        Cache::forget($key);

        Validator::make(['email' => $email], ['email' => $this->emailRules($user->id, $user->organisation_id)])->validate();

        try {
            DB::transaction(function () use ($user, $email): void {
                $previous = $user->email;

                $user->forceFill(['email' => $email])->save();

                // Reset links issued for the old address must not work any more.
                DB::table('password_reset_tokens')->where('email', $previous)->delete();
            });
        } catch (UniqueConstraintViolationException) {
            // Another request took the address between validation and save (FU3-8).
            $user->refresh();

            throw ValidationException::withMessages(['email' => [__('This address can\'t be used.')]]);
        }
    }
}
```

The catch sits **outside** `DB::transaction()`: the transaction has rolled back to its savepoint by then, so PostgreSQL accepts the `refresh()` query (inside the transaction it would answer "current transaction is aborted").

`app/Notifications/EmailChangedByAdministrator.php`:

```php
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace App\Notifications;

use Illuminate\Bus\Queueable;
use Illuminate\Contracts\Queue\ShouldQueue;
use Illuminate\Notifications\Messages\MailMessage;
use Illuminate\Notifications\Notification;

/** Sent to the old address after an administrator changed it (§4.4, D-14); the M3 parity of EmailChangeRequested. */
final class EmailChangedByAdministrator extends Notification implements ShouldQueue
{
    use Queueable;

    public function __construct(public readonly string $newEmail)
    {
        $this->afterCommit();
    }

    /** @return list<string> */
    public function via(object $notifiable): array
    {
        return ['mail'];
    }

    public function toMail(object $notifiable): MailMessage
    {
        return new MailMessage()
            ->subject(__('An administrator changed your email address'))
            ->line(__('An administrator changed the email address of your account to :email.', ['email' => $this->newEmail]))
            ->line(__('From now on you sign in with that address.'))
            ->line(__('If you did not expect this, contact your administrator.'));
    }
}
```

```php
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace App\Actions\Users;

use App\Actions\Settings\RequestEmailChange;
use App\Concerns\ProfileValidationRules;
use App\Enums\UserStatus;
use App\Models\User;
use App\Notifications\EmailChangedByAdministrator;
use Illuminate\Auth\Access\AuthorizationException;
use Illuminate\Database\UniqueConstraintViolationException;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Cache;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Gate;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Notification;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Validator;
use Illuminate\Support\Str;
use Illuminate\Validation\ValidationException;

/**
 * The administrator's edit of a user's name and address (§4.4, USR-12). Needs the update ability,
 * so the permission-subset rule applies (RL-26). Addresses are stored in lower case and must be
 * available (W9). Your own address changes only through the signed self-service link on the
 * profile page (E1), and a pending user's address only by cancelling and re-inviting. A changed
 * address applies at once: the old address loses its reset links and any pending self-service
 * change link (FU3-7) and gets a notice after commit (D-14). user.updated is recorded by
 * UserActivityObserver, not here.
 */
final class UpdateUser
{
    use ProfileValidationRules;

    /**
     * @throws AuthorizationException
     * @throws ValidationException
     */
    public function handle(User $actor, User $target, string $name, string $email): void
    {
        Gate::forUser($actor)->authorize('update', $target);

        $name = trim($name);
        $email = Str::lower(trim($email));
        $previousEmail = $target->email;
        $changesEmail = $email !== $previousEmail;

        if ($changesEmail && $actor->is($target)) {
            throw ValidationException::withMessages(['email' => [__('Change your own address on your profile page.')]]);
        }

        if ($changesEmail && $target->status === UserStatus::PendingActivation) {
            throw ValidationException::withMessages(['email' => [__('Cancel the invitation and invite the new address.')]]);
        }

        Validator::make(['name' => $name, 'email' => $email], [
            'name' => $this->nameRules(),
            'email' => $this->emailRules($target->id, $target->organisation_id),
        ])->validate();

        try {
            DB::transaction(function () use ($target, $name, $email, $previousEmail, $changesEmail): void {
                $target->forceFill(['name' => $name, 'email' => $email])->save();

                if ($changesEmail) {
                    // Reset links issued for the old address must not work any more.
                    DB::table('password_reset_tokens')->where('email', $previousEmail)->delete();
                }
            });
        } catch (UniqueConstraintViolationException) {
            // Another request took the address between validation and save (FU3-8).
            $target->refresh();

            throw ValidationException::withMessages(['email' => [__('This address can\'t be used.')]]);
        }

        if (! $changesEmail) {
            return;
        }

        // A self-service link requested before this change must not move the address again (FU3-7).
        Cache::forget(RequestEmailChange::cacheKey($target));
        Notification::route('mail', $previousEmail)->notify(new EmailChangedByAdministrator($email));
    }
}
```

### Task 6: Status, delete and restore actions with lock-out guards (W2, W12)

**Covers:** USR-8 (action), USR-11 (action), USR-13, USR-14 (restore), USR-2 (`color()`), ROLE-15, DEC26-3, DEC26-10, DEC26-11, W2, W12, W4, FU2-5, RL-16, RL-28, C-9, RK-I7, OR-M4.

What this task delivers, in full:
- **`UpdateUserStatus`** (enable/disable). Authorises the always-checked `updateStatus` ability, so nobody changes their own status, super admins included. `pending_activation` is never set by hand, and a pending user's status never changes here (only accepting the invitation activates, W4). Disabling an active user never removes the last active super admin (when the target is a super admin) or the last active organisation admin of the target's team (when the target holds the template role, checked by role id), **whoever asks, super admins included** (W2, W12). The guards come from Task 3's `LockoutGuard`, which locks the whole candidate set in id order inside the transaction. Every decision (pending, no-op, whether to run the guards, whether the target is a super admin) is taken on the stored `users` row read as the first statement inside the transaction, never on the model the caller passed in, which may be stale (FU2-5, as `SetSuperAdmin` does since Task 3). Disabling ends the target's sessions and cycles `remember_token` through `Sessions::endFor()` (below) in the same transaction, so re-enabling never revives an old session or remember cookie (RL-28). A real change logs `user.status_changed` with old/new status; a no-op change logs nothing.
- **`DeleteUser`** (soft delete). Always-checked `delete`; refuses pending users ("Cancel the invitation instead."); deleting an **active** user applies the same two lock-out guards (a disabled user never counts as the remaining admin, so deleting one cannot lock anyone out); like `UpdateUserStatus` it decides on the stored row read first inside the transaction (an already deleted row is a no-op), so a stale "disabled" model of a user who is now the last active admin is still refused (FU2-5); ends the sessions and cycles the remember token (`Sessions::endFor()`); logs `user.deleted`.
- **`App\Tenancy\Auth\Sessions::endFor(list<int> $userIds)`**, the one place that cuts sessions on a lock-out (used here, and by Task 15's `ArchiveOrganisation` and `PurgeOrganisation`). A plain delete, run inside the caller's transaction: it deletes every `sessions` row whose `user_id` is one of the users (with the database session driver, the kit default, that signs them out on every device) and cycles their `remember_token` by setting it to null, so no "remember me" cookie matches any more (Laravel sets a new token at the next remember-me sign-in). No payload is decoded. Purge deletes nothing session-related beyond this; its deletion of the users' `password_reset_tokens` is a purge step of its own (Task 15). Impersonation does not exist yet: Task 20's `ImpersonationAwareSessionHandler` writes the impersonator's id into `sessions.user_id` during an impersonation, which alone keeps the impersonator's session out of a target's `endFor()`.
- **`RestoreUser`**. Authorises `restore` (Task 4: `users.delete` + same organisation + subset rule; super admins pass through `Gate::before`, which is why the domain guards live in the action and apply to super admins too): refused for a pending user (a cancelled invitation's soft-deleted user, C-9), while the user's organisation is archived, and when `AvailableEmail` (Task 5) says the address is in use again; a unique race becomes a validation error; logs `user.restored`.
- `UserStatus::color()` for the badges (`Active` lime, `PendingActivation` amber, `Disabled` zinc).
- Callers resolve trashed targets themselves (`withTrashed()` inside `HostScope::read()`, Task 8); the actions take models.

**Files:**
- Create: `app/Tenancy/Auth/Sessions.php`, `app/Actions/Users/UpdateUserStatus.php`, `app/Actions/Users/DeleteUser.php`, `app/Actions/Users/RestoreUser.php`
- Modify: `app/Enums/UserStatus.php` (`color()`), `lang/nl.json`, `lang/en.json`
- Test: `tests/Feature/Users/UserLifecycleTest.php` (new), `tests/Feature/Tenancy/SessionsTest.php` (new), `tests/Feature/Users/UserModelTest.php` (colour)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `UserPolicy::{updateStatus,delete}` (always checked) and `UserPolicy::restore` (Task 4); `EffectivePermissions::holdsTemplate(list<int> $userIds, int $teamId): list<int>` (Task 4); `App\Authorization\LockoutGuard::ensureAnotherActiveSuperAdmin(User $user, string $field): void` and `::ensureAnotherActiveOrganisationAdmin(User $user, int $teamId, string $field): void` (Task 3; throw `ValidationException` under `$field` with `__('At least one active super admin must remain.')` / `__('An organisation needs at least one active organisation admin.')`); `App\Actions\Audit\RecordActivity::handle(ActivityEvent $event, ?Model $subject = null, array $properties = [], array $changes = [], ?User $causer = null, ?Organisation $organisation = null, bool $defaultCauser = true): Activity` and `ActivityEvent::{UserStatusChanged,UserDeleted,UserRestored}` (Task 1; called with named arguments `changes:` and `causer:`); `AvailableEmail` (Task 5); test helper `recordedActivity(ActivityEvent $event): Collection<int, Activity>` (Task 1).
- Produces:
  - `App\Actions\Users\UpdateUserStatus::handle(User $actor, User $target, UserStatus $status): void` — `@throws AuthorizationException|ValidationException`; every validation error is on `status`.
  - `App\Actions\Users\DeleteUser::handle(User $actor, User $target): void` — errors on `user` (`__('Cancel the invitation instead.')`, the lock-out messages); a trashed target is a no-op.
  - `App\Actions\Users\RestoreUser::handle(User $actor, User $target): void` — errors on `user` (`__('This user never accepted their invitation. Invite the address again.')`, `__('Restore the organisation first.')`) or `email` (`AvailableEmail` messages, `__('This address can\'t be used.')` for a lost race); a target that is not trashed is a no-op.
  - `App\Tenancy\Auth\Sessions` (final): `/** @param list<int> $userIds */ public static function endFor(array $userIds): void` — deletes every `sessions` row whose `user_id` is in `$userIds` and sets those users' `remember_token` to null, through `DB::table()` (so soft-deleted users are reached too); `[]` is a no-op; no payload decoding. Consumed by Task 15 (`ArchiveOrganisation`, `PurgeOrganisation`).
  - `UserStatus::color(): string`.
  - All three actions are `final readonly` classes resolved from the container: `UpdateUserStatus` and `DeleteUser` inject `LockoutGuard`, `EffectivePermissions` and `RecordActivity`; `RestoreUser` injects `RecordActivity`. The activity causer is always the `$actor` passed in.
  - `UpdateUserStatus` and `DeleteUser` decide on the stored row (`status`, `is_super_admin`, `deleted_at`), read as the first statement inside their transaction; their private `ensureAnotherActiveAdmin(User $target, bool $isSuperAdmin): void` takes the stored super-admin flag.

```php
/** covers §4.4, §4.6 */

use Illuminate\Validation\ValidationException;

/**
 * The validation errors an action throws, or [] when it succeeds.
 *
 * @return array<string, array<int, string>>

$errorsOf = function (Closure $action): array {
    try {
        $action();
    } catch (ValidationException $exception) {
        return $exception->errors();
    }

    return [];
};

$adminOf = function (Organisation $organisation, User $user): User {
    withPermissionsTeam($organisation->id, fn (): User => $user->assignRole(Role::OrganisationAdmin->value));
    $user->unsetRelation('roles');

    return $user;

        ->and($errorsOf(fn () => app(DeleteUser::class)->handle($disabledSuperAdmin, $onlyActive)))
        ->toBe(['user' => [__('At least one active super admin must remain.')]])
        ->and($onlyActive->refresh()->isActive())->toBeTrue()

    $first = $adminOf($organisation, User::factory()->for($organisation)->create());
```
