- [ ] **Step 4: The controller — `show` and `store`**

Replace `app/Http/Controllers/Auth/HandoffController.php` with:

```php
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace App\Http\Controllers\Auth;

use App\Events\HandoffConsumed;
use App\Http\Controllers\Controller;
use App\Models\HandoffToken;
use App\Models\User;
use App\Tenancy\Auth\HostLoginRule;
use App\Tenancy\Hosts;
use Illuminate\Http\RedirectResponse;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
use Illuminate\Http\Response;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Auth;
use Illuminate\Support\Str;

/**
 * Consumes a handoff link on its target host (§6.4). A guest is signed in. The user the link was issued
 * for, already signed in here, just continues: no new sign-in, so the session and the remember token stay
 * as they are. A different signed-in user is asked first, and only the CSRF-protected confirmation POST
 * replaces this browser's session; a GET never replaces another user's session (FU3-2, RL-22).
 */
final class HandoffController extends Controller
{
    public function show(Request $request, HostLoginRule $rule, string $token): RedirectResponse|Response
    {
        $handoff = $this->usableHandoff($request, $token);
        $user = $handoff instanceof HandoffToken ? $this->userOf($handoff, $rule) : null;

        if (! $handoff instanceof HandoffToken || ! $user instanceof User) {
            return $this->refuse();
        }

        $current = $request->user();

        if ($current instanceof User && ! $current->is($user)) {
            return response()
                ->view('pages::auth.handoff-confirm', [
                    'currentName' => $current->name,
                    'targetName' => $user->name,
                    'action' => route('auth.handoff.store', ['token' => $token]),
                ])
                ->header('Referrer-Policy', 'no-referrer');
        }

        return $this->consume($request, $handoff, $user);
    }

    public function store(Request $request, HostLoginRule $rule, string $token): RedirectResponse
    {
        $handoff = $this->usableHandoff($request, $token);
        $user = $handoff instanceof HandoffToken ? $this->userOf($handoff, $rule) : null;

        if (! $handoff instanceof HandoffToken || ! $user instanceof User) {
            return $this->refuse();
        }

        return $this->consume($request, $handoff, $user);
    }

    /**
     * Claims the token, signs the user in unless they already are, and redirects to the token's path:
     * absolute on the target host so the redirect never depends on a URL origin forced earlier.
     */
    private function consume(Request $request, HandoffToken $handoff, User $user): RedirectResponse
    {
        if (! $this->claim($handoff)) {
            return $this->refuse();
        }

        $current = $request->user();

        if (! $current instanceof User || ! $current->is($user)) {
            $this->signIn($request, $user);
        }

        event(new HandoffConsumed($user, $handoff->target_host));

        return redirect()->to(Hosts::url($handoff->target_host, $handoff->path))->header('Referrer-Policy', 'no-referrer');
    }

    /** An unconsumed, unexpired token issued for this host. Reading it changes nothing. */
    private function usableHandoff(Request $request, string $token): ?HandoffToken
    {
        return HandoffToken::query()
            ->where('token_hash', hash('sha256', $token))
            ->whereNull('consumed_at')
            ->where('expires_at', '>', now())
            ->where('target_host', Str::lower($request->getHost()))
            ->first();
    }

    /** The token's user, read without the tenant scope, when the host login rule lets them in here. */
    private function userOf(HandoffToken $handoff, HostLoginRule $rule): ?User
    {
        $user = Auth::createUserProvider('users')?->retrieveById($handoff->user_id);

        return $user instanceof User && $rule->allows($user) ? $user : null;
    }

    /** Atomic: only one request can mark the token as consumed, and only before it expires. */
    private function claim(HandoffToken $handoff): bool
    {
        return HandoffToken::query()
            ->whereKey($handoff->id)
            ->whereNull('consumed_at')
            ->where('expires_at', '>', now())
            ->update(['consumed_at' => now()]) === 1;
    }

    /**
     * Replaces this browser's session only. logoutCurrentDevice() leaves the previous user's remember
     * token alone (logout() would cycle it and sign them out everywhere); nothing from the earlier
     * session (password confirmation, intended URL) carries over.
     */
    private function signIn(Request $request, User $user): void
    {
        $guard = Auth::guard('web');

        if ($guard->check()) {
            $guard->logoutCurrentDevice();
        }

        $request->session()->invalidate();
        $guard->login($user);
        $request->session()->regenerateToken();
    }

    private function refuse(): RedirectResponse
    {
        return to_route('login')->with('status', __('This sign-in link is invalid or has expired.'));
    }
}
```

### Task 17: Organisations index — archived view, Open via handoff, archive/restore/purge UI, `/` for super admins

**Covers:** ORG-3, ORG-6..10 (UI), ORG-18, ORG-19, TEN-1, TEN-4, DEC26-1, DEC26-2, DEC27-2, DEC27-3, DEC27-4, HND-1 (Open), FU3-1, RL-10 (`organisations`), RL-17, RL-18.

What this task builds (spec §4.3, §6.2):

- `GET /organisations` (`organisations.index`, any host, route gate `organisations.view`). On a tenant host it shows only that organisation (ORG-3); on a central host (where only super admins get through the membership middleware) it lists every organisation, with a search on name and address and an "Active / Archived" segmented switch bound to `?view=` (ORG-7; the archived view exists only for super admins on central hosts).
- Row actions: **Open** (super admins on central hosts, enforced in the action too: it answers 404 on a tenant host; signs the actor in on the organisation's host through a single-use handoff, ORG-18 — only `$this->currentUser()` is ever handed off, FU3-1); **Archive** (confirmation modal, `ArchiveOrganisation`); **Restore** (archived view, `RestoreOrganisation`); **Purge** (archived view; asks for a fresh password confirmation first and comes back to the archived view, then a modal where the slug must be typed, `PurgeOrganisation`, RL-18).
- Every action re-resolves the organisation from a plain `int` id inside this host's scope (another organisation's id from a tenant host → 404) and re-authorises before calling the action; the action authorises again.
- `/` sends a super admin on the apex or the admin host to `organisations.index` (TEN-1, DEC26-2); everyone else keeps today's behaviour.
- The interim "Administration" sidebar group gets an "Organisations" link for `organisations.view` holders.
- The route × host matrix gets the `organisations` outcome (with its assertion arm) for `home`, and the `organisations.index` row.

**Files:**
- Create: `resources/views/pages/organisations/index/index.php`, `resources/views/pages/organisations/index/index.blade.php`
- Modify: `routes/web.php` (`/`), `routes/admin.php`, `resources/views/layouts/app/sidebar.blade.php` (Organisations item), `tests/Feature/Tenancy/RouteHostMatrixTest.php` (`organisations.index` row, `organisations` outcome + `assertRedirect(route('organisations.index'))` arm, `home` arm), `tests/Feature/Navigation/AdministrationLinksTest.php`, `lang/nl.json`, `lang/en.json`
- Test: `tests/Feature/Organisations/OrganisationsIndexTest.php`

**Interfaces:**

In `tests/Feature/Tenancy/RouteHostMatrixTest.php`:

2. `routeMatrixOutcome()` gets the new `organisations` outcome for `home` and the `organisations.index` row in the `forbidden` list (the route-less member gets 403 on every permission page of its own host; Task 8 introduced that arm). After this step the function reads:

```php
/** @return 'ok'|'login'|'dashboard'|'confirm'|'forbidden'|'organisations' */
function routeMatrixOutcome(string $route, string $actor, string $host): string
{
    $signedIn = $actor !== 'guest';
    $belongsHere = $actor === 'super admin' || $host === 'tenant';

    return match (true) {
        $signedIn && ! $belongsHere => 'login',           // membership middleware logs out first
        $route === 'home' => match (true) {
            ! $signedIn => 'login',
            $actor === 'super admin' && $host !== 'tenant' => 'organisations', // TEN-1
            default => 'dashboard',
        },
        in_array($route, ['login', 'password.request', 'two-factor.login'], true) => match (true) {
            $signedIn => 'dashboard',                     // guest-only pages
            $route === 'two-factor.login' => 'login',     // no challenge in the session
            default => 'ok',
        },
        ! $signedIn => 'login',
        $route === 'security.edit' => 'confirm',
        $actor === 'member' && in_array($route, [
            'users.index', 'users.edit', 'users.invite', 'invitations.pending', 'organisations.index',
        ], true) => 'forbidden',                          // the matrix member holds no permission
        default => 'ok',
    };
}
```

(If Task 8 wrote the `forbidden` arm with a differently named list, keep its form and add `'organisations.index'` to it; the `home` arm and the `@return` change as shown.)

Run: `php artisan make:livewire pages::organisations.index --no-interaction`

Replace `resources/views/pages/organisations/index/index.php` with:

```php
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

use App\Actions\Auth\IssueHandoff;
use App\Actions\Organisations\ArchiveOrganisation;
use App\Actions\Organisations\PurgeOrganisation;
use App\Actions\Organisations\RestoreOrganisation;
use App\Concerns\ConfirmsPasswords;
use App\Concerns\ResolvesCurrentUser;
use App\Models\Organisation;
use App\Tenancy\Hosts;
use App\Tenancy\HostScope;
use Flux\Flux;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Builder;
use Illuminate\Pagination\LengthAwarePaginator;
use Livewire\Attributes\Computed;
use Livewire\Attributes\Locked;
use Livewire\Attributes\Title;
use Livewire\Attributes\Url;
use Livewire\Component;
use Livewire\WithPagination;

/**
 * Organisations index (§4.3, §6.2). A tenant host shows its own organisation; super admins on a central
 * host see every organisation, the archived view, "Open" (a handoff to the organisation's host) and
 * archive / restore / purge. Every action re-resolves its organisation inside this host's scope from a
 * plain id, re-authorises and calls the action, which authorises again.
 */
new #[Title('Organisations')] class extends Component
{
    use ConfirmsPasswords;
    use ResolvesCurrentUser;
    use WithPagination;

    #[Url]
    public string $view = 'active';

    #[Url]
    public string $search = '';

    #[Locked]
    public ?int $archivingId = null;

    #[Locked]
    public ?int $purgingId = null;

    public string $purgeConfirmation = '';

    public function mount(): void
    {
        $this->authorize('viewAny', Organisation::class);
    }

    /** Back to the first page whenever the view or the search changes. */
    public function updated(string $property): void
    {
        if (in_array($property, ['view', 'search'], true)) {
            $this->resetPage();
        }
    }

    /**
     * "Open": sign the current user in on the organisation's own host through a handoff; super admins on a
     * central host only (ORG-18). On a tenant host it answers 404 for every actor, so nobody can mint a
     * sign-in link for themselves there.
     */
    public function open(int $organisationId, IssueHandoff $issueHandoff): void
    {
        abort_unless(HostScope::organisationId() === null, 404);

        $organisation = $this->findOrganisation($organisationId);
        $this->authorize('view', $organisation);

        // FU3-1: only the signed-in actor is ever handed off. An absolute URL on another host: no navigate.
        $this->redirect($issueHandoff->handle($this->currentUser(), Hosts::tenant($organisation->slug)));
    }

    public function confirmArchive(int $organisationId): void
    {
        $organisation = $this->findOrganisation($organisationId);
        $this->authorize('delete', $organisation);

        $this->archivingId = $organisation->id;
        Flux::modal('archive-organisation')->show();
    }

    public function archive(ArchiveOrganisation $archiveOrganisation): void
    {
        if ($this->archivingId === null) {
            return;
        }

        $organisation = $this->findOrganisation($this->archivingId);
        $this->authorize('delete', $organisation);

        $archiveOrganisation->handle($this->currentUser(), $organisation);

        $this->archivingId = null;
        Flux::modal('archive-organisation')->close();
        Flux::toast(variant: 'success', text: __('Organisation :name archived.', ['name' => $organisation->name]));
    }

    public function restore(int $organisationId, RestoreOrganisation $restoreOrganisation): void
    {
        $organisation = $this->findOrganisation($organisationId, archived: true);
        $this->authorize('restore', $organisation);

        $restoreOrganisation->handle($this->currentUser(), $organisation);

        Flux::toast(variant: 'success', text: __('Organisation :name restored.', ['name' => $organisation->name]));
    }

    /** RL-18: a purge needs a fresh password confirmation, asked before the modal opens. */
    public function confirmPurge(int $organisationId): void
    {
        $organisation = $this->findOrganisation($organisationId, archived: true);
        $this->authorize('forceDelete', $organisation);

        if ($this->passwordConfirmationRequired($this->archivedViewUrl())) {
            return;
        }

        $this->purgingId = $organisation->id;
        $this->purgeConfirmation = '';
        $this->resetErrorBag('purgeConfirmation');
        Flux::modal('purge-organisation')->show();
    }

    /** Checked again here: the confirmation may have expired while the modal was open, or the call is replayed. */
    public function purge(PurgeOrganisation $purgeOrganisation): void
    {
        if ($this->purgingId === null) {
            return;
        }

        $this->resetErrorBag('purgeConfirmation');

        $organisation = $this->findOrganisation($this->purgingId, archived: true);
        $this->authorize('forceDelete', $organisation);

        if ($this->passwordConfirmationRequired($this->archivedViewUrl())) {
            return;
        }

        if ($this->purgeConfirmation !== $organisation->slug) {
            $this->addError('purgeConfirmation', __('Type :slug to confirm.', ['slug' => $organisation->slug]));

            return;
        }

        $purgeOrganisation->handle($this->currentUser(), $organisation, $this->purgeConfirmation);

        $this->purgingId = null;
        $this->purgeConfirmation = '';
        Flux::modal('purge-organisation')->close();
        Flux::toast(variant: 'success', text: __('Organisation :name purged.', ['name' => $organisation->name]));
    }

    /** @return LengthAwarePaginator<int, Organisation> */
    #[Computed]
    public function organisations(): LengthAwarePaginator
    {
        // RK-I4: organisations are central models, so this host's scope is applied explicitly.
        $organisationId = HostScope::organisationId();
        $search = trim($this->search);
        $query = $this->showsArchived() ? Organisation::onlyTrashed() : Organisation::query();

        return $query
            ->when($organisationId !== null, fn (Builder $query): Builder => $query->whereKey($organisationId))
            ->when($search !== '', fn (Builder $query): Builder => $query->where(fn (Builder $query): Builder => $query
                ->whereLike('name', '%'.$search.'%', caseSensitive: false)
                ->orWhereLike('slug', '%'.$search.'%', caseSensitive: false)))
            ->orderBy('name')
            ->paginate(25);
    }

    /** A super admin on the apex or the admin host: the archived view and "Open" are shown only there. */
    #[Computed]
    public function onCentralHost(): bool
    {
        return HostScope::organisationId() === null;
    }

    #[Computed]
    public function archivingOrganisation(): ?Organisation
    {
        return $this->archivingId === null ? null : Organisation::query()->find($this->archivingId);
    }

    #[Computed]
    public function purgingOrganisation(): ?Organisation
    {
        return $this->purgingId === null ? null : Organisation::onlyTrashed()->find($this->purgingId);
    }

    /** An organisation this host may act on: on a tenant host only its own, otherwise 404. */
    private function findOrganisation(int $organisationId, bool $archived = false): Organisation
    {
        $hostOrganisationId = HostScope::organisationId();

        abort_if($hostOrganisationId !== null && $hostOrganisationId !== $organisationId, 404);

        $query = $archived ? Organisation::onlyTrashed() : Organisation::query();

        return $query->findOrFail($organisationId);
    }

    private function showsArchived(): bool
    {
        return $this->view === 'archived' && HostScope::organisationId() === null;
    }

    /** Built server-side: where the password confirmation sends the super admin back to. */
    private function archivedViewUrl(): string
    {
        return route('organisations.index', ['view' => 'archived'], absolute: false);
    }
};
```

### Task 18: Organisation wizard and edit page (slug-rename redirect)

**Covers:** ORG-4 (UI), ORG-5 (UI), ORG-14 (UI), ORG-16, ORG-19, TEN-4, DEC26-1, DEC27-2, FU3-1, RL-10 (`not found`), RL-12, RL-17 (no second-factor setting), OD-3 (= B); OR-M5.

What this task builds (spec §4.3, §6.2):

- **Wizard** `GET /organisations/create` (`organisations.create`, `Route::central()`: apex and admin host only, a tenant host answers 404 — the host check runs before the `organisations.create` route gate; route gate `organisations.create`, super-admin only). Fields: name; slug, suggested from the name (`Str::slug`, at most 63 characters, no edge hyphen) until the slug is edited, with live availability and a `slug.apex` preview; description; the first admin's email address and language (`App\Enums\Locale`, default `Locale::default()`). Submitting calls `CreateOrganisation`, which creates the organisation, the pending first admin (organisation_admin template) and the invitation in one transaction and queues the invitation mail after commit (Task 14). The super admin returns to `organisations.index` with a `status` flash, which the flash→toast bridge (Task 12) shows as a toast.
- **Edit page** `GET /organisations/{organisation}/edit` (`organisations.edit`, any host, `->whereNumber('organisation')`, route gate `organisations.update`). It takes a plain `int` id and resolves the organisation per request (no model binding, OR-M5): on a tenant host only that host's organisation (any other id → 404), on a central host any active organisation for a super admin; archived organisations → 404. Name and description are editable by organisation admins of that organisation and by super admins. **Only super admins change the slug (OD-3 = B)**; organisation admins see the address read-only, and a slug they send anyway is ignored (the action refuses it too). No `require_second_factor` setting is shown until M7 (RL-17). After a slug rename made on that organisation's own host (the host stops existing), the page sends the editor on through `IssueHandoff::handle($this->currentUser(), Hosts::tenant($newSlug), route('organisations.edit', $id, absolute: false))`, issued only after the update committed (ORG-16); a rename on the admin host stays on the page.
- The organisations index gets a "New organisation" button (super admins on central hosts) and an "Edit" link per row (`@can('update', $organisation)`).
- The matrix gets the `not found` outcome with its `assertNotFound()` arm and the `organisations.create` / `organisations.edit` rows (`matrixParameters()` supplies `{organisation}`).

**Files:**
- Create: `resources/views/pages/organisations/create/create.php`, `resources/views/pages/organisations/create/create.blade.php`, `resources/views/pages/organisations/edit/edit.php`, `resources/views/pages/organisations/edit/edit.blade.php`
- Modify: `routes/admin.php`, `resources/views/pages/organisations/index/index.blade.php` ("New organisation", edit links), `tests/Feature/Tenancy/RouteHostMatrixTest.php` (rows, `not found` outcome + `assertNotFound()` arm, `matrixParameters()` arm for `organisations.edit`), `tests/Arch/AuthorizationRulesTest.php` (the permission-string rule stops flagging route names such as `organisations.create`), `lang/nl.json`, `lang/en.json`
- Test: `tests/Feature/Organisations/OrganisationWizardTest.php`, `tests/Feature/Organisations/OrganisationEditTest.php`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `App\Actions\Organisations\CreateOrganisation::handle(User $actor, string $name, string $slug, ?string $description, string $adminEmail, Locale $adminLocale): Organisation` and `UpdateOrganisation::handle(User $actor, Organisation $organisation, string $name, string $slug, ?string $description): Organisation` (Task 14); `App\Concerns\OrganisationValidationRules::organisationNameRules(?int $ignoreId = null, bool $revealArchived = false): array` and `organisationSlugRules(?int $ignoreId = null, bool $revealArchived = false): array` and `organisationDescriptionRules(): array` (`nullable|string|max:1000`, the rule `CreateOrganisation` and `UpdateOrganisation` use, so page and action never drift apart) (Task 14); `App\Rules\AvailableEmail::__construct(?int $organisationId, ?int $ignoreUserId = null)` (Task 5); `App\Enums\Locale` (`cases()`, `label()`, `default()`, Task 10); `IssueHandoff::handle()` (Task 16); `Hosts::tenant()`; `HostScope::organisationId()`, `ResolvesCurrentUser::currentUser()` (Task 7); `OrganisationPolicy::{create,update}`; `matrixParameters(string $route, Organisation $organisation): array<string, int>` (Task 9).
- Produces:
  - Page `pages::organisations.create`: `public string $name = ''`, `public string $slug = ''`, `public bool $slugEdited = false`, `public ?string $description = null`, `public string $adminEmail = ''`, `public string $adminLocale = ''` (set to `Locale::default()->value` in `mount()`); `mount(): void`; `updatedName(): void` (suggests the slug until it is edited); `updatedSlug(): void` (lower-cases, marks it edited); `#[Computed] slugStatus(): array{available: bool, message: string|null, host: string}`; `create(CreateOrganisation $createOrganisation): void` (redirect `organisations.index` with `status`).
  - Page `pages::organisations.edit`: `mount(int $organisation): void` (`authorize('update', …)`); `#[Locked] public int $organisationId`; `public string $name = ''`, `public string $slug = ''`, `public ?string $description = null`; `#[Computed] organisation(): Organisation` (tenant host: only `Tenant::current()`'s id, else 404; central: super admins, any active id); `#[Computed] canChangeSlug(): bool`; `save(UpdateOrganisation $updateOrganisation, IssueHandoff $issueHandoff): void`.
  - Routes `Route::central(function (): void { Route::livewire('organisations/create', 'pages::organisations.create')->can(Permission::OrganisationsCreate)->name('organisations.create'); })` and `Route::livewire('organisations/{organisation}/edit', 'pages::organisations.edit')->whereNumber('organisation')->can(Permission::OrganisationsUpdate)->name('organisations.edit')`.

In `tests/Arch/AuthorizationRulesTest.php`, replace the first test, `it('spells permission names only in the Permission enum', …)`, with the version below. Why: the wizard route is named `organisations.create` (spec §6.2, the matrix and later tasks use that name), which is exactly the value of `Permission::OrganisationsCreate`. The current rule flags every quoted string equal to a permission name, so `->name('organisations.create')` in `routes/admin.php` and `route('organisations.create')` in the index Blade would fail `composer check`. The new version first drops route-name arguments (`name(`, `route(`, `to_route(`, `redirectRoute(`, `routeIs(`) and ignores a component name such as `pages::organisations.create` (double colon), while `->can('organisations.create')` and `'can:organisations.create'` are still flagged. Its self-checks pin both sides. The imports of the file (`App\Authorization\Permission`, `Illuminate\Support\Str`) stay as they are, and the other tests in the file are unchanged.

```php
it('spells permission names only in the Permission enum', function (): void {
    $names = implode('|', array_map(fn (string $name): string => preg_quote($name, '/'), Permission::values()));
    $files = array_values(array_diff(kitSourceFiles('app', 'routes', 'resources/views'), ['app/Authorization/Permission.php']));

    // A name as a whole string, after a single-colon `prefix:` (can:, permission:) or inside a `|` / `,` list.
    // `pages::organisations.create` (a component name, double colon) is not a permission.
    $pattern = "/(['\"])(?:[^'\"]*(?<!:)[:|,])?(?:{$names})(?<!:)(?:[|,][^'\"]*)?\\1/";
    // Route names may equal a permission name (organisations.create): drop route-name arguments first.
    $routeNames = '/\b(?:name|route|to_route|redirectRoute|routeIs)\(\s*([\'"])[\w.*-]+\1/';
    $spells = fn (string $contents): bool => preg_match($pattern, (string) preg_replace($routeNames, '', $contents)) === 1;

    expect($spells("->can('organisations.create')"))->toBeTrue()
        ->and($spells("'can:organisations.create'"))->toBeTrue()
        ->and($spells("->name('organisations.create')"))->toBeFalse()
        ->and($spells("route('organisations.create')"))->toBeFalse()
        ->and($spells("'pages::organisations.create'"))->toBeFalse()
        ->and(array_values(array_filter($files, fn (string $path): bool => $spells((string) file_get_contents(base_path($path))))))->toBe([]);
});
```

function matrixParameters(string $route, Organisation $organisation): array
{

(Keep Task 9's `users.edit` arm exactly as Task 9 wrote it if it differs from the line above; only the `organisations.edit` arm is new.)

3. `routeMatrixOutcome()` gets the `not found` outcome: the wizard is a `Route::central()` page, and `EnsureCentralHost` runs before `can:`, so **every** signed-in actor on a tenant host gets 404 (guests are still sent to login first, non-super actors on central hosts are still logged out first). `organisations.edit` joins the `forbidden` list (the matrix member holds no `organisations.update`). After this step the function reads:

```php
/** @return 'ok'|'login'|'dashboard'|'confirm'|'forbidden'|'organisations'|'not found' */
function routeMatrixOutcome(string $route, string $actor, string $host): string
{
    $signedIn = $actor !== 'guest';
    $belongsHere = $actor === 'super admin' || $host === 'tenant';

    return match (true) {
        $signedIn && ! $belongsHere => 'login',           // membership middleware logs out first
        $route === 'home' => match (true) {
            ! $signedIn => 'login',
            $actor === 'super admin' && $host !== 'tenant' => 'organisations', // TEN-1
            default => 'dashboard',
        },
        in_array($route, ['login', 'password.request', 'two-factor.login'], true) => match (true) {
            $signedIn => 'dashboard',                     // guest-only pages
            $route === 'two-factor.login' => 'login',     // no challenge in the session
            default => 'ok',
        },
        ! $signedIn => 'login',
        $route === 'organisations.create' && $host === 'tenant' => 'not found', // central page; host before can:
        $route === 'security.edit' => 'confirm',
        $actor === 'member' && in_array($route, [
            'users.index', 'users.edit', 'users.invite', 'invitations.pending', 'organisations.index',
            'organisations.edit',
        ], true) => 'forbidden',                          // the matrix member holds no permission
        default => 'ok',
    };
}
```

The organisation admin reaches `organisations.create` only on its tenant host (404 there) and is logged out on central hosts, so it never reaches the super-only route gate.

Replace `resources/views/pages/organisations/create/create.php` with:

```php
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

use App\Actions\Organisations\CreateOrganisation;
use App\Concerns\OrganisationValidationRules;
use App\Concerns\ResolvesCurrentUser;
use App\Enums\Locale;
use App\Models\Organisation;
use App\Rules\AvailableEmail;
use App\Tenancy\Hosts;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Validator;
use Illuminate\Support\Str;
use Illuminate\Validation\Rule;
use Illuminate\Validation\ValidationException;
use Livewire\Attributes\Computed;
use Livewire\Attributes\Title;
use Livewire\Component;

/**
 * Organisation wizard (§4.3, ORG-14): name, slug (suggested, live availability, slug.apex preview),
 * description and the first admin's address and language. CreateOrganisation creates the organisation,
 * the pending first admin and the invitation in one transaction (RL-12). Central hosts only.
 */
new #[Title('New organisation')] class extends Component
{
    use OrganisationValidationRules;
    use ResolvesCurrentUser;

    public string $name = '';

    public string $slug = '';

    public bool $slugEdited = false;

    public ?string $description = null;

    public string $adminEmail = '';

    public string $adminLocale = '';

    public function mount(): void
    {
        $this->authorize('create', Organisation::class);

        $this->adminLocale = Locale::default()->value;
    }

    /** The slug follows the name until someone edits it. */
    public function updatedName(): void
    {
        if (! $this->slugEdited) {
            $this->slug = trim(Str::limit(Str::slug($this->name), 63, ''), '-');
        }
    }

    /** An emptied slug follows the name again. */
    public function updatedSlug(): void
    {
        $this->slug = Str::lower(trim($this->slug));
        $this->slugEdited = $this->slug !== '';
    }

    /** @return array{available: bool, message: string|null, host: string} */
    #[Computed]
    public function slugStatus(): array
    {
        if ($this->slug === '') {
            return ['available' => false, 'message' => null, 'host' => ''];
        }

        $validator = Validator::make(
            ['slug' => $this->slug],
            ['slug' => $this->organisationSlugRules(null, $this->currentUser()->isSuperAdmin())],
        );

        return [
            'available' => $validator->passes(),
            'message' => $validator->passes() ? null : $validator->errors()->first('slug'),
            'host' => Hosts::tenant($this->slug),
        ];
    }

    public function create(CreateOrganisation $createOrganisation): void
    {
        $this->authorize('create', Organisation::class);

        $actor = $this->currentUser();

        $this->validate([
            'name' => $this->organisationNameRules(null, $actor->isSuperAdmin()),
            'slug' => $this->organisationSlugRules(null, $actor->isSuperAdmin()),
            'description' => $this->organisationDescriptionRules(),
            // A new organisation has no users yet: any holder of the address is elsewhere (W9 generic message).
            'adminEmail' => ['required', 'string', 'email', 'max:255', new AvailableEmail(null)],
            'adminLocale' => ['required', 'string', Rule::enum(Locale::class)],
        ]);

        try {
            $organisation = $createOrganisation->handle(
                $actor,
                $this->name,
                $this->slug,
                $this->normalisedDescription(),
                $this->adminEmail,
                Locale::from($this->adminLocale),
            );
        } catch (ValidationException $exception) {
            // The invitation step reports the address as "email"; this form calls it "adminEmail".
            throw ValidationException::withMessages(collect($exception->errors())
                ->mapWithKeys(fn (array $messages, string $field): array => [$field === 'email' ? 'adminEmail' : $field => $messages])
                ->all());
        }

        session()->flash('status', __('Organisation :name created. Its first admin has been invited.', ['name' => $organisation->name]));
        $this->redirectRoute('organisations.index', navigate: true);
    }

    private function normalisedDescription(): ?string
    {
        return $this->description === null || trim($this->description) === '' ? null : trim($this->description);
    }
};
```

Replace `resources/views/pages/organisations/edit/edit.php` with:

```php
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

use App\Actions\Auth\IssueHandoff;
use App\Actions\Organisations\UpdateOrganisation;
use App\Concerns\OrganisationValidationRules;
use App\Concerns\ResolvesCurrentUser;
use App\Models\Organisation;
use App\Tenancy\Facades\Tenant;
use App\Tenancy\Hosts;
use App\Tenancy\HostScope;
use Flux\Flux;
use Illuminate\Support\Str;
use Livewire\Attributes\Computed;
use Livewire\Attributes\Locked;
use Livewire\Attributes\Title;
use Livewire\Component;

/**
 * Organisation edit page (§4.3). Takes a plain id and resolves it per request inside the host's scope
 * (OR-M5). Organisation admins edit name and description; only super admins change the slug (OD-3 = B).
 * A rename made on the organisation's own host continues on the new host through a handoff (ORG-16).
 * No second-factor setting until M7 (RL-17).
 */
new #[Title('Edit organisation')] class extends Component
{
    use OrganisationValidationRules;
    use ResolvesCurrentUser;

    #[Locked]
    public int $organisationId;

    public string $name = '';

    public string $slug = '';

    public ?string $description = null;

    public function mount(int $organisation): void
    {
        $this->organisationId = $organisation;
        $model = $this->organisation();
        $this->authorize('update', $model);

        $this->name = $model->name;
        $this->slug = $model->slug;
        $this->description = $model->description;
    }

    public function save(UpdateOrganisation $updateOrganisation, IssueHandoff $issueHandoff): void
    {
        $actor = $this->currentUser();
        $organisation = $this->organisation();
        $this->authorize('update', $organisation);

        $previousSlug = $organisation->slug;
        // OD-3: only super admins change the slug; for everyone else the stored one is kept, whatever is sent.
        $this->slug = $actor->isSuperAdmin() ? Str::lower(trim($this->slug)) : $previousSlug;

        $rules = [
            'name' => $this->organisationNameRules($organisation->id, $actor->isSuperAdmin()),
            'description' => $this->organisationDescriptionRules(),
        ];

        if ($actor->isSuperAdmin()) {
            $rules['slug'] = $this->organisationSlugRules($organisation->id, true);
        }

        $this->validate($rules);

        $updated = $updateOrganisation->handle($actor, $organisation, $this->name, $this->slug, $this->normalisedDescription());

        if ($updated->slug !== $previousSlug && Tenant::check()) {
            // ORG-16: this host no longer exists. The update has committed; continue on the new host as the
            // signed-in actor only (FU3-1). Absolute URL on another host: no navigate.
            $this->redirect($issueHandoff->handle(
                $actor,
                Hosts::tenant($updated->slug),
                route('organisations.edit', $this->organisationId, absolute: false),
            ));

            return;
        }

        $this->slug = $updated->slug;
        Flux::toast(variant: 'success', text: __('Organisation saved.'));
    }

    /** On a tenant host only that host's organisation; on a central host (super admins) any active one. */
    #[Computed]
    public function organisation(): Organisation
    {
        $hostOrganisationId = HostScope::organisationId();

        abort_if($hostOrganisationId !== null && $hostOrganisationId !== $this->organisationId, 404);

        return Organisation::query()->findOrFail($this->organisationId);
    }

    #[Computed]
    public function canChangeSlug(): bool
    {
        return $this->currentUser()->isSuperAdmin();
    }

    private function normalisedDescription(): ?string
    {
        return $this->description === null || trim($this->description) === '' ? null : trim($this->description);
    }
};
```

### Task 19: Impersonation policy and the module flag (CI off path)

**Covers:** IMP-2, IMP-3 (policy), IMP-4, IMP-5 (policy), IMP-10, IMP-11 (policy), IMP-12 (CI env), IMP-13, USR-15 (impersonation matrix), DEC26-5, FU2-2, FU2-9, FU3-17, W3 (policy), W6 (location), X6, C-3, C-4, RL-20 (policy), RL-21 (flag, CI), RL-26; OR-B2, OR-I7 (first half), CV-2, RK-I6.

What this task delivers, in plain words (spec §4.7, §6.8, §7.2):

- Impersonation is an optional module behind `config('skv.modules.impersonation')` (env `MODULE_IMPERSONATION`, default `true`; the key exists since Task 11's `config/skv.php`). It is built in-house on the stock session guard (owner ruling OD-1 = C); no package is added.
- This task adds who **may** impersonate whom, nothing that swaps a session yet:
  - `impersonate` is in `SuperAdminGate::ALWAYS_CHECKED`, so `Gate::before` does not grant it to super admins; `UserPolicy::impersonate` decides for everyone and grants super admins explicitly (FU2-2). A policy method wins over a `Gate::define('impersonate')`, so none is added (C-3).
  - The policy is true only when the module is on, this session is not impersonating already (depth 1, IMP-3) and the **matrix** allows the pair.
  - The matrix (IMP-4, IMP-5, C-4, X6): only on a tenant host; the target belongs to that organisation, is active (not pending, not disabled, W3), not deleted, not a super admin and not the actor. Then a super admin may impersonate anyone (organisation admins included). Anyone else needs `users.impersonate` in that organisation and may only impersonate "non-admins": a target that does not hold the `organisation_admin` template role (checked by role id, W6 — the rule lives in the policy, not in a role name) and whose effective permissions (role and direct permissions in that team, read with explicit queries, RK-I6) are all held by the actor (the permission-subset rule, RL-26).
- The users index evaluates that same matrix for a whole page in one batch (`UserAbilities::forPage()` gains an `impersonate` column); the policy and the page can never disagree.
- `App\Tenancy\Auth\Impersonation` starts with its read-only part: the module flag (`enabled()`) and whether this session is impersonating (`isActive()`, a session key, **independent of the flag** so that turning the module off can still end a running impersonation, RK-I3).
- The CI job `sqlite-free` runs the whole suite with `MODULE_IMPERSONATION=false` (IMP-12). `phpunit.xml` pins `MODULE_IMPERSONATION=true` **without** `force`, so that environment value wins in CI; every impersonation test from now on calls the new helper `useImpersonationModule(true)` (or `false` for off rows) instead of relying on the boot value. While editing `phpunit.xml`, the host pins get `force="true"` (FU2-9) and `PASSKEYS_RELYING_PARTY_ID` / `TRUSTED_PROXIES` are pinned to today's effective (empty) values (FU3-17).
- From this task on every gate also runs the suite with the module off: `php artisan config:clear && MODULE_IMPERSONATION=false vendor/bin/pest --parallel` (OR-I1). `php artisan test` clears every variable named in .env before it starts PHPUnit, so the off run calls Pest directly, as test:pgsql does.

**Files:**
- Create: `app/Tenancy/Auth/Impersonation.php` (read-only part: flag and session state)
- Modify: `app/Policies/UserPolicy.php` (`impersonate`), `app/Authorization/UserAbilities.php` (`mayImpersonate()`, `impersonate` column in `forPage()`), `phpunit.xml`, `.github/workflows/tests.yml` (`sqlite-free`: `MODULE_IMPERSONATION=false`), `tests/Pest.php` (`useImpersonationModule()` — config only), `tests/Arch/NameLeakTest.php` (allow `config(['skv.…' => …])` in tests)
- Test: `tests/Feature/Impersonation/ImpersonationPolicyTest.php` (new), `tests/Feature/Tooling/CiWorkflowTest.php` (added cases)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `config('skv.modules.impersonation')` (Task 11, `(bool) env('MODULE_IMPERSONATION', true)`); `App\Authorization\EffectivePermissions::forUsers(list<int> $userIds, int $teamId): array<int, list<string>>` and `::holdsTemplate(list<int> $userIds, int $teamId): list<int>` (Task 4); `App\Authorization\UserAbilities` as built in Task 4 (`final readonly`, constructor `__construct(private EffectivePermissions $permissions)`, `covers()`, `forTarget()`, `forPage()`, private `manages()`); `App\Policies\UserPolicy` as built in Task 4 (`final readonly`, constructor `__construct(private UserAbilities $abilities)`); `App\Tenancy\Facades\Tenant::current(): ?Organisation`.
- Produces:
  - `App\Tenancy\Auth\Impersonation` (final, all methods static): `public const string SESSION_KEY = 'impersonation.impersonator_id'`; `enabled(): bool`; `isActive(): bool` (session state only, independent of the flag, RK-I3); `impersonatorId(): ?int`.
  - `App\Authorization\UserAbilities::mayImpersonate(User $actor, User $target): bool` (instance method, like the rest of the class) — the matrix without the session and module clauses.
  - `UserAbilities::forPage(User $actor, Collection<int, User> $users): array<int, array{view: bool, update: bool, updateStatus: bool, delete: bool, restore: bool, impersonate: bool}>` — the `impersonate` column equals `UserPolicy::impersonate` per row, from one batch of queries. `forTarget()` keeps its five keys and does not compute the column (so `view`/`update`/… policy checks cost no extra queries).
  - `UserPolicy::impersonate(User $actor, User $target): bool` — always checked: `Impersonation::enabled()`, `! Impersonation::isActive()` (depth 1), then `UserAbilities::mayImpersonate()`.
  - Test helper `useImpersonationModule(bool $enabled): void` in `tests/Pest.php` (config only in this task; Task 20 adds the route rebuild).

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

/** covers §4.7, §6.8, §7.2 */

use App\Authorization\Permission;
use App\Authorization\Role;
use App\Authorization\SetSuperAdmin;
use App\Authorization\UserAbilities;
use App\Models\Organisation;
use App\Models\User;
use App\Tenancy\Auth\Impersonation;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Gate;
use Illuminate\Support\Str;
use Spatie\Permission\Models\Role as RoleModel;

beforeEach(function (): void {
    useImpersonationModule(true);
});

/**
 * A user of $in promoted to super admin. DEC-26 (10): the promotion keeps organisation_id, so only the
 * "never a super admin" clause of the matrix keeps them out (IMP-4).
 */
$promoted = function (Organisation $in): User {
    $user = User::factory()->for($in)->create();
    app(SetSuperAdmin::class)->handle($user, true);

    return $user->refresh();
};

/** A user of $organisation holding the organisation_admin template role (DEC-21), not signed in. */
$organisationAdmin = function (Organisation $organisation): User {
    $user = User::factory()->for($organisation)->create();
    withPermissionsTeam($organisation->id, fn (): User => $user->assignRole(Role::OrganisationAdmin->value));
    $user->unsetRelation('roles');

    return $user;
};

/** A user of $organisation whose only role is a custom team role with exactly $permissions. */
$customRoleHolder = function (Organisation $organisation, Permission ...$permissions): User {
    $role = RoleModel::query()->create([
        'name' => 'role-'.Str::lower(Str::random(8)),
        'guard_name' => 'web',
        'team_id' => $organisation->id,
    ]);
    $role->givePermissionTo(array_map(fn (Permission $permission): string => $permission->value, $permissions));
    $user = User::factory()->for($organisation)->create();
    withPermissionsTeam($organisation->id, fn (): User => $user->assignRole($role));
    $user->unsetRelation('roles');

    return $user;
};

/** A user of $organisation with one direct permission in that team and no role. */
$directPermissionHolder = function (Organisation $organisation, Permission $permission): User {
    $user = User::factory()->for($organisation)->create();
    withPermissionsTeam($organisation->id, fn (): User => $user->givePermissionTo($permission->value));
    $user->unsetRelation('permissions');

    return $user;
};

it('decides who may impersonate whom on a tenant host (IMP-4, IMP-5, IMP-13, W3, W6, X6, RK-I6)', function (string $case, bool $allowed) use ($promoted, $organisationAdmin, $customRoleHolder, $directPermissionHolder): void {
    $organisation = Organisation::factory()->create();
    $other = Organisation::factory()->create();

        'super admin → promoted super admin of this organisation' => [$superAdmin(), $promoted($organisation)],
        'organisation admin → promoted super admin of this organisation' => [$organisationAdmin($organisation), $promoted($organisation)],
        'super admin → member of another organisation' => [$superAdmin(), $member($other)],
        'organisation admin → member' => [$organisationAdmin($organisation), $member($organisation)],
        'organisation admin → another organisation admin' => [$organisationAdmin($organisation), $organisationAdmin($organisation)],
        'organisation admin → member of another organisation' => [$organisationAdmin($organisation), $member($other)],

    $member = User::factory()->for($organisation)->create();
    $otherAdmin = $organisationAdmin($organisation);
    $disabled = User::factory()->for($organisation)->disabled()->create();
    $directHolder = $directPermissionHolder($organisation, Permission::UsersDelete);

    $promotedMember = $promoted($organisation);
    $superAdmin = User::factory()->superAdmin()->create();
    onTenant($organisation);

    // A collection of several models: any lazy-loaded relation would throw in strict mode.
    $users = User::query()->orderBy('id')->get();

    $page = app(UserAbilities::class)->forPage($helpdesk, $users);

    foreach ($users as $user) {

        ->and($page[$disabled->id]['impersonate'])->toBeFalse()
        ->and($page[$directHolder->id]['impersonate'])->toBeFalse()
        ->and($page[$helpdesk->id]['impersonate'])->toBeFalse()
        ->and($page[$promotedMember->id]['impersonate'])->toBeFalse();

    expect(app(UserAbilities::class)->forPage($superAdmin, $users)[$promotedMember->id]['impersonate'])->toBeFalse()
        ->and(app(UserAbilities::class)->forPage($superAdmin, $users)[$member->id]['impersonate'])->toBeTrue();
});

- [ ] **Step 3: The read-only part of `Impersonation`**

`app/Tenancy/Auth/Impersonation.php`:

```php
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace App\Tenancy\Auth;

use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Session;

/**
 * Impersonation (§4.7, §6.8): an in-house, session-level identity swap on the stock session guard
 * (DEC-28, OD-1). This part answers whether the module is on and whether this session is impersonating;
 * the swap itself arrives with the stop route (Task 20).
 */
final class Impersonation
{
    /** The impersonator's id; its presence in the session is what "impersonating" means. */
    public const string SESSION_KEY = 'impersonation.impersonator_id';

    /** The module flag (§6.8): config('skv.modules.impersonation'), from MODULE_IMPERSONATION. */
    public static function enabled(): bool
    {
        return (bool) config('skv.modules.impersonation', false);
    }

    /**
     * Whether this session is impersonating. Deliberately independent of the flag: a module that is turned
     * off mid-impersonation must still be able to end it (RK-I3), and the audit causer rewrite still applies.
     */
    public static function isActive(): bool
    {
        return Session::has(self::SESSION_KEY);
    }

    public static function impersonatorId(): ?int
    {
        return self::idFrom(Session::get(self::SESSION_KEY));
    }

    private static function idFrom(mixed $value): ?int
    {
        if (is_int($value)) {
            return $value;
        }

        return is_string($value) && ctype_digit($value) ? (int) $value : null;
    }
}
```

`Session::has()` only reads the store's attributes, so the check costs nothing in the console or a queue worker (no session is started there).

- [ ] **Step 4: The impersonation matrix in `UserAbilities`**

Replace `app/Authorization/UserAbilities.php` with the version below. The Task 4 body of `forPage()` moves unchanged into the private `managementRows()`; `forTarget()` reads `managementRows()` directly, and `forPage()` adds the `impersonate` column.

```php
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace App\Authorization;

use App\Models\Organisation;
use App\Models\User;
use App\Tenancy\Auth\Impersonation;
use App\Tenancy\Facades\Tenant;
use Illuminate\Support\Collection;

/**
 * The user-management decisions (§4.4, RL-26), held once: UserPolicy asks for one target, index
 * pages for a page of users with one batch load. Super admins manage everyone but never disable or
 * delete themselves (W2). Other actors need the permission, the same organisation, a target that is
 * not a super admin and, for every write, a target whose effective permissions in that team are a
 * subset of their own, so a helpdesk role with users.update cannot touch an organisation admin.
 * Equal sets pass: organisation admins still manage each other (W12 guards the last one).
 *
 * Impersonation (§4.7) follows the same principle with stricter targets: see mayImpersonate().
 */
final readonly class UserAbilities
{
    public function __construct(private EffectivePermissions $permissions) {}

    /**
     * @param  list<string>  $actorPermissions
     * @param  list<string>  $targetPermissions
     */
    public function covers(array $actorPermissions, array $targetPermissions): bool
    {
        return array_diff($targetPermissions, $actorPermissions) === [];
    }

    /** @return array{view: bool, update: bool, updateStatus: bool, delete: bool, restore: bool} */
    public function forTarget(User $actor, User $target): array
    {
        return $this->managementRows($actor, collect([$target]))[$target->id];
    }

    /**
     * Every control of an index row, with the impersonate column equal to UserPolicy::impersonate.
     *
     * @param  Collection<int, User>  $users
     * @return array<int, array{view: bool, update: bool, updateStatus: bool, delete: bool, restore: bool, impersonate: bool}>
     */
    public function forPage(User $actor, Collection $users): array
    {
        $impersonate = $this->impersonationColumn($actor, $users);
        $rows = [];

        foreach ($this->managementRows($actor, $users) as $userId => $row) {
            $rows[$userId] = [...$row, 'impersonate' => $impersonate[$userId] ?? false];
        }

        return $rows;
    }

    /**
     * The impersonation matrix (§4.7, IMP-4, IMP-5, C-4, X6) for one pair, without the module and depth
     * clauses that UserPolicy::impersonate adds. Only on a tenant host, and only for a target of that
     * organisation who is active, not deleted, not a super admin and not the actor. A super admin may then
     * impersonate anyone; everyone else needs users.impersonate in the organisation, a target without the
     * organisation_admin template (by role id, W6) and a target whose effective permissions — role and
     * direct ones, read with explicit queries (RK-I6) — they hold themselves.
     */
    public function mayImpersonate(User $actor, User $target): bool
    {
        $tenant = Tenant::current();

        if (! $tenant instanceof Organisation || ! $this->isImpersonationTarget($actor, $target, $tenant)) {
            return false;
        }

        if ($actor->isSuperAdmin()) {
            return true;
        }

        if ($actor->organisation_id !== $tenant->id) {
            return false;
        }

        $sets = $this->permissions->forUsers([$actor->id, $target->id], $tenant->id);

        return $this->memberMayImpersonate(
            $sets[$actor->id] ?? [],
            $sets[$target->id] ?? [],
            $this->permissions->holdsTemplate([$target->id], $tenant->id) !== [],
        );
    }

    /**
     * view, update, updateStatus, delete and restore for every given user (Task 4).
     *
     * @param  Collection<int, User>  $users
     * @return array<int, array{view: bool, update: bool, updateStatus: bool, delete: bool, restore: bool}>
     */
    private function managementRows(User $actor, Collection $users): array
    {
        if ($actor->isSuperAdmin()) {
            return $users->mapWithKeys(fn (User $user): array => [$user->id => [
                'view' => true,
                'update' => true,
                'updateStatus' => $actor->isNot($user),
                'delete' => $actor->isNot($user),
                'restore' => true,
            ]])->all();
        }

        $managed = $users->filter(fn (User $user): bool => $this->manages($actor, $user));
        $sets = $actor->organisation_id === null || $managed->isEmpty()
            ? []
            : $this->permissions->forUsers([$actor->id, ...array_values($managed->map(fn (User $user): int => $user->id)->all())], $actor->organisation_id);
        $actorPermissions = $sets[$actor->id] ?? [];

        $mayView = $actor->can(Permission::UsersView);
        $mayUpdate = $actor->can(Permission::UsersUpdate);
        $mayDelete = $actor->can(Permission::UsersDelete);

        $abilities = [];

        foreach ($users as $user) {
            $manages = $this->manages($actor, $user);
            $covered = $manages && $this->covers($actorPermissions, $sets[$user->id] ?? []);
            $isSelf = $actor->is($user);

            $abilities[$user->id] = [
                'view' => $mayView && $manages,
                'update' => $mayUpdate && $covered,
                'updateStatus' => $mayUpdate && $covered && ! $isSelf,
                'delete' => $mayDelete && $covered && ! $isSelf,
                'restore' => $mayDelete && $covered,
            ];
        }

        return $abilities;
    }

    /**
     * UserPolicy::impersonate for a page of users, from one batch of queries (RK-I6). Users missing from
     * the result may not be impersonated.
     *
     * @param  Collection<int, User>  $users
     * @return array<int, bool>
     */
    private function impersonationColumn(User $actor, Collection $users): array
    {
        $tenant = Tenant::current();

        if (! $tenant instanceof Organisation || ! Impersonation::enabled() || Impersonation::isActive()) {
            return [];
        }

        $candidates = $users->filter(fn (User $user): bool => $this->isImpersonationTarget($actor, $user, $tenant));

        if ($candidates->isEmpty()) {
            return [];
        }

        if ($actor->isSuperAdmin()) {
            return $candidates->mapWithKeys(fn (User $user): array => [$user->id => true])->all();
        }

        if ($actor->organisation_id !== $tenant->id) {
            return [];
        }

        $ids = array_values($candidates->map(fn (User $user): int => $user->id)->all());
        $sets = $this->permissions->forUsers([$actor->id, ...$ids], $tenant->id);
        $templateHolders = $this->permissions->holdsTemplate($ids, $tenant->id);

        return $candidates->mapWithKeys(fn (User $user): array => [$user->id => $this->memberMayImpersonate(
            $sets[$actor->id] ?? [],
            $sets[$user->id] ?? [],
            in_array($user->id, $templateHolders, true),
        )])->all();
    }

    /** A target of this host's organisation who could be impersonated by someone. */
    private function isImpersonationTarget(User $actor, User $target, Organisation $tenant): bool
    {
        return $target->organisation_id === $tenant->id
            && $target->isActive()
            && ! $target->trashed()
            && ! $target->isSuperAdmin()
            && $actor->isNot($target);
    }

    /**
     * The rule for actors who are not super admins: users.impersonate, a "non-admin" target (no template
     * role) and the permission-subset rule.
     *
     * @param  list<string>  $actorPermissions
     * @param  list<string>  $targetPermissions
     */
    private function memberMayImpersonate(array $actorPermissions, array $targetPermissions, bool $targetHoldsTemplate): bool
    {
        return in_array(Permission::UsersImpersonate->value, $actorPermissions, true)
            && ! $targetHoldsTemplate
            && $this->covers($actorPermissions, $targetPermissions);
    }

    /** Organisation members never act on super admins, even promoted ones that keep an organisation_id (§6.3). */
    private function manages(User $actor, User $target): bool
    {
        return ! $target->isSuperAdmin()
            && $actor->organisation_id !== null
            && $actor->organisation_id === $target->organisation_id;
    }
}
```

`users.impersonate` is read from the actor's effective permission set (the same explicit queries) instead of `$actor->can()`; for an actor of the tenant's organisation the two agree, and the page batch stays free of Spatie relations.

### Task 20: Impersonation session swap, actions and per-request enforcement

**Covers:** IMP-1, IMP-3 (runtime), IMP-5 (runtime), IMP-6, IMP-7 (route), IMP-8, IMP-9 (stop route), IMP-11 (routes off), IMP-15 (helper), AUD-1 (causer rewrite), FU3-6, W3 (runtime), R-2, RL-20, RL-21 (routes), RL-28 (impersonation session row); OR-B2, OR-I7 (second half), OR-M6, CV-19, RK-B4, RK-I1, RK-I2, RK-I3, RK-I9, RK-I12, RK-M6, RK-D7.

What this task delivers, in plain words (spec §4.1, §4.7, §6.4, §6.8):

- **The swap.** `Impersonation::enter()` stores the impersonator's id and an HMAC of their password hash in the session, puts the target's id under the `web` guard's own login key, migrates the session id and sets the target on the guard. It also rewrites `password_hash_web` (so `AuthenticateSession` accepts the next request) and forgets `auth.password_confirmed_at` (nobody inherits a password confirmation, RK-D7). `leave()` reverses it. `signOut()` clears the state and signs this browser out with `logoutCurrentDevice()` — never `logout()`, which would cycle the impersonated user's remember token and sign them out on their own devices (RK-I1).
- **Start** (`StartImpersonation`): a reason is required — trimmed, not blank, at most 500 characters (IMP-1, error on `reason`); then `Gate::forUser($actor)->authorize('impersonate', $target)` (Task 19's policy); then the swap; then `impersonation.start` is logged with the reason (logged **after** the swap, so the causer rewrite applies).
- **Stop** (`StopImpersonation`): logs `impersonation.stop` **before** leaving, with an explicit causer (the impersonator; when they no longer exist: no causer and `properties.impersonator_id`, RK-M6), `impersonated_as` = the target's id and, when the stop was not asked for, `ended_because`. Then it returns to the impersonator when they still qualify (exist, active, may use this host, unchanged password), otherwise it signs out.
- **Audit causer rewrite** (IMP-6, AUD-1): while a session impersonates, every entry whose causer is the impersonated user is caused by the impersonator and records `impersonated_as`. Independent of the module flag.
- **Per-request enforcement** (`EnforceImpersonation`, in the `web` group, prioritised before `Authenticate`): on every request of an impersonating session it re-checks, from the session and without resolving the guard's user, that the module is on, the impersonator still exists, is active, passes the host login rule and has the same password, the target still exists, is active, passes the host login rule and has the same password as at the swap, and the matrix still allows the pair. Otherwise it ends the impersonation through `StopImpersonation` with `ended_because` = `module_disabled`, `impersonator_unavailable`, `impersonator_credentials_changed`, `target_unavailable`, `target_credentials_changed` or `no_longer_allowed`, and redirects: back in your own account → `users.index` when you hold `users.view`, else `dashboard` (OR-M6); signed out → `login`. Running before `Authenticate` matters: a deleted target must never let the guard fall back to the impersonator's remember-me cookie behind the scenes (RK-I1). This replaces the membership middleware's old plan of an "impersonation branch": `VerifyTenantMembership` now applies `HostLoginRule` to everyone (FU3-6, it also refuses deleted users) and needs no special case.
- **The target's password.** `enter()` stores the target's password hash under `password_hash_web`. When the target changes their password elsewhere meanwhile (for example with "sign out other devices"), `AuthenticateSession` would see the mismatch on the next request, flush the session (the impersonation keys with it) and sign the browser out without a logged stop. `EnforceImpersonation` runs first and ends the impersonation itself (`ended_because` = `target_credentials_changed`), so every impersonation is logged at start and at stop.
- **The session row follows the real person** (RL-28). With the database session driver (the kit default), Laravel writes the guard's id — the impersonated user — into `sessions.user_id`. Disabling or deleting a user (Task 6) and archiving or purging an organisation (Task 15) end the affected users' sessions with `Sessions::endFor()`, a plain delete of the `sessions` rows whose `user_id` is one of those users (RL-28), so with the stock handler disabling the target would delete the impersonator's live session: the next request would start empty, no stop would be logged, and `Authenticate` would fall back to the impersonator's remember-me cookie (a silent sign-in, RK-I1). `ImpersonationAwareSessionHandler` (registered for the `database` driver) writes the impersonator's id instead. This handler alone protects the impersonator's session: the row carries the impersonator's id, so `endFor()` on the target does not delete it, and `EnforceImpersonation` ends the impersonation on the next request (the target is no longer active) with a logged stop. The remaining case: disabling or deleting the **impersonator** deletes their impersonation session too, so that stop is not logged; the same `endFor()` call clears their `remember_token`, so there is no silent sign-in either — the browser is simply signed out. (`phpunit.xml` uses the `array` driver, so the test for this switches to `database` itself.)
- **Stop route**: `DELETE /impersonation` (`impersonation.stop`, any host, `auth`) lives in `routes/impersonation.php`, which `routes/web.php` requires only while the module is on (spec §6.8 "not registered"); the controller also answers 404 when the flag is off at runtime (RK-I12). Tests flip routes with `useImpersonationModule()`, which now rebuilds the route collection (CV-19).
- **Handoffs**: no handoff can be issued while impersonating; consuming one while impersonating stops the impersonation first (logged, `ended_because` = `handoff`) and never takes the same-user shortcut (RK-I1).
- A real sign-in (`Login` event) clears any impersonation state.

In `tests/Pest.php`, add these imports to the existing `use` block:

use App\Actions\Users\StartImpersonation;
use Illuminate\Routing\RouteCollection;
use Illuminate\Routing\Router;

and `use function Pest\Laravel\post;` next to `use function Pest\Laravel\actingAs;`. Replace Task 19's `useImpersonationModule()` and add `startImpersonatingOverHttp()` after it:

```php
/**
 * Turns the impersonation module on or off for the rest of the test (§6.8, RL-21): the flag, and the
 * module's routes as routes/web.php registers them at boot for that value. The CI job sqlite-free boots
 * the suite with MODULE_IMPERSONATION=false, so every test that needs the module on calls this first.
 * RouteCollection has no remove API, so "off" swaps in a copy without the impersonation.* routes.
 */
function useImpersonationModule(bool $enabled): void
{
    config(['skv.modules.impersonation' => $enabled]);

    $router = app(Router::class);

    if ($enabled && ! $router->getRoutes()->hasNamedRoute('impersonation.stop')) {
        Route::middleware('web')->group(base_path('routes/impersonation.php'));
    }

    if (! $enabled) {
        $kept = new RouteCollection;

        foreach ($router->getRoutes()->getRoutes() as $route) {
            if (! str_starts_with((string) $route->getName(), 'impersonation.')) {
                $kept->add($route);
            }
        }

        $router->setRoutes($kept);
    }

    $router->getRoutes()->refreshNameLookups();
    $router->getRoutes()->refreshActionLookups();
}

/**
 * Signs $impersonator in through the login route on the current (tenant) host and starts impersonating
 * $target in a real web request, so the swap runs the whole web middleware stack (§4.7). The guard's
 * cached user is dropped before and after each request, as a new request in production would (RK-I9).
 */
function startImpersonatingOverHttp(User $impersonator, User $target, string $reason = 'Support ticket'): void
{
    Route::middleware(['web', 'auth'])->post('_start-impersonating', function () use ($target, $reason): string {
        $actor = Auth::user();

        if (! $actor instanceof User) {
            throw new LogicException('Nobody is signed in.');
        }

        app(StartImpersonation::class)->handle($actor, $target, $reason);

        return 'impersonating';
    });

    Auth::guard('web')->forgetUser();
    post(route('login.store'), ['email' => $impersonator->email, 'password' => 'password'])->assertRedirect();
    Auth::guard('web')->forgetUser();
    post('/_start-impersonating')->assertOk();
    Auth::guard('web')->forgetUser();
}
```

it('requires a reason that is not blank and at most 500 characters (IMP-1)', function () use ($organisationAdmin): void {

Replace `app/Tenancy/Auth/Impersonation.php` with:

```php
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace App\Tenancy\Auth;

use App\Models\User;
use Illuminate\Auth\SessionGuard;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Auth;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Cookie;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Session;
use LogicException;

/**
 * Impersonation (§4.7, §6.8): an in-house, session-level identity swap on the stock `web` session guard
 * (DEC-28, OD-1). The session keeps the impersonator's id and an HMAC of their password hash next to the
 * guard's own login key, which holds the impersonated user. Sessions are host-only, so an impersonation
 * never leaves the tenant host it started on. Start and stop go through StartImpersonation and
 * StopImpersonation; EnforceImpersonation re-checks the pair on every request.
 */
final class Impersonation
{
    /** The impersonator's id; its presence in the session is what "impersonating" means. */
    public const string SESSION_KEY = 'impersonation.impersonator_id';

    /** HMAC of the impersonator's password hash at start; a password change ends the impersonation (RK-B4). */
    public const string IMPERSONATOR_HASH_KEY = 'impersonation.impersonator_hash';

    /** The module flag (§6.8): config('skv.modules.impersonation'), from MODULE_IMPERSONATION. */
    public static function enabled(): bool
    {
        return (bool) config('skv.modules.impersonation', false);
    }

    /**
     * Whether this session is impersonating. Deliberately independent of the flag: a module that is turned
     * off mid-impersonation must still be able to end it (RK-I3), and the audit causer rewrite still applies.
     */
    public static function isActive(): bool
    {
        return Session::has(self::SESSION_KEY);
    }

    public static function impersonatorId(): ?int
    {
        return self::idFrom(Session::get(self::SESSION_KEY));
    }

    /** The impersonated user's id, read from the guard's login key without resolving the guard's user. */
    public static function targetId(): ?int
    {
        return self::idFrom(Session::get(self::guard()->getName()));
    }

    /** The impersonator across organisations (super admins have none); null once deleted. */
    public static function impersonator(): ?User
    {
        return self::findUser(self::impersonatorId());
    }

    /** The impersonated user, looked up like the guard would; null once deleted. */
    public static function target(): ?User
    {
        return self::findUser(self::targetId());
    }

    public static function impersonatorPasswordUnchanged(User $impersonator): bool
    {
        $stored = Session::get(self::IMPERSONATOR_HASH_KEY);

        return is_string($stored)
            && hash_equals($stored, self::guard()->hashPasswordForCookie($impersonator->getAuthPassword()));
    }

    /**
     * Whether the target's password is the one enter() stored for AuthenticateSession. A change elsewhere
     * (logoutOtherDevices) would otherwise make AuthenticateSession sign the browser out without a logged stop.
     */
    public static function targetPasswordUnchanged(User $target): bool
    {
        $guard = self::guard();

        return hash_equals((string) Session::get('password_hash_'.$guard->name), $guard->hashPasswordForCookie($target->getAuthPassword()));
    }

    /**
     * Continue as $target in this session. The impersonator must be the signed-in user; authorisation is
     * StartImpersonation's.
     */
    public static function enter(User $impersonator, User $target): void
    {
        if (self::isActive()) {
            throw new LogicException('An impersonation is already active in this session.');
        }

        $guard = self::guard();

        Session::put(self::SESSION_KEY, $impersonator->id);
        Session::put(self::IMPERSONATOR_HASH_KEY, $guard->hashPasswordForCookie($impersonator->getAuthPassword()));

        self::signInAs($target);
    }

    /** Back to the impersonator in this session. */
    public static function leave(): User
    {
        if (! self::isActive()) {
            throw new LogicException('No impersonation is active in this session.');
        }

        $impersonator = self::impersonator() ?? throw new LogicException('The impersonator no longer exists.');

        self::clear();
        self::signInAs($impersonator);

        return $impersonator;
    }

    /** Forget the impersonation keys; the guard's login key is left as it is. */
    public static function clear(): void
    {
        Session::forget([self::SESSION_KEY, self::IMPERSONATOR_HASH_KEY]);
    }

    /**
     * Sign this browser out. logoutCurrentDevice(), never logout(): logout() would cycle the impersonated
     * user's remember token and sign them out on their own devices (RK-I1).
     */
    public static function signOut(): void
    {
        $guard = self::guard();

        self::ignoreRememberCookie();
        self::clear();
        $guard->logoutCurrentDevice();
        Cookie::queue(Cookie::forget($guard->getRecallerName()));
        Session::invalidate();
        Session::regenerateToken();
    }

    /**
     * Takes the remember-me cookie out of the current request (the browser keeps it). The guard falls back
     * to that cookie as soon as the session's user cannot be loaded; while an impersonation is undone it must
     * never sign anyone in behind the scenes (RK-I1).
     */
    public static function ignoreRememberCookie(): void
    {
        $guard = self::guard();

        $guard->getRequest()->cookies->remove($guard->getRecallerName());
    }

    /**
     * The guard's own login key, a fresh session id, the password hash AuthenticateSession compares on the
     * next request, and no inherited password confirmation (RL-20, RK-D7).
     */
    private static function signInAs(User $user): void
    {
        $guard = self::guard();

        Session::put($guard->getName(), $user->getAuthIdentifier());
        Session::migrate(true);
        $guard->setUser($user);
        Session::put('password_hash_'.$guard->name, $guard->hashPasswordForCookie($user->getAuthPassword()));
        Session::forget('auth.password_confirmed_at');
    }

    private static function findUser(?int $id): ?User
    {
        if ($id === null) {
            return null;
        }

        $user = Auth::createUserProvider('users')?->retrieveById($id);

        return $user instanceof User ? $user : null;
    }

    private static function idFrom(mixed $value): ?int
    {
        if (is_int($value)) {
            return $value;
        }

        return is_string($value) && ctype_digit($value) ? (int) $value : null;
    }

    private static function guard(): SessionGuard
    {
        return Auth::guard('web');
    }
}
```

Larastan resolves `Auth::guard('web')` to `Illuminate\Auth\SessionGuard` from `config/auth.php`, so `guard()` needs no `instanceof` check (one would be reported as always true).

The database session row follows the real person. `app/Tenancy/Auth/ImpersonationAwareSessionHandler.php`:

```php
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace App\Tenancy\Auth;

use Illuminate\Session\DatabaseSessionHandler;

/**
 * The database session handler with one change (§4.7, RL-28): while a session impersonates, its sessions.user_id
 * is the impersonator, not the impersonated user the guard reports. The row follows the real person, so cutting
 * the target's sessions (disable, delete, archive) leaves the impersonation session for EnforceImpersonation to
 * end with a logged stop, instead of an empty session that falls back to the impersonator's remember-me cookie
 * (RK-I1). Disabling the impersonator still cuts this session; Sessions::endFor() clears their remember token with it.
 */
final class ImpersonationAwareSessionHandler extends DatabaseSessionHandler
{
    protected function userId(): mixed
    {
        return Impersonation::impersonatorId() ?? parent::userId();
    }
}
```

In `app/Providers/TenancyServiceProvider.php`, add the imports `use App\Tenancy\Auth\ImpersonationAwareSessionHandler;`, `use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Session;` and `use SessionHandlerInterface;`, and add at the end of `boot()` (after the `Livewire::addPersistentMiddleware(…)` line):
