Replace `resources/views/pages/activity/index/index.php` with:

```php
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

use App\Authorization\Permission;
use App\Enums\ActivityEvent;
use App\Models\Activity;
use App\Models\Invitation;
use App\Models\Organisation;
use App\Models\User;
use App\Tenancy\HostScope;
use App\Tenancy\UserNames;
use Illuminate\Contracts\Pagination\LengthAwarePaginator;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Builder;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Relations\Relation;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Gate;
use Livewire\Attributes\Computed;
use Livewire\Attributes\Locked;
use Livewire\Attributes\Title;
use Livewire\Attributes\Url;
use Livewire\Component;
use Livewire\WithPagination;
use Spatie\Permission\Models\Role as RoleModel;

new #[Title('Activity log')] class extends Component
{
    use WithPagination;

    /** @var list<string> The filters that send the list back to its first page (AUD-8). */
    private const array FILTERS = ['from', 'until', 'event', 'subject', 'causer', 'organisation'];

    #[Url]
    public string $from = '';

    #[Url]
    public string $until = '';

    #[Url]
    public string $event = '';

    #[Url]
    public string $subject = '';

    #[Url]
    public string $causer = '';

    /** Central hosts only; ignored on a tenant host (RK-I4). */
    #[Url]
    public string $organisation = '';

    #[Locked]
    public ?int $detailId = null;

    public bool $detailOpen = false;

    /**
     * Mount the component.
     */
    public function mount(): void
    {
        Gate::authorize(Permission::ActivityLogView);
    }

    /**
     * Back to the first page whenever a filter changes (AUD-8).
     */
    public function updated(string $property): void
    {
        if (in_array($property, self::FILTERS, true)) {
            $this->resetPage();
        }
    }

    /**
     * Open the detail flyout for an entry this viewer may read; any other id answers 404.
     */
    public function showDetail(int $activityId): void
    {
        $activity = HostScope::read(fn () => $this->baseQuery()->findOrFail($activityId));

        $this->detailId = (int) $activity->getKey();
        $this->detailOpen = true;
    }

    /**
     * Close the detail flyout.
     */
    public function closeDetail(): void
    {
        $this->detailOpen = false;
        $this->detailId = null;
    }

    /**
     * The filtered entries, 50 per page, newest first (AUD-3).
     *
     * @return LengthAwarePaginator<int, Activity>
     */
    #[Computed]
    public function activities(): LengthAwarePaginator
    {
        return HostScope::read(fn () => $this->filteredQuery()
            ->orderByDesc('created_at')
            ->orderByDesc('id')
            ->paginate(50));
    }

    /**
     * The page's entries as display rows.
     *
     * @return list<array<string, mixed>>
     */
    #[Computed]
    public function rows(): array
    {
        /** @var LengthAwarePaginator<int, Activity> $activities */
        $activities = $this->activities;
        /** @var array<int, string> $names */
        $names = $this->causerNames;
        $items = $activities->items();
        $organisations = $this->organisationNames($items);
        $rows = [];

        foreach ($items as $activity) {
            $rows[] = $this->row($activity, $names, $organisations);
        }

        return $rows;
    }

    /**
     * The entry in the detail flyout, read again through the host scope.
     *
     * @return array<string, mixed>|null
     */
    #[Computed]
    public function detail(): ?array
    {
        if ($this->detailId === null) {
            return null;
        }

        $activity = HostScope::read(fn () => $this->baseQuery()->find($this->detailId));

        if (! $activity instanceof Activity) {
            return null;
        }

        return $this->row($activity, UserNames::of($this->userIdsOf([$activity])), $this->organisationNames([$activity]));
    }

    /**
     * Names of the causers, impersonated users, impersonators and user subjects on this page,
     * across organisations and including deleted users. Only ids from rows read through the
     * host scope are looked up (RL-9, RK-M4).
     *
     * @return array<int, string>
     */
    #[Computed]
    public function causerNames(): array
    {
        /** @var LengthAwarePaginator<int, Activity> $activities */
        $activities = $this->activities;

        return UserNames::of($this->userIdsOf($activities->items()));
    }

    /**
     * Every action of the audit vocabulary with its label.
     *
     * @return array<string, string>
     */
    #[Computed]
    public function eventOptions(): array
    {
        $options = [];

        foreach (ActivityEvent::cases() as $event) {
            $options[$event->value] = $event->label();
        }

        return $options;
    }

    /**
     * The subject types that occur in this viewer's entries.
     *
     * @return array<string, string>
     */
    #[Computed]
    public function subjectOptions(): array
    {
        $types = HostScope::read(fn () => $this->baseQuery()
            ->whereNotNull('subject_type')
            ->distinct()
            ->orderBy('subject_type')
            ->pluck('subject_type')
            ->all());

        $options = [];

        foreach ($types as $type) {
            $options[(string) $type] = $this->subjectTypeLabel((string) $type);
        }

        return $options;
    }

    /**
     * The users who caused entries this viewer may read; a ?causer= outside this list is ignored (RK-M4).
     *
     * @return array<int, string>
     */
    #[Computed]
    public function causerOptions(): array
    {
        $ids = HostScope::read(fn () => $this->baseQuery()
            ->where('causer_type', new User()->getMorphClass())
            ->whereNotNull('causer_id')
            ->distinct()
            ->pluck('causer_id')
            ->map(fn (mixed $id): int => (int) $id)
            ->all());

        $names = UserNames::of(array_values($ids));
        asort($names);

        return $names;
    }

    /**
     * Every organisation, archived ones included, for the central filter; empty on a tenant host.
     *
     * @return array<int, string>
     */
    #[Computed]
    public function organisationOptions(): array
    {
        if (! $this->isCentral()) {
            return [];
        }

        $options = [];

        foreach (Organisation::withTrashed()->orderBy('name')->get(['id', 'name']) as $organisation) {
            $options[$organisation->id] = $organisation->name;
        }

        return $options;
    }

    /**
     * True for a super admin on a central host: every organisation's entries and the central ones.
     */
    #[Computed]
    public function isCentral(): bool
    {
        return HostScope::organisationId() === null;
    }

    /**
     * The viewer's entries without filters. Call inside HostScope::read().
     *
     * @return Builder<Activity>
     */
    private function baseQuery(): Builder
    {
        $query = Activity::query();

        if ($this->isCentral()) {
            // Central viewers also see archived organisations' rows, soft-deleted by the cascade (RL-7).
            $query->withTrashed();
        }

        return $query;
    }

    /**
     * The entries with every valid filter applied; invalid filter values are ignored (AUD-8).
     * Call inside HostScope::read().
     *
     * @return Builder<Activity>
     */
    private function filteredQuery(): Builder
    {
        $query = $this->baseQuery();
        $from = $this->day($this->from);
        $until = $this->day($this->until);

        if ($from !== null) {
            $query->where('created_at', '>=', $from);
        }

        if ($until !== null) {
            $query->where('created_at', '<', $until->add(new DateInterval('P1D')));
        }

        if (ActivityEvent::tryFrom($this->event) !== null) {
            $query->where('event', $this->event);
        }

        /** @var array<string, string> $subjects */
        $subjects = $this->subjectOptions;

        if (array_key_exists($this->subject, $subjects)) {
            $query->where('subject_type', $this->subject);
        }

        /** @var array<int, string> $causers */
        $causers = $this->causerOptions;
        $causerId = $this->digits($this->causer);

        if ($causerId !== null && array_key_exists($causerId, $causers)) {
            $query->where('causer_type', new User()->getMorphClass())->where('causer_id', $causerId);
        }

        $organisationId = $this->digits($this->organisation);

        if ($organisationId !== null && $this->isCentral()) {
            $query->where('organisation_id', $organisationId);
        }

        return $query;
    }

    /**
     * One entry as a display row.
     *
     * @param  array<int, string>  $names
     * @param  array<int, string>  $organisations
     * @return array{id: int, when: string, event: string, event_key: string, causer: string, subject: string, organisation: string|null, changes: list<array{attribute: string, old: string, new: string}>, details: string|null, ip_address: string|null, user_agent: string|null, properties: string}
     */
    private function row(Activity $activity, array $names, array $organisations): array
    {
        $changes = [];

        foreach ($activity->changeSummary() as $change) {
            $changes[] = [
                'attribute' => $change['attribute'],
                'old' => $this->displayValue($change['old']),
                'new' => $this->displayValue($change['new']),
            ];
        }

        $key = (string) ($activity->event ?? $activity->description);

        return [
            'id' => (int) $activity->getKey(),
            'when' => $activity->created_at?->format('Y-m-d H:i') ?? '',
            // An unknown key (older rows) renders raw.
            'event' => $activity->kitEvent()?->label() ?? $key,
            'event_key' => $key,
            'causer' => $this->causerLabel($activity, $names),
            'subject' => $this->subjectLabel($activity, $names),
            'organisation' => $this->isCentral() ? $this->organisationLabel($activity->organisation_id, $organisations) : null,
            'changes' => $changes,
            'details' => $this->details($activity),
            'ip_address' => $activity->ip_address,
            'user_agent' => $activity->user_agent,
            'properties' => json_encode(
                $activity->properties?->toArray() ?? [],
                JSON_PRETTY_PRINT | JSON_UNESCAPED_SLASHES | JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE | JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR,
            ),
        ];
    }

    /**
     * User ids the rows refer to: causers, user subjects, impersonated users and impersonators.
     *
     * @param  array<int, Activity>  $activities
     * @return list<int>
     */
    private function userIdsOf(array $activities): array
    {
        $ids = [];

        foreach ($activities as $activity) {
            $ids[] = $this->isUserType($activity->causer_type) ? $activity->causer_id : null;
            $ids[] = $this->isUserType($activity->subject_type) ? $activity->subject_id : null;
            $ids[] = $this->userId($activity->getProperty('impersonated_as'));
            $ids[] = $this->userId($activity->getProperty('impersonator_id'));
        }

        return array_values(array_unique(array_filter($ids, fn (?int $id): bool => $id !== null)));
    }

    /**
     * Names of the organisations of the given rows, archived ones included; central only.
     *
     * @param  array<int, Activity>  $activities
     * @return array<int, string>
     */
    private function organisationNames(array $activities): array
    {
        if (! $this->isCentral()) {
            return [];
        }

        $ids = array_values(array_unique(array_filter(array_map(
            fn (Activity $activity): ?int => $activity->organisation_id,
            $activities,
        ))));
        $names = [];

        foreach (Organisation::withTrashed()->whereKey($ids)->get(['id', 'name']) as $organisation) {
            $names[$organisation->id] = $organisation->name;
        }

        return $names;
    }

    /**
     * The causer's name, "as :name" while impersonating; the impersonator of a stop that was
     * logged without a causer; "System" for entries without one.
     *
     * @param  array<int, string>  $names
     */
    private function causerLabel(Activity $activity, array $names): string
    {
        $causerId = $this->isUserType($activity->causer_type) ? $activity->causer_id : null;
        $impersonatorId = $this->userId($activity->getProperty('impersonator_id'));

        $label = match (true) {
            $causerId !== null => $names[$causerId] ?? __('Deleted user'),
            $impersonatorId !== null => $names[$impersonatorId] ?? __('Deleted user'),
            default => __('System'),
        };

        $impersonatedId = $this->userId($activity->getProperty('impersonated_as'));

        if ($impersonatedId === null) {
            return $label;
        }

        return $label.' '.__('as :name', ['name' => $names[$impersonatedId] ?? __('Deleted user')]);
    }

    /**
     * The subject's type and id, with the user's name or a stored name where there is one.
     *
     * @param  array<int, string>  $names
     */
    private function subjectLabel(Activity $activity, array $names): string
    {
        if ($activity->subject_type === null) {
            return '—';
        }

        $label = $this->subjectTypeLabel($activity->subject_type).' #'.$activity->subject_id;
        $storedName = $activity->getProperty('name');
        $name = $this->isUserType($activity->subject_type)
            ? ($names[(int) $activity->subject_id] ?? null)
            : (is_string($storedName) ? $storedName : null);

        return $name === null ? $label : $label.' · '.$name;
    }

    private function subjectTypeLabel(string $type): string
    {
        $class = Relation::getMorphedModel($type) ?? $type;

        return match ($class) {
            User::class => __('User'),
            Organisation::class => __('Organisation'),
            Invitation::class => __('Invitation'),
            RoleModel::class => __('Role'),
            default => class_basename($class),
        };
    }

    /**
     * Central rows without an organisation are platform entries; a missing one was purged.
     *
     * @param  array<int, string>  $organisations
     */
    private function organisationLabel(?int $organisationId, array $organisations): string
    {
        if ($organisationId === null) {
            return __('Platform');
        }

        return $organisations[$organisationId] ?? __('Purged organisation');
    }

    /**
     * The reason column: the stated reason, or what a failed sign-in typed (RL-7).
     */
    private function details(Activity $activity): ?string
    {
        $reason = $activity->getProperty('reason');

        if (is_string($reason) && $reason !== '') {
            return $reason;
        }

        if ($activity->getProperty('invalid_address') === true) {
            return __('Not an email address');
        }

        $email = $activity->getProperty('email');

        return is_string($email) && $email !== '' ? $email : null;
    }

    private function displayValue(mixed $value): string
    {
        return match (true) {
            $value === null => '—',
            is_bool($value) => $value ? __('Yes') : __('No'),
            is_scalar($value) => (string) $value,
            is_array($value) && array_is_list($value) && array_filter($value, fn (mixed $item): bool => ! is_scalar($item)) === [] => implode(', ', array_map(fn (mixed $item): string => (string) $item, $value)),
            default => json_encode($value, JSON_UNESCAPED_SLASHES | JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE | JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR),
        };
    }

    private function isUserType(?string $type): bool
    {
        return $type !== null && (Relation::getMorphedModel($type) ?? $type) === User::class;
    }

    private function userId(mixed $value): ?int
    {
        return is_int($value) || (is_string($value) && ctype_digit($value)) ? (int) $value : null;
    }

    private function digits(string $value): ?int
    {
        return ctype_digit($value) ? (int) $value : null;
    }

    /**
     * A Y-m-d filter value as the start of that day in the app timezone; anything else is ignored.
     */
    private function day(string $value): ?DateTimeImmutable
    {
        $day = DateTimeImmutable::createFromFormat('!Y-m-d', $value, new DateTimeZone((string) config('app.timezone')));

        return $day !== false && $day->format('Y-m-d') === $value ? $day : null;
    }
};
```

The component file has no namespace, so `DateInterval`, `DateTimeImmutable` and `DateTimeZone` are used without `use` statements (a `use` of a single-segment name in the global namespace raises a PHP warning).

Append to `docs/decisions.md`, after DEC-27 (the file ends with DEC-27's **Consequence** line; leave one blank line between the entries):

```markdown
### DEC-28 — Administration build rulings (M4)

**Question:** Which choices made while building M4 refine the spec, what did the owner decide, and what is deferred?
**Answer:** Items (1)–(30) are the M4 plan's rulings RL-1…RL-30 (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-11-m4-administration.md`) as built, (31)–(33) the owner's rulings, (34)–(37) further build choices. (1) M4 adds one package, `spatie/laravel-activitylog` 5.1.1. Impersonation is kit code (31); `pestphp/pest-plugin-livewire` is not used (tests keep `Livewire::test()`) and the browser plugin stays in M5. (2) `config/skv.php` holds `invitations.expires_in_days` (`INVITATION_EXPIRES_IN_DAYS`, default 7), `invitations.signature_grace_days` (30) and `modules.impersonation` (`MODULE_IMPERSONATION`, default true); the passkeys and backups flags and `second_factor.*` arrive with their features. (3) Migrations are additive and numbered after M3's handoff table: `0001_01_01_000005_create_activity_log_table`, `0001_01_01_000006_add_locale_to_users_table`, `0001_01_01_000007_create_invitations_table`. The activity table is hand-written (the package does not load its migration) with explicit morph index names. Existing databases need only `php artisan migrate`. (4) `App\Models\Activity` extends the vendor model as a tenant model (`BelongsToOrganisation`, `SoftDeletes`, listed in `tenancy.tenant_models`, allowed without an organisation) with `organisation_id` guarded; the table adds `organisation_id` (indexed, no foreign key), `ip_address`, `user_agent`, `deleted_at` and indexes on `event`, `created_at` and `(organisation_id, created_at)`. `event` is a plain string without an enum cast, because the vendor logger assigns the raw event name before any hook runs; `Activity::kitEvent()` maps it to `App\Enums\ActivityEvent` (`tryFrom`) for labels, and an unknown value renders as its raw key. Every kit row stores the `ActivityEvent` value as `event` and `description` and its group (`authentication`, `security`, `users`, `invitations`, `organisations`, `roles`, `impersonation`) as `log_name`; diffs go in `attribute_changes`, everything else (reason, typed address, `impersonated_as`, host, counts) in `properties`; buffering is off. (5) Organisation tagging (`App\Actions\Audit\LogActivity`, the package's `log_activity` action): authentication, security and impersonation events take the bound tenant, else none (central), and ignore the subject, so a promoted super admin's sign-in is tagged by the host it happened on; every other event takes an explicit organisation, else the subject's organisation, else the bound tenant, else none. Role events always pass the organisation explicitly (a Spatie role carries `team_id`). An explicitly central entry while a tenant is bound is not supported; no M4 flow needs one. Central actions on an organisation's data appear in that organisation's log. (6) One writer: every kit entry goes through `App\Actions\Audit\RecordActivity`; the vendor `LogsActivity` trait, `activity()` and the vendor facade are used nowhere (`tests/Arch/AuditRulesTest.php`). `App\Observers\UserActivityObserver` records `user.updated` with old and new values when `name` or `email` changes, whoever saves; writers that log their own event save quietly (`AcceptInvitation`). Status, super-admin, role, deletion and restore changes are explicit events; role CRUD is logged in the role actions (no Spatie `Role` subclass); `permissions:sync` is not audited (deploy-time console; M6's doctor reports drift). (7) Central viewers see every row, archived organisations' (soft-deleted) rows and rows without an organisation included; tenant viewers see their organisation's rows only. Retention (`App\Actions\Audit\CleanActivityLog`, the package's `clean_log` action, `ACTIVITYLOG_RETENTION_DAYS`) force-deletes old rows, trashed ones included, inside `Tenant::bypass()`, for every organisation alike. A failed sign-in stores the typed value only when it is a valid email address (lower-cased, `properties.email`); otherwise `email` is null and `invalid_address` true, so a password typed into the email field is never kept; the password itself is never stored. Viewers of that host see the typed address. Causer names are shown across scopes, super admins included. (8) Any-host pages read tenant models only through `App\Tenancy\HostScope::read()`: scoped on a tenant host, `Tenant::bypass()` for a super admin on a central host, otherwise an `AuthorizationException`. Pages are not on the bypass allow-list (this replaces §6.2's "central Livewire components"). `HostScope` scopes tenant models only: reads of central tables (organisations, Spatie roles, permissions and pivots, `sessions`) filter by `HostScope::organisationId()` (the tenant on a tenant host, all organisations for a super admin centrally), and organisation ids sent by the client are ignored on tenant hosts. `HostScope::lockForWrite()` locks and re-reads an organisation inside the caller's transaction and refuses an archived one (validation error) or one that is not the bound tenant (authorisation error); actions that take an organisation call it before `Tenant::run()`. `users.edit` and `organisations.edit` take integer parameters and resolve per request; components hold `#[Locked]` ids, never Eloquent model properties, because Livewire rehydrates those without the tenant scope. (9) `App\Tenancy\UserNames::of()` resolves display names across organisations, deleted users included, for causers, inviters and impersonators, and is fed only ids from rows the caller already read through its own scope, never an id sent by the client. (10) The route × host matrix keeps the parameter pages through `matrixParameters()` and gained the outcomes `forbidden`, `organisations` (super admins on `/` centrally) and `not found` (`organisations.create` on a tenant host); the signed `invitations.accept` route is excluded and tested on its own hosts. (11) Interim UI until M5: one permission-gated "Administration" ("Beheer") group in the current sidebar, a `<x-flash-toast />` bridge that shows `session('status')` as a Flux toast (the profile page's duplicate status callout is gone) and a sticky `<x-impersonation-banner />` in the app layout. (12) The organisation wizard (`organisations.create`, central hosts only) creates the organisation, its pending first admin (the organisation_admin template, the chosen locale) and the invitation in one transaction; the mail is queued after commit and builds its link in the worker; no per-organisation role is ever created; the wizard writes exactly `organisation.created`, `user.roles_changed` and `invitation.sent`. (13) Invitations: roles attach to the pending user at invite time through `UpdateUserRoles`, so inviting needs `users.create` and `roles.assign` (`InvitationPolicy::create`, also checked when the invite page mounts) and only grants roles whose permissions the inviter holds; at least one role is required. The pending user's name is the address until the invitee chooses one. The token (64 random characters) is stored as `token_hash` (sha256, unique, used for lookup) and as an encrypted `token` (for mails and "Copy invite link") that is cleared on accept; it is never stored in plain text or on `users`, and never logged, nor is the accept link. "Copy invite link" needs the `viewLink` ability (the remind rights, `roles.assign` and the subset rule (26); super admins always), because the link is a bearer credential for the invitation's roles. Foreign keys: `invited_by` set null on delete, `organisation_id` restrict (purge deletes invitations first), `user_id` cascade. Cancel force-deletes the invitation and soft-deletes the pending user (§4.5); remind renews `expires_at`, keeps the token, sets `reminder_sent_at`, works on expired invitations and is refused for accepted ones; cancel is refused for accepted ones; accept locks the row. Mail links are built in the worker when the mail renders; links sent before a slug rename work again after a reminder. `remind`, `cancel` and `viewLink` are not always-checked abilities, so super admins pass through `Gate::before`. (14) One address rule, `App\Rules\AvailableEmail`, serves invite, admin edit, restore and the profile email change: deleted users never block; an address held by another organisation's user or by a super admin gets "This address can't be used."; inside the actor's own organisation the message names the conflict ("This address already has an open invitation." for a pending holder, whether or not an invitation row exists, otherwise "This address is already used in this organisation."). A unique-index race at save time becomes a validation error, also in `ConfirmEmailChange`. (15) The accept page shows, in this order: already accepted ("please log in"), expired (with a resend button for signed-in users who may remind), signed in as someone ("You are signed in as :name" with a sign-out button), the form. `accept()` refuses while anyone is signed in and re-checks inside the locked transaction that the pending user still exists and is still pending; Livewire updates skip the `signed` middleware, so every action re-resolves the locked invitation under the tenant scope. Unknown and cancelled tokens and foreign hosts answer 404 (friendly wording comes with M5's error pages); a tampered or expired signature answers 403. The page sends `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, renders in the invitee's locale, and signs the invitee in (session regenerated) onto the dashboard with a welcome toast. (16) Users: `users.edit` is gated by `users.view` and doubles as the show page, with editable sections per ability. Your own address is read-only there (change it through the profile's signed link) and `UpdateUser` refuses it, so DEC-27 (7) also holds for administrators; your own account shows no status or role controls. A pending user's address and status are read-only (only accepting activates; cancel and re-invite to change the address), and deleting a pending user is refused (cancel the invitation). Changing another user's address asks for a fresh password confirmation, applies directly, notifies the old address (`App\Notifications\EmailChangedByAdministrator`) after commit and forgets that user's pending self-service email-change link and the old address's reset tokens. `App\Actions\Users\RestoreUser` enforces restore (`users.delete`, same organisation, the subset rule; refused while the organisation is archived, while the address is taken and for a cancelled invitation's user); `restore` stays out of the always-checked list. The central users index lists every user, super admins included (organisation column "Platform"), filters by organisation and reads team roles with one pivot query; organisation admins never see super admins; the archived view leaves out pending users; row controls come from one batch evaluation of the policy's rules (`UserAbilities::forPage()`). `UserStatus::color()` gives each status its badge colour. (17) Organisations: `require_second_factor` is not shown until M7. Archive, restore and purge are actions with a transaction and an audit entry (the cascade stays in the observer); restore and purge lock the row and re-check `trashed()` inside the transaction. Restore is refused while a cascaded user's address is taken by another user (the message lists the addresses). Archive cuts the cascaded users' sessions and remember tokens (28). Purge detaches promoted super admins, trashed ones included (`organisation_id` becomes null; their ids are listed in `organisation.purged`), force-deletes invitations including trashed ones, deletes the users' `sessions` rows (no foreign key) and `password_reset_tokens`, force-deletes the users (passkeys and handoff tokens cascade), the team's roles and pivot rows, then the organisation, forgets the permission cache after commit and keeps the activity rows. Names and slugs of archived organisations stay taken; only super admins are told why, everyone else gets "This name can't be used." or "This address can't be used.". Demoting a promoted super admin while their organisation is archived is refused ("Restore the organisation before removing super admin."), so the password-reset and email-change paths never call `Hosts::homeOf()` for a member whose organisation is archived (members of an archived organisation are themselves archived by the cascade). `restore` and `forceDelete` stay super-admin only. (18) A fresh password confirmation (`App\Concerns\ConfirmsPasswords`, whose `passwordConfirmationRequired()` now takes a return URL built on the server) guards purge, the super-admin switch and changing another user's address; archive, deleting a user and starting an impersonation do not ask (reversible, or session-bound with a reason and an audit entry). (19) Roles: system-role names are refused after trimming, lower-casing and folding spaces and hyphens to `_` (`App\Authorization\Role::isReservedName()`), in the role actions and in `UpdateUserRoles`; names are compared in PHP, not with `LIKE` (where `_` is a wildcard). Deleting an assigned custom role is allowed: the confirmation shows the holder count, the holders lose the role and the count is logged. `App\Policies\RolePolicy` is registered with `Gate::policy()` for the Spatie role model (auto-discovery misses it) and, for non-super actors, requires the role's team to be the actor's organisation; system-role protection lives in the actions (`Gate::before` passes super admins through `update`) and in `RolePolicy::delete` (always checked). Only `roles.manage` (super-only) manages roles; organisation admins see them read-only. `UpdateRole` keeps held permissions that the editor hides (`users.impersonate` while the module is off), so a save never strips them. Permission input goes through `Permission::tryFrom()`; unknown and non-assignable values are a validation error, never a `ValueError`. Role actions lock the organisation (`HostScope::lockForWrite()`) and forget the permission cache after commit; role lookups by id are scoped to that organisation's team. (20) Impersonation starts from a `#[RequiresTenant]` (`App\Tenancy\Attributes\RequiresTenant`) Livewire action on `users.index` (this is §6.8's "start route") and stops through `DELETE /impersonation` (`impersonation.stop`, `routes/impersonation.php`), which is registered only while the module is on; the controller and the start and confirm actions also answer 404 when it is off. `UserPolicy::impersonate` holds the flag check and the matrix (a policy method wins over `Gate::define`, so none is defined): module on; not already impersonating (depth 1); a tenant host and a target of that tenant (super admins "Open" the organisation first); a target that is active, not deleted, not a super admin and not yourself; super admins may then impersonate anyone; others need `users.impersonate`, the same organisation, a target without the organisation_admin template (checked by id) and a target whose effective permissions, role and direct ones, are a subset of theirs. Targets with 2FA are allowed. `App\Tenancy\Auth\Impersonation` swaps the identity on the stock session guard: at start it stores the impersonator's id and an HMAC of their password hash, migrates the session, rewrites `password_hash_web` and forgets `auth.password_confirmed_at`, and it reverses that at stop. `App\Tenancy\Http\Middleware\EnforceImpersonation` runs in the web group before `Authenticate`, reads the pair from the session without resolving the guard, and re-checks on every request, Livewire updates included: module on; target resolvable, active and passing `HostLoginRule`; impersonator resolvable, active, passing `HostLoginRule` and with an unchanged password hash; the matrix still true. On a failure it logs `impersonation.stop` with `properties.ended_because` (`module_disabled`, `target_unavailable`, `no_longer_allowed`, `impersonator_unavailable`, `impersonator_credentials_changed`) and the impersonator as causer (no causer plus `properties.impersonator_id` when they no longer resolve), then returns to the impersonator when they still qualify and otherwise signs out with `logoutCurrentDevice()`, never `logout()`, which would cycle the target's remember token. A real sign-in clears impersonation state; signing out while impersonating stops it first (logged; `ended_because` = `logout`; a consumed handoff stops it with `handoff`), both through the `logout` route (`StopImpersonationBeforeLogout`) and through the Livewire `Logout` action; handoffs cannot be issued while impersonating, and consuming one stops it first and never takes the same-user shortcut (22). After a stop the impersonator lands on `users.index` when they hold `users.view`, otherwise on the dashboard. Settings actions while impersonating stay behind the target's password confirmation, which start forgets; there is no extra block. Start is logged after the swap (with the reason), stop before it; everything logged meanwhile has the impersonator as causer and `properties.impersonated_as` = the target's id. `Impersonation::isActive()` and the causer rewrite do not depend on the flag. (21) Module-flag tests: `phpunit.xml` pins `MODULE_IMPERSONATION=true` without `force`, so the `sqlite-free` CI job's `MODULE_IMPERSONATION=false` runs the whole suite on the off path, and every M4 gate from the module work on ran that suite locally too; tests that depend on the module call `useImpersonationModule(true|false)`, which sets the config and rebuilds the route collection (Laravel's `RouteCollection` has no remove API). (22) Handoff, refining DEC-27 (8): a link opened by the user who is already signed in is consumed and dispatches `HandoffConsumed` without a new sign-in (no remember-token cycling); a link opened while another user is signed in renders a confirmation page whose CSRF-protected POST (`auth.handoff.store`) consumes the token and replaces only this browser's session (`logoutCurrentDevice()`, invalidate); a GET never replaces another user's session. DEC-27 (8)'s "always start a clean session" therefore holds whenever a session is replaced. `IssueHandoff` turns `Hosts::homeOf()`'s `LogicException` into an `AuthorizationException`, and its callers (organisations "Open", the slug-rename redirect) pass only the authenticated actor. Consumption is tested on tenant hosts, the apex and the admin host. (23) `App\Rules\OrganisationSlug`: lower-case `[a-z0-9-]`, 3–63 characters, no leading or trailing hyphen, not in `tenancy.reserved_slugs` and not `config('tenancy.admin_subdomain')`; `Hosts::slugOf()` never resolves the configured admin subdomain as a tenant. (24) Rate limits on invite and remind, and the other limiter items, are M7 hardening; M4's senders are signed in, permission-gated and audited. (25) The per-component `user(): User` helper became `App\Concerns\ResolvesCurrentUser::currentUser()`, used by the settings and admin components. (26) Permission-subset rule: for non-super actors, `UserPolicy::{update,updateStatus,delete,restore,impersonate}` and `InvitationPolicy::viewLink` also require that the target's effective permissions in the target's team are a subset of the actor's. `App\Authorization\EffectivePermissions` reads them with explicit queries (roles assigned with that team id, the template included, plus direct permissions of that team; no Spatie relations, no cache), also for a whole page of users; `App\Authorization\UserAbilities` holds the decisions once, for the policy and for index pages. Equal sets pass, so organisation admins still manage each other (the last-admin guard still applies); a helpdesk role with `users.update` cannot touch an organisation admin. (27) `App\Authorization\LockoutGuard` locks every candidate row (all non-deleted super admins, or all non-deleted template holders of the team), the target included, in id order with `lockForUpdate()->pluck()`, and decides in PHP whether another active one remains; concurrent demotions serialise instead of deadlocking, so no deadlock retry was added (it could not work inside the nested transactions of `InviteUser` and `CreateOrganisation` anyway). `UpdateUserRoles` matches the template by id, rejects reserved names and other guards' roles and logs `user.roles_changed` only when the set changed. `SetSuperAdmin` decides on the locked row, always syncs the badge and logs only a real change; pages switch super admin through `App\Actions\Users\UpdateSuperAdmin`, which authorises first, while the console and seeders keep calling `SetSuperAdmin`. (28) Disabling or deleting a user and archiving an organisation (for its cascaded users) delete the users' `sessions` rows and cycle `remember_token` (set to null) in the same transaction, so a re-enable or restore revives no old session or remember cookie (with the database session driver, the kit default); purge ends the purged users' sessions the same way. One helper does it: `App\Tenancy\Auth\Sessions::endFor()`, a plain delete by `sessions.user_id` that decodes no payload. During an impersonation `ImpersonationAwareSessionHandler` writes the impersonator's id into `sessions.user_id`, so cutting the target's sessions leaves the impersonator's session, and `EnforceImpersonation` ends the impersonation on the next request with a logged stop. (29) The authentication subscriber (`App\Listeners\RecordAuthenticationActivity`) records sign-ins, failed sign-ins, sign-outs, password reset requests and completions, 2FA enabled (on confirmation) and disabled, regenerated recovery codes, registered and deleted passkeys and consumed handoffs, and also failed two-factor codes (`auth.two_factor_failed`) and used recovery codes (`auth.recovery_code_used`), all tagged by host; the security page logs `security.password_changed`. (30) Residuals accepted for v1: `AvailableEmail` still tells an administrator that an address is used somewhere (until M7's limits); a purged organisation's personal data stays in its activity rows until retention removes them (the spec keeps activity rows; anonymisation is a possible later option); invitation links sent before a slug rename point at the old host until a reminder is sent. (31) Owner ruling: impersonation is built in-house (`App\Tenancy\Auth\Impersonation` on the stock session guard) instead of with `lab404/laravel-impersonate`, whose auto-discovery replaces Laravel's `session` guard driver for the whole app, dropping `auth.timebox_duration` (DEC-27 (1)) and keying the password-hash cookie HMAC with a constant instead of `APP_KEY`, and whose `take()`/`leave()` do no authorisation or depth check. The per-request enforcement (20) would have been kit code with the package too. Consequences: no new dependency besides activitylog, full Larastan typing, no forced logout of existing sessions on install; the kit owns the swap code, pinned by HTTP tests; the spec §3 row is struck. (32) Owner ruling: M4 adds `App\Enums\Locale` (`nl`, `en`; `default()` from `app.locale`, Dutch as fallback) and `users.locale` (migration default from `Locale::default()` when the migration runs); the invite form and the wizard ask for the invitee's locale, and invitation mails and the accept page use it. M5 adds only the locale middleware, the language switchers and the profile field. This pulls DEC-26's M5 "per-user locale" forward for invitations and settles the conflict between §4.5 "invite by email with locale" and DEC-26. (33) Owner ruling: only super admins change an organisation's slug; organisation admins edit name and description and see the slug read-only. A rename made on the organisation's own host moves the editor to the new host through a handoff; a rename on the admin host stays there. The old slug is free immediately; there is no reservation or redirect of old slugs in v1. (34) Settled while planning, without the owner: cancelling an invitation soft-deletes the pending user (§4.5) and such users stay out of the archived users view and out of restore; the expired state wins over "signed in as" on the accept page; organisation admins see super admins' names in their activity log (§4.8 "cross-scope causer names"). (35) Copy: every `__()` key used in `app/Actions`, `app/Authorization`, `app/Enums`, `app/Http/Controllers`, `app/Mail`, `app/Notifications`, `app/Rules`, `app/Tenancy`, the users, invitations, organisations, roles and activity pages, the handoff confirmation page, the toast and banner components and `resources/views/mail` is in both `lang/nl.json` and `lang/en.json` (`tests/Feature/LangCoverageTest.php`); the starter screens follow in M5. `ActivityEvent` and `Locale` labels are Dutch keys; `#[Title]` values stay English literals until M5. (36) Tests: after-commit mail is tested on the real sync queue with the `array` mailer, because `MailFake::queue()` ignores `afterCommit`; session-swap tests sign in through `login.store` and forget the guard user between requests; M4 added the global test helpers `recordedActivity`, `pageSnapshot`, `callPageAction`, `inviteMember`, `acceptLinkFor`, `useImpersonationModule` and `startImpersonatingOverHttp` (`tests/Pest.php`) and `matrixParameters` (matrix test), and moved `dutchTranslationKeys` into `tests/Pest.php`. `phpunit.xml` pins `TENANCY_*` and `APP_URL` with `force="true"` and pins `PASSKEYS_RELYING_PARTY_ID` and `TRUSTED_PROXIES` to their empty test values. The bypass arch rule also catches `newModelQuery(` and an aliased `TenantScope` import, and raw `like` operators are banned in the app. (37) Invitation tokens are encrypted with `APP_KEY`: after a key rotation a reminder cannot rebuild an outstanding link, so those invitations need a cancel and a new invite.
**Evidence:** `tests/Feature/Audit/{ActivityLog,ActivityRetention,AuthenticationActivity,UserActivity,ActivityViewer}Test.php`, `tests/Feature/Users/{UpdateUserRoles,UpdateUser,UserLifecycle,UserModel,UsersIndex,UsersEdit,Locale}Test.php`, `tests/Feature/Authorization/{EffectivePermissions,UserPolicy,LockoutGuard,SetSuperAdmin}Test.php`, `tests/Feature/Invitations/{InviteUser,CancelInvitation,InvitationMail,InvitationPolicy,RemindInvitation,AcceptInvitation,InvitePage,PendingInvitations}Test.php`, `tests/Feature/Organisations/{OrganisationSlug,CreateOrganisation,UpdateOrganisation,ArchiveRestorePurge,OrganisationCascade,OrganisationsIndex,OrganisationWizard,OrganisationEdit}Test.php`, `tests/Feature/Roles/{RoleActions,RolePolicy,RolesIndex}Test.php`, `tests/Feature/Impersonation/{ImpersonationPolicy,Impersonation,ImpersonationEnforcement,ImpersonationUi,ImpersonationModule}Test.php`, `tests/Feature/Tenancy/{HostScope,UserNames,RequiresTenant,RouteHostMatrix,Membership,ResolveTenant}Test.php`, `tests/Feature/Auth/{Handoff,InviteOnly}Test.php`, `tests/Feature/Settings/{ProfileUpdate,EmailChange}Test.php`, `tests/Feature/Navigation/{AdministrationLinks,FlashToast}Test.php`, `tests/Feature/Tooling/CiWorkflowTest.php`, `tests/Feature/LangCoverageTest.php`, `tests/Arch/{AuditRules,TenancyRules}Test.php`, and the whole suite with `MODULE_IMPERSONATION=false`; vendor reads of spatie/laravel-activitylog 5.1.1 (`ActivityLogger::setEvent`, `LogActivityAction::beforeActivityLogged`, `CleanActivityLogAction::deleteOldActivities`, `CauserResolver`, the unloaded migration stub), lab404/laravel-impersonate 1.7.8 (service provider re-registering the `session` driver, `ImpersonateManager::take()`/`leave()`), Livewire 4.4.7 (`SupportAttributes::call()`, persistent middleware on updates, model-property rehydration through `newQueryWithoutScopes()`, `#[Url]` decoding), Laravel 13.35 (`SessionGuard::hashPasswordForCookie()`, `logout()` versus `logoutCurrentDevice()`, `MailFake::queue()` versus `SyncQueue` after-commit, `RouteCollection`), Fortify 1.41 (`Failed` carries the password, `TwoFactorAuthenticationFailed`, `RecoveryCodeReplaced`, `PasswordResetLinkSent` inside `defer()`) and spatie/laravel-permission 8.3 (`roles` relation filtered on the current team, `getAllPermissions()` lazy-loading).
**Consequence:** Deferred: M5 — the single navigation definition with its role × module render test and the Overzicht/Beheer/Systeem groups (replacing M4's interim group), `layouts/base` (the toast bridge and the impersonation banner move there), translated `#[Title]`s and Dutch copy for the starter screens, error pages including a friendly "this invitation is no longer valid" 404, the dashboard with the last-10 activity widget (on `UserNames`), the locale middleware, language switchers and profile language field, the Pest browser plugin with the browser tests for invitation acceptance and impersonation, the Flux Pro variants and Pro lint test, removing unused starter layouts and links, an arch rule that `organisation_id` is never fillable on tenant models (M4 tests its own two models), tenant 404s for JSON and Livewire requests, the passkeys module flag and `MODULE_PASSKEYS` in CI, and the M3 follow-ups for WebAuthn and Fortify routes (failed WebAuthn ceremonies no longer reported, the relying-party id lower-cased through `Hosts::apex()`, the redefined Fortify routes honouring `fortify.prefix`/`fortify.domain`, the recovery-code download from the stored codes, the awaited clipboard copy). M6 — doctor checks for the template role and badge drift, `SyncResult` reporting stripped badge permissions, `skv:create-organisation` reusing `CreateOrganisation`, a demo seeder with invitations and activity. M7 — the `require_second_factor` toggle, its enforcement and audit, `EnsureSecondFactor` letting impersonation sessions through (`Impersonation::isActive()` exists), the sessions list and its audit, bulk invitations, the audit CSV export, avatars including purge's avatar-file deletion, scheduling `activitylog:clean --force` and `model:prune` for handoff tokens, and hardening: rate limits on invite, remind and email-change requests, limiter input casting, clearing failure counters on a successful sign-in, request-independent origins for the password-reset and email-change mail links (built during the request) and other request-built links, the passkey bucket key and origin listener. M8 — the remaining test-strength gaps (soft-delete exclusion, idempotency, protections without a failing test), the debug-call arch rule and the strict-default test, and the `config/trustedproxy.php` docblock. Not in v1: reserving or redirecting an organisation's old slug (33). Residuals: (30).

Livewire pages are not on that list: any-host pages read tenant models through `App\Tenancy\HostScope::read()` (scoped on a tenant host; `Tenant::bypass()` inside `App\Tenancy` for super admins on central hosts) and filter central models with `HostScope::organisationId()` (DEC-28).

§6.4 Cross-host handoff (C-21, DEC-27 (8), RL-22):

Old:
```markdown
Super admins (and slug renames) move between hosts with a single-use signed token: `/auth/handoff/{token}` on the target host, valid 60 seconds, bound to the user and target host, consumed on use, audited. Session cookies stay host-only.
```
New:
```markdown
Super admins (and slug renames) move between hosts with a single-use token, stored as a sha256 hash in the central `handoff_tokens` table instead of a signed URL (DEC-27 (8)): `/auth/handoff/{token}` on the target host, valid 60 seconds, bound to the user and target host, consumed on use, audited. A link opened by the user who is already signed in continues without a new sign-in; a link opened while another user is signed in asks first, and only the confirming POST replaces this browser's session (DEC-28). Session cookies stay host-only.
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Changelog**

In `CHANGELOG.md`, under `## [Unreleased]` → `### Added`, append after the last bullet (`- Failed sign-ins take at least …`):

```markdown
- Organisation administration: a wizard that creates an organisation and invites its first admin, editing (only super admins change an organisation's address), archive, restore and purge, and "Open" to sign in on an organisation's own address.
- User administration: search, filters and pagination, an edit page that doubles as the user's profile, status changes, delete and restore. Administrators only manage users whose permissions they hold themselves; changing someone else's address asks for your password and notifies the old address.
- Invitations with roles and language: invite, remind, cancel, copy the invite link and a list of pending invitations. Invitees choose their own name and password on the organisation's address and are signed in right away. Links stay valid for `INVITATION_EXPIRES_IN_DAYS` (7 by default).
- Custom roles per organisation, managed by super admins; the organisation admin and super admin roles are protected.
- Optional impersonation (`MODULE_IMPERSONATION`): sign in as a member with a reason, a banner with a stop button, checked again on every request and fully audited.
- An audit log of sign-ins, security changes and every administrative change, with a filterable viewer and a retention clean-up after `ACTIVITYLOG_RETENTION_DAYS` (365 by default).
- A cross-host sign-in link opened while someone else is signed in asks before it switches accounts.
```

Under `### Fixed`, append after the last bullet (`- Real \`tests/Feature/ExampleTest.php\` …`):

```markdown
- Roles can only be changed through the roles form, never to the super admin badge, another organisation's role or a role with permissions the administrator lacks, and roles of another organisation cannot be edited (skv2 W1).
- Nobody can delete or disable themselves or the last active super admin (skv2 W2).
- Impersonating a pending or disabled user is refused, and an impersonation that is no longer allowed ends cleanly and is logged instead of signing the impersonator out (skv2 W3).
- The pending invitations list keeps working when the inviter was deleted or a user was set to pending by hand (skv2 W4).
- Accepted invitations can no longer be resent, and the accept page says "already accepted" instead of "expired" (skv2 W5).
- The organisation admin role cannot be renamed, deleted or reused as a role name, and organisation admins cannot impersonate each other (skv2 W6).
- A user created without an organisation never becomes a super admin (skv2 W8).
- Deleted users no longer block an address, and the invite and edit forms no longer reveal addresses used in other organisations (skv2 W9).
- Invitation mails are sent only after everything is saved, and a mail failure no longer leaves an orphan pending user (skv2 W10).
- A failed invitation no longer leaves the wrong permission team active (skv2 W11).
- Administrators cannot remove their own admin role, disable themselves or demote the last organisation admin (skv2 W12).
- Invitation tokens are stored once, hashed, with an encrypted copy for the invite link that is removed on acceptance (skv2 W13).
- Invitations need at least one role, and their link works only on the organisation's own address (skv2 W14).
- The admin subdomain is never treated as an organisation, also when `TENANCY_ADMIN_SUBDOMAIN` is changed.
```

Organisation roles change only through `App\Actions\Users\UpdateUserRoles`; custom roles only through `App\Actions\Roles\{CreateRole,UpdateRole,DeleteRole}`.

Replace the password-confirmation bullet (the last bullet of the section):

Old:
```markdown

```
New:
```markdown

Append to the end of the "Tenancy and authorization" section (after the password-confirmation bullet):

```markdown
- Any-host pages read tenant models only through `App\Tenancy\HostScope::read(fn () => …)`. `HostScope` scopes tenant models only: filter central tables (organisations, Spatie roles and permissions, `model_has_*`, `sessions`) with `HostScope::organisationId()` and ignore organisation ids sent by the client on a tenant host.
- Administrative actions (users, invitations, organisations, roles, impersonation start) take the acting user as their first argument and authorise themselves with `Gate::forUser($actor)`; session-level actions (`AcceptInvitation`, `StopImpersonation`) and the audit writer take no actor. An action that takes an `Organisation` calls `HostScope::lockForWrite($organisation)` inside its transaction before `Tenant::run()`.
- Livewire components authorise in `mount()` and again before calling an action, keep `#[Locked]` ids instead of Eloquent model properties, and re-resolve the model on every request. Actions that only make sense on a tenant host carry `#[App\Tenancy\Attributes\RequiresTenant]`.
- A non-super administrator acts on a user only when the user's effective permissions are a subset of their own: read them with `App\Authorization\EffectivePermissions` (never Spatie relations on a collection) and decide with `App\Authorization\UserAbilities`, also for index rows.
- A policy method named like an always-checked ability (`impersonate`, `delete`, `forceDelete`, `updateStatus`, `updateRoles`, `updateSuperAdmin`) grants super admins itself; other abilities rely on `Gate::before`.
- Audit entries are written only through `App\Actions\Audit\RecordActivity` with an `App\Enums\ActivityEvent` case; never `activity()`, the activitylog facade or the `LogsActivity` trait. Never log a password, a token or an accept URL.
- Invitations are created only through `App\Actions\Invitations\InviteUser`; their links come from `Invitation::acceptUrl()`, built when the queued mail renders. Mails implement `ShouldQueue` and call `afterCommit()`; test them on the sync queue with the `array` mailer, not `Mail::fake()`.
- Impersonation runs only through `App\Actions\Users\{StartImpersonation,StopImpersonation}`; check it with `App\Tenancy\Auth\Impersonation::isActive()`. Tests that depend on the module call `useImpersonationModule(true)` or `useImpersonationModule(false)` first, because CI also runs the suite with `MODULE_IMPERSONATION=false`.
- Every new `__()` key goes into both `lang/nl.json` and `lang/en.json` (`LangCoverageTest`); Dutch copy uses the informal "je".
```

`skv3-m3-carried-followups.md` — new `description`:

```text
Deferred minor findings from building skv3 M3 (authentication); M4 closed its items, the rest is assigned to M5, M7 and M8
```

New body:

```markdown
M3 was merged to main on 2026-10-10 (merge c416f61, 438 tests green on SQLite + PostgreSQL). DEC-27 in docs/decisions.md records the rulings; these minor review findings exist only here. M4 (DEC-28) closed its items:

- **Closed in M4:** handoff callers pass only the authenticated actor; a link opened by the same signed-in user continues, another signed-in user confirms with a POST first; handoffs are tested on the apex and the admin host; `IssueHandoff` turns `Hosts::homeOf()`'s LogicException into AuthorizationException, and demoting a promoted super admin of an archived organisation is refused, so the reset and email-change paths never meet it; `Hosts::slugOf()` excludes the admin subdomain; `VerifyTenantMembership` uses HostLoginRule; an admin email change forgets the pending self-service link; ConfirmEmailChange turns the unique-index race into a validation error; spec §4.4 no longer lists 'unverified'; invitation mail links are built in the worker; the bypass arch rule catches `newModelQuery` and an aliased TenantScope import; phpunit pins PASSKEYS_RELYING_PARTY_ID and TRUSTED_PROXIES.
- **M7 (hardening, with the limiter family):** no rate limit on email-change requests, updatePassword, invite or remind (mail bombing); limiter closures cast raw input before validation ((string) on email[] gives an "Array to string" error); a successful login does not clear the email+IP failure counter; password-reset and email-change mail links (built during the request) and other request-built links take scheme and port from the request (Host header / X-Forwarded-* with TRUSTED_PROXIES=*); the passkey bucket key comes from the client; the passkey origin listener trusts the request scheme and port.
- **M5:** failed WebAuthn ceremonies are still reported with a stack trace (log flood); stop reporting them. The RP id is not lower-cased and does not use Hosts::apex(). The redefined Fortify routes (forgot-password, reset-password, user/confirm-password) hard-code URIs and break if fortify.prefix or fortify.domain is set. The recovery-code download streams the page snapshot, not the stored codes. The copy handler does not await the clipboard promise.
- **M8 (release polish):** protections without a test that can fail: the 2FA and passkey limits counting only failures, a passkey refused for org A's member on org B's host, the 2FA host rule narrowed to isActive, the JobTenancy SyncJob leg, AuthenticateSession on Livewire updates, `CentralContext::enter` in the bypass rule. The global test-helper namespace grew (M3 added 11, M4 added 8); consider grouping. The config/trustedproxy.php docblock overstates which hosts Laravel auto-trusts (only Laravel Cloud and the *.on-forge.com / *.on-vapor.com domains).

**Why:** per-task and final reviews found these but rated them Minor; they were deliberately not fixed in M3.

- [ ] **Step 8: Manual smoke test per host**

The development database needs the three new migrations first. Ask the owner before running `php artisan migrate` (it is not pre-approved); never run `migrate:fresh` or `db:wipe`. The owner runs `composer dev` (Vite, queue worker, Pail, scheduler); Herd serves the site — never `artisan serve`. Get the apex URL with the Boost `get-absolute-url` tool (never `herd sites`); the admin host is `admin.` + apex and an organisation's host is `{slug}.` + apex. Mail goes to the log mailer, so invitation links appear in Pail and `storage/logs/laravel.log`. Sign in as the seeded super admin `test@example.com` (password `password`). The owner runs the list, or Claude runs it in the browser after the owner agrees; record each result as pass or fail.

Admin host (`admin.{apex}`), as the super admin:
1. `/` opens the organisations index; the sidebar shows the "Beheer" group (Users, Pending invitations, Organisations, Roles, Activity log).
2. "New organisation": typing the name "Smoke Test" suggests the slug `smoke-test` with an availability message and the `smoke-test.{apex}` preview; first admin `smoke-admin@example.com`, language English; saving returns to the index with a toast, and Pail shows an English invitation mail whose link points at `smoke-test.{apex}`.
3. Users index: the super admin's organisation column says "Platform"; filtering by "Smoke Test" shows the pending first admin, whose row links to the pending invitations list and has no delete control.
4. Pending invitations: inviter and relative expiry are shown; "Copy invite link" reveals the link; "Remind" shows a toast and Pail shows a second mail.
5. Roles: pick "Smoke Test", create "Helpdesk" with `users.view`; the system roles are listed as protected; `users.impersonate` is offered.
6. Activity log: `organisation.created`, `user.roles_changed`, `invitation.sent`, `invitation.reminder_sent`, `role.created` and `auth.login` are listed; changing a filter changes the URL; the detail flyout shows the properties.

Tenant host (`smoke-test.{apex}`):
7. In a private window, open the invitation link: the form is in English; choose a name and password; you land on the dashboard, signed in, with a welcome toast. Opening the link again shows "already accepted — please log in".
8. As that organisation admin: the "Beheer" group shows Users, Pending invitations, Organisations, Roles (read-only, no create button) and Activity log; invite `smoke-member@example.com` with "Helpdesk"; accept it in another private window.
9. Users → edit the member: rename them; set the status to disabled — the member's window is signed out on its next request; set it back to active.
10. Organisations → edit "Smoke Test": the slug is read-only; changing the description saves with a toast.
11. Users → "Inloggen als" on the member, with a reason: you land on the dashboard as the member with a sticky banner; "Terug naar je eigen account" (Back to your own account) brings you back to the users index with the "stopped" toast; the activity log shows `impersonation.start` with the reason and `impersonation.stop`, both caused by the organisation admin.
12. Open `/organisations/create` on this host: 404.

Apex (`{apex}`):
13. As a guest, `/` sends you to the login page. Signing in as the organisation admin on the apex is refused like a wrong password; signing in as the super admin works and `/` opens the organisations index.

Admin host again, as the super admin:
14. Organisations → "Open" on "Smoke Test" lands on `smoke-test.{apex}` signed in as the super admin; back on the admin host you are still signed in there.
15. Edit "Smoke Test" on the admin host and change the slug to `smoke-renamed`: you stay on the admin host. Then on `smoke-renamed.{apex}` (through "Open") change it back to `smoke-test`: you are moved to `smoke-test.{apex}` through a handoff and stay signed in.
16. Archive "Smoke Test": the organisation admin's window is signed out on its next request; the archived view lists it; restore it; archive it again; "Purge" asks for your password and the typed slug, then removes it. The activity log still lists the organisation's entries and `organisation.purged`.

Module off:
17. Ask the owner to set `MODULE_IMPERSONATION=false` in `.env` (Claude never reads or edits `.env`) and run `php artisan config:clear`. On a tenant host the "Inloggen als" action and the banner are gone and `DELETE /impersonation` answers 404; as the super admin, the role editor no longer offers `users.impersonate`, and saving "Helpdesk" keeps any `users.impersonate` it already held. Ask the owner to set it back to `true` and run `php artisan config:clear`.

Any failure becomes a finding: fix it as in Step 7 and re-run Steps 1–5.
